fix: Wired the outcome filter so it actually filters the trail.

title: Forget-device button lacked a confirmation
symptom: The forget-this-device shortcut (a trash/X button) executed with no confirmation, against the every-destructive-action-confirms rule.
root_cause: The button had no confirm dialog.
fix: Added a confirmation before forgetting the device.

title: Insights dashboard grid misrendered
symptom: The Insights dashboard's 4-column stat-tile row (plus donuts, bars, heatmap and comparison) didn't lay out correctly.
root_cause: An Insights grid class bug broke the layout.
fix: Fixed the grid class (v24) so the stat-tile row and charts render properly.

title: srcdoc iframe thumbnails render blank
symptom: Prompt thumbnails showed blank.
root_cause: `loading="lazy"` on srcdoc iframes plus a `height:200%` that never resolved against an aspect-ratio height.
fix: Removed lazy loading, set srcdoc as a property, and deferred one frame so thumbnails render.

title: i18n script not included in index.html
symptom: The i18n script wasn't loaded, so localization wouldn't run.
root_cause: The i18n script tag was never added to index.html (only security.js had a bumped version).
fix: Added the i18n script to index.html.

title: NUL bytes in worker.js source make grep/file treat it as binary
symptom: A plain grep silently matched nothing in a 1568-line source file, so an agent wrongly concluded the /api/log, /api/worklog and /worklog.mjs endpoints didn't exist and was about to recreate the client; `file` reported the source as data, not text.
root_cause: translateRoute's cache key used a literal NUL (0x00) as a delimiter (tgt + '\0' + s), embedding raw NUL bytes at lines 525/542 — which makes grep/file classify the whole file as binary and match nothing.
fix: Replaced the literal NULs with the \u0000 escape (byte-identical runtime string, cache unchanged) so the source stays plain UTF-8 text and grep/file work; use grep -a as a fallback. (Same trap hit BugLedger's own scan.mjs earlier.)

title: Worklog CLI prompt assumed ~/.breadcrumb/worklog.mjs was already installed
symptom: The agent couldn't find ~/.breadcrumb/worklog.mjs because the one-time install had never been run — the prompt assumed the CLI already existed, so the flow failed at the first step.
root_cause: No install step; the CLI wasn't served anywhere and the key depended on a shell-profile variable.
fix: Serve the CLI from a public /worklog.mjs route so it installs with a single curl (self-healing in the prompt), and read the key from a small key file (~/.breadcrumb/key) instead of a shell-profile dependency.

title: TOTP QR service leaked 2FA secret
symptom: Enabling 2FA sent the TOTP secret to a third-party QR service.
root_cause: The QR code was generated via an external service, exposing the secret.
fix: Removed the external QR call and replaced it with private manual key entry.

title: Excel month selector wrote to the wrong cell
symptom: Changing the month in the Social Tracker workbook did not affect the formulas' results.
root_cause: The month selector wrote to a cell the formulas never read.
fix: Pointed the selector at the cell the formulas read and re-verified 0 error cells.

title: note() call destroyed the month selector cell
symptom: A merged note silently wiped the month selector cell in the workbook.
root_cause: A note() call wrote a merged cell over the month selector.
fix: Reworked the merge so the note no longer overwrites the month cell.

title: Celebrate tab crashes on saved payment card
symptom: The Celebrate tab crashed for a fresh guest and whenever a payment card existed.
root_cause: S.cards was shared by both the card register and celebration gallery, so Celebrate read .copy.headline off a payment card.
fix: Moved celebration cards to their own S.celebCards key and made the gallery defensive against malformed entries.

title: Vault C1 brute-force / no per-account retrieval token
symptom: The encrypted vault was brute-forceable and lacked per-account isolation.
root_cause: No per-account retrieval token; a shared retrieval path was guessable.
fix: Added a per-account retrieval token with a dual-read migration (legacy accounts sign in with zero lockout), first mitigated by a rate limit.

title: Broken social link handling
symptom: Pasting a social URL produced a dead link, and bad image URLs showed a broken icon.
root_cause: Links without an https:// prefix and junk text were not normalized, and image errors were unhandled.
fix: Auto-prefix bare URLs to working links, reject junk text, and degrade broken images to a placeholder.

title: Invoice button silently added an investment
symptom: Clicking the Business invoice button silently created an investment instead.
root_cause: The invoice button shared a DOM element id with the Investments add-holding button.
fix: Gave the buttons unique ids and hardened the wiring; verified invoices and investments now act independently.

title: Merged-cell collision in pillars card
symptom: Merged cells in the pillars card collided, corrupting the layout/values.
root_cause: Overlapping merged-cell ranges in the pillars card.
fix: Resolved the merged-cell collision and re-verified.

title: toISOString() shifted calendar events a day early
symptom: Calendar events appeared one day earlier than the chosen date.
root_cause: toISOString() applied a UTC timezone shift to local dates.
fix: Avoided the UTC conversion so dates stay on the intended day.

title: Untranslated card titles and chart labels
symptom: Card titles and chart row labels stayed in English after switching language.
root_cause: Those strings were missed by the localization pass.
fix: Translated the remaining titles/labels and redeployed.

title: Calendar alignment assignment typo
symptom: The calendar rendered with broken alignment.
root_cause: A typo in the alignment assignment for the calendar.
fix: Corrected the alignment assignment in review.

title: Jumbled platform-mix card in summary band
symptom: The platform-mix card layout appeared jumbled in the planner summary band.
fix: Reworked the platform-mix card layout in the summary band.

title: recalc.py crashed on Python 3.9
symptom: The recalc verification script threw a TypeError.
root_cause: ignore_cleanup_errors is unsupported on Python 3.9.
fix: Replaced it with an AppleScript-driven Excel recalc harness.

title: arguments.callee ReferenceError breaks task ticking
symptom: To-do items wouldn't tick off; the first render's refresh callback threw silently.
root_cause: `arguments.callee` used inside an arrow function throws a ReferenceError in strict mode.
fix: Replaced it with a hoisted `refreshTasks` declaration.

title: Gradient theme crash from id mismatch
symptom: The gradient theme never applied because its checks never matched.
root_cause: Theme objects used `id:'grad'` but code checked `t.grad`.
fix: Changed all references to `t.id === 'grad'`.

title: Service worker cached a 404 for a later-added file
symptom: A vendor file added after first cache stayed permanently broken.
root_cause: The service worker had cached a 404 from before the file existed and kept serving it.
fix: Fixed the worker/caching path so all vendor files serve correctly.

title: Monochrome theme hue not updating
symptom: Changing the mono hue had no effect.
fix: Fixed the mono hue to update.

title: Schedule data-model change regression
symptom: After changing schedule data from string to an object, consumers still reading it as a string could break (calm mode, week view, search, celebrate cards).
root_cause: Schedule model changed from string to `{t,c,done,note}` but readers of `D.sched[h]` weren't updated.
fix: Updated the consumers to the new object model.

title: '0/0' task counter not updating live
symptom: The task counter stayed at 0/0 instead of reflecting progress.
root_cause: The counter wasn't refreshed after a toggle.
fix: Made the counter update live.

title: Both modal dialogs render on load
symptom: Two modal sheets both showed on first boot.
root_cause: A `display:grid` CSS rule overrode the `hidden` attribute.
fix: Corrected the CSS so hidden sheets stay hidden and the app boots to Today.

title: Duplicate calmBtn DOM id
symptom: Two elements shared the `calmBtn` id.
root_cause: The Today hero button reused an existing element id.
fix: Renamed the Today hero button to `calmStart`.

title: Kawaii theme buttons unreadable
symptom: Kawaii-theme buttons used white ink that failed contrast.
root_cause: Light ink on light buttons.
fix: Applied dark ink to kawaii buttons per the contrast research.

title: Meal grid misaligns below 860px
symptom: The meal grid broke below 860px, silently misaligning days against meals.
root_cause: Responsive grid layout failed under the 860px breakpoint.
fix: Fixed the grid so days and meals stay aligned at narrow widths.

title: PDF cover text overlapping
symptom: Cover words overlaid each other on the planner's first page/PDF cover.
root_cause: Insufficient vertical spacing in the cover layout.
fix: Fixed spacing between title, subtitle and year, and rebuilt all 12 PDFs.

title: Beauty-mark descriptor produced a lip piercing
symptom: Subject prompts rendered an unwanted lip piercing.
root_cause: The phrase 'beauty mark above the left lip' near the mouth was interpreted as a piercing.
fix: Changed subject descriptors to freckles/cheekbones/dimples, never a mark near the lips.

title: Ebook hyperlinks not rendered inline
symptom: PDF link annotations weren't appearing, undercutting the 'fully hyperlinked' claim.
root_cause: reportlab requires links to be drawn inline, which the generator wasn't doing.
fix: Drew the links inline so the ebook is fully hyperlinked (27,993 link annotations verified).

title: Mirror-reversed, garbled on-image timestamp
symptom: Generated mirror-selfie images produced a flipped, broken timestamp.
root_cause: Prompts let text render inside the mirror, so it came out reversed.
fix: Added a text-overlay clause telling the model to render on-image text as a flat, upright overlay, never inside the mirror.

title: Prompts produced generic, non-model subjects
symptom: Users got a generic subject instead of a model-grade one.
root_cause: Only 3 of 1,480 mega prompts demanded a beautiful/model-grade subject.
fix: Added a subject-lock/beauty-floor transform across all mega prompts.

title: Search returned zero results
symptom: Search returned 0 results despite the 'find anything you've ever written' claim.
root_cause: Notes, Books and Content were added without extending the search index.
fix: Extended the search index to include the new content types.

title: Text-fix clause injected inside the --oref placeholder
symptom: The orientation-fix clause landed inside the [your model … --oref …] placeholder, breaking it.
root_cause: The build transform treated --oref as a trailing parameter when inserting the clause.
fix: Placed the orientation-fix clause at the end so the placeholder stays intact.

title: Transparent card background over content
symptom: A card used a transparent background causing a visual glitch.
root_cause: The background was not opaque/theme-aware.
fix: Switched it to an opaque, theme-aware background.

title: Incorrect flat '696 pages' label
symptom: All files were labeled '696 pages' but the 2028 files are actually 697-701 pages.
root_cause: A hardcoded page count ignored leap-year and week-alignment variation.
fix: Corrected the per-year page-count labels.

title: Weak recovery keys and unescaped attribute sinks
symptom: Recovery keys were brute-forceable and some attributes were unescaped (XSS risk now that spaces are shared).
root_cause: Recovery keys used weak `Math.random()`; attribute sinks were unescaped.
fix: Strengthened recovery-key generation and escaped the attribute sinks, in Hello Baby and the same inherited code in Happy Travel.

title: Entities deleted without confirmation
symptom: Five places deleted data without asking.
root_cause: Missing delete-confirmation guards.
fix: Added delete confirmations to all five places plus broader edit-everything support.

title: Arrival without due date routed to wrong screen
symptom: A baby with no due date fell into the wrong screen.
root_cause: Ordering logic mishandled a missing due date.
fix: Route arrival-without-due-date straight to the correct age-based screen (e.g. '3RD BIRTHDAY').

title: App showed Happy Travel nav instead of baby app
symptom: The brand said Hello Baby but the nav showed Happy Travel's 'My Trips / Journey / Passport'.
root_cause: Leftover Happy Travel app code from the fork.
fix: Restored the correct baby nav (Home / Events / Babymoon & Trips / Milestones).

title: Blurry, hard-to-read wording
symptom: Text looked fuzzy and dark numbers collided with the dark silhouette.
root_cause: A soft glow added for legibility made text fuzzy, and dark-on-dark clashed.
fix: Removed the glow and fixed the number/silhouette contrast.

title: Budget edits buried and unfindable
symptom: The user couldn't find budget edits because they were buried at the bottom of the Events tab.
root_cause: Budget was nested inside Events instead of surfaced.
fix: Promoted Budget to its own standalone tab and added a hamburger menu.

title: Literal \n rendering escaped
symptom: A literal `\n` was showing instead of a line break.
root_cause: Incorrect newline escaping.
fix: Corrected the escaping.

title: openpyxl StyleProxy crash on font copy
symptom: xlsx generation failed when copying fonts.
root_cause: Assigning `.font = ws[cell].font` uses an unhashable StyleProxy.
fix: Apply named fonts conditionally instead of copying the StyleProxy.

title: Analysis donut rendered incorrectly
symptom: The analysis donut chart displayed wrong.
fix: Fixed the donut rendering.

title: Duplicated block in wedding-party view
symptom: The wedding party showed a duplicated half-block.
root_cause: Duplicated code lines in wed.js (caught by node --check).
fix: Removed the duplicate lines and converted the cramped table to readable cards + editor.

title: Filler images not loading (naturalWidth 0)
symptom: Filler/Unsplash images failed to load (naturalWidth 0).
root_cause: Image URL handling prevented the images from loading.
fix: Store the image URL directly and let the `` element load it.

title: Seating flow dead-ends after adding a table
symptom: Adding a table left an empty table with no way forward.
root_cause: There was no way to seat guests into a newly added table.
fix: Added capacity meters, per-table '+ Seat a guest here' dropdowns, meal tallies, auto-seat and a 'still to seat' pool.

title: Nested git repo leaked into monorepo commit
symptom: A wedding-planner gitlink was committed into the BUDGETLEVELUP monorepo.
root_cause: wedding-planner has its own repo and was added as a gitlink.
fix: Removed the leaked gitlink from the monorepo commit.

title: Service worker pins returning users to old build
symptom: Returning visitors saw stale builds — old splash rings, white space under content, and a mis-sized rainbow ring.
root_cause: The root `/` navigation was served cache-first, pinning users to a stale index.html.
fix: Made navigations network-first and bumped the cache version to purge stale caches; the identical bug was also fixed in Planner Studio.

title: Join boot race gives joiners the wrong cloud key
symptom: Users joining a shared space were given their own cloud key and shown the wrong 'your key' popup.
root_cause: Two boot-time races in the share/join flow.
fix: Fixed the boot races so joiners use the correct shared key and popup.

title: Choose-a-photo box shows literal ${imgIconSVG(34)}
symptom: The photo-picker box displayed the literal text `${imgIconSVG(34)}` (plus a fallback clock glyph) instead of an image icon.
root_cause: `imgIconSVG(34)` was inside a single-quoted string (wed-data.js:15), so it wasn't evaluated.
fix: Broke out of the single-quoted string to call imgIconSVG so a real image icon renders.

title: tvPhoto icon printed as literal text
symptom: `${IMG_ICON(32)}` showed as literal text in tvPhoto instead of the icon.
root_cause: The placeholder sat inside a single-quoted string, so it wasn't interpolated.
fix: Built the string with concatenation so IMG_ICON is actually called.

title: Corrupted emoji entry
symptom: One corrupted emoji entry had slipped into the data.
root_cause: Malformed emoji entry.
fix: Corrected the emoji entry.

title: SSRF via /api/open and /api/fetch
symptom: Server-side fetch endpoints could be pointed at arbitrary internal hosts.
root_cause: The browser-open/fetch paths had no host allowlist.
fix: Added a host allowlist to /api/open and /api/fetch in worker.js.

title: XSS in Listing Lab render path
symptom: Untrusted content could execute script in Listing Lab.
root_cause: Unsanitized input rendered into the page.
fix: Applied output sanitization to close the XSS vector.

title: AI misattributed quotes between listings
symptom: The analyzer attributed one listing's quote to a different listing.
root_cause: The prompt allowed cross-listing bleed when run on many listings.
fix: Tightened the prompt and re-ran 10 listings to confirm correct attribution.

title: Digit confusion when reading listing images
symptom: Digits were misread from images.
root_cause: No image preprocessing before digit recognition.
fix: Added proper image preprocessing and generalized the digit-confusion fix.

title: Scraper pulled related-item ads and foreign shops
symptom: Analyses were polluted by related-item ads and other shops' listings, which would have produced wrong results.
root_cause: The scraper didn't filter related-item ads or restrict to the listing's own shop.
fix: Filter out related-item ads and keep only the dominant shop, detected via the shop ID embedded in image URLs.

title: XSS via paste into contenteditable notes editor
symptom: Pasting HTML into the notes editor could inject script.
root_cause: Contenteditable paste was unsanitized (same class as Trix CVE-2024-53847).
fix: Sanitized pasted content in the notes editor and applied the same fix to the budget app's notes editor.

title: cur0 is not defined crash on post save
symptom: Saving a post with income entered crashed the app.
root_cause: An undeclared identifier (cur0) was referenced during post-save.
fix: Guarded with a typeof money0 check so income posts save cleanly.

title: Older profiles crash on missing state fields
symptom: Profiles created before new features crashed on load.
root_cause: normalize() did not backfill newly added state fields.
fix: Backfilled the new state fields in normalize() so old profiles load.

title: To-do done button crash
symptom: Clicking a to-do's done button threw undefined.split.
root_cause: The attribute was written as data-tododone but read as dataset.todoDone (case mismatch).
fix: Aligned the dataset key naming so the done button reads correctly.

title: Report page dies on a transient fetch failure ('Couldn't load — Failed to fetch')
symptom: Opening a sweep report during a network blip or mid-deploy showed 'Couldn't load — TypeError: Failed to fetch' and never recovered.
root_cause: The report did Promise.all of three fetches; /api/checks had no .catch, so any one rejecting failed the whole load, with no retry.
fix: Wrapped each fetch in a retrying getJSON() (2 retries + backoff) that returns a fallback instead of rejecting; on empty data show a friendly 'connection dropped' + a Retry link instead of a raw error.

title: Activity timeline re-renders every poll, replaying entrance animations (flicker)
symptom: The /timeline feed rebuilt its whole innerHTML on every 4s poll even when nothing changed, so every card replayed its 'rise' entrance animation and the page visibly flickered.
root_cause: render() unconditionally set feed.innerHTML each poll; recreated DOM nodes re-run their CSS entrance animation. (Same class as the earlier /live blink, but the timeline was missed.)
fix: Compute a content signature from stable fields (event ids/status/coverage/progress) and skip the re-render when it's unchanged; only rebuild when content actually changes.

title: Automated git commit used `git add -A`, sweeping a co-editing session's work
symptom: The hourly harvester's auto-commit ran mid-work and its `git add -A` staged an in-progress session's unrelated edits, committing them under the wrong message.
root_cause: harvest.mjs/scan.mjs staged everything (`git add -A`) instead of only their own generated files.
fix: Stage an explicit allow-list of the tool's own outputs (harvested.json / scan-findings.json + their gen artefacts), never `git add -A`. (This is the 'stage only files you touched' optimiser.)

title: Bulk rename introduced a grammar slip ('a account')
symptom: A bulk find-replace of 'studio' → 'account' produced 'a account' where the article should agree ('an account').
root_cause: Blind string replace doesn't fix the preceding article; 'a/an' depends on the following word's sound.
fix: Corrected 'a account' → 'an account' and verified the copy renders live; left the internal importStudio() function name (never user-visible) untouched. Lesson: after a bulk rename, grep for 'a <newword>' article mismatches.

title: Unlock keypad numbers float high and misalign
symptom: On the unlock PIN pad the numbers sat too high inside their circles and 1/0 didn't line up with the lettered keys — it still looked off after a first tidy pass.
root_cause: Each key reserved a letter row (ABC/DEF/…), which pushed the number upward instead of centering it; the digit wasn't positioned independently of the letters.
fix: Centered each number dead-centre in the key and absolute-positioned the letters tucked at the bottom; added a hairline border + subtle fill, tighter spacing and a smoother press state; also relabeled 'Create a studio' → 'Create account' on the unlock screen.

title: Orphaned dead whitespace in FAQ + Policies section
symptom: The FAQ and Policies cards sat only in the right column while the left column ended at the testimonials card, leaving a dead bottom-left quadrant.
root_cause: The section used a 5fr/7fr split where the short left column (About + Testimonials) ended early while the long right column (Gallery + FAQ + Policies) ran on, orphaning the bottom-left quadrant.
fix: Restructured the section into a balanced editorial layout — a full-width gallery strip then a 2x2 equal-height card grid (About / Testimonials / FAQ / Policies) so rows align and nothing is orphaned.

title: Screenshot box completely unstyled
symptom: A box looked cheap because it had no styling at all.
root_cause: The element rendered completely unstyled.
fix: Applied proper styling to the box.

title: Break-even card said 'covers 100%' when revenue was 152% of costs
symptom: Finance dashboard displayed 'covers 100%' even though MRR was 152% of monthly costs
root_cause: Coverage copy capped/miscomputed the revenue-to-cost ratio instead of reporting the real percentage
fix: Compute and show the true coverage ratio (e.g. 152%) rather than a hardcoded/clamped 100%

title: Negative currency rendered as $-59.17 instead of minus-$59.17
symptom: Negative money values showed the minus sign after the dollar sign
root_cause: Money formatter prefixed the symbol then let the numeric minus fall inside
fix: Format negatives with the minus before the currency symbol in the shared money formatter

title: One malformed report blanked the entire Reports list
symptom: The whole Reports view rendered blank when a single report had a string (not array) tasks field
root_cause: reportCard assumed well-formed data; one bad row threw and aborted rendering of the entire list
fix: Make reportCard defensive so a malformed report degrades gracefully and never breaks the list

title: Activity timeline dumped the entire status_note field
symptom: status_note edits printed the whole note into the activity timeline, cluttering it
root_cause: Timeline rendered raw field values with no length cap
fix: Truncate long field values in the activity event builder so entries stay tidy

title: Upsert ON CONFLICT omitted meta, dropping an edited prompt's asks ledger on sync
symptom: Editing a prompt lost its asks/convo/estimated data after cloud sync
root_cause: The docs/prompts ON CONFLICT update clause did not include the meta column, so edits to meta never persisted on re-sync
fix: Add meta to the ON CONFLICT update set (and fix the size cap) so edited prompt metadata round-trips

title: Landing-demo 'Sam' data bled into newly created accounts
symptom: Exploring the landing-page demo, then signing up, produced an account pre-filled with demo projects/prompts and greeted the user as 'Sam'
root_cause: Signup adopted the in-memory demo state via cloudPush instead of resetting to a blank trail first
fix: Reset state to blank on signup before adopting the account; added a cloudPull auto-heal that resets accounts matching the demo fingerprint

title: Plans feature row wrapped its text below the tick
symptom: The long 'Automatic capture' feature line wrapped underneath its checkmark instead of beside it
root_cause: .row used flex-wrap:wrap, letting the label drop to a new line
fix: Prevent the row from wrapping so the label stays inline with its tick

title: No brute-force lockout on 5-digit passcode sign-in/recovery
symptom: A 5-digit passcode could be guessed with unlimited attempts on sign-in and forgot-passcode
root_cause: Auth had no attempt throttling; PBKDF2 is capped at 100k iterations on Workers so an unlimited-guess passcode was the real hole
fix: Added an attempts table with gateCheck/gateFail/gateClear keyed separately by email and device IP, wired into sign-in and recovery; escalating lockouts 5->5min, 8->30min, 12->6h; cleared on success. Verified live: 6th miss returns HTTP 429

title: Opening a picker modal from inside a form wiped the parent form
symptom: Opening the currency picker from inside New-lead / Settings / Invoice destroyed the parent modal and every value already typed into it
root_cause: The app uses a single-overlay model — openModal() calls closeOverlays() first — so drawing the picker tore down the form underneath it
fix: Rewrote openCurPick as its own stacked overlay (z-index above the parent modal) that closes only itself, leaving the form intact

title: Notification panel could not be closed with its X
symptom: Clicking X on the notifications panel set hidden=true but the panel stayed on screen
root_cause: Author rule .notif-panel{display:flex} beats the browser's built-in [hidden]{display:none}, so the hidden attribute never took effect
fix: Added .notif-panel[hidden]{display:none}

title: Sidebar collapse toggle sheared off by the sticky sidebar's overflow
symptom: The circular collapse chevron rendered clipped/half-cut at the sidebar's right edge
root_cause: The sticky sidebar was given overflow-y:auto, which also clips the x-axis, cutting off the absolutely-positioned toggle that pokes past the right edge (right:-11px)
fix: Made the toggle position:fixed (like the drag grip) so the sidebar's overflow can't clip it

title: e-business-card preview collapsed to a 2px sliver
symptom: The e-card live preview rendered as a 2px strip with its contents out of flow
root_cause: .ecard has overflow:hidden and, as a flex item in the modal's flex column, that zeroes its auto min-height so it collapses
fix: Set the card to flex:none so it keeps its intrinsic height

title: Sidebar stopped scrolling partway down long pages
symptom: On pages taller than one screen the left sidebar cut off (couldn't reach items below 'Calls')
root_cause: Two .side rules existed; a later .side{position:relative} (left over from the old absolute grip) overrode the base position:sticky, so the sidebar was only 100dvh tall and scrolled away
fix: Removed the stray position:relative, restoring sticky full-height

title: AI outage: hardcoded Gemini model retired by the provider
symptom: All AI features returned errors; /api/ai gave 'gemini-2.0-flash is no longer available' (404)
root_cause: The default model and the GEMINI_MODEL secret were pinned to gemini-2.0-flash, which Google deprecated (and the key's Cloud project separately returned 403 PERMISSION_DENIED)
fix: Changed the default to the gemini-flash-latest alias and added a Claude/Anthropic fallback so AI recovers when one provider errors

title: Business tier badge rendered washed-out and see-through
symptom: The BUSINESS badge next to the name showed as a pale, blurry, semi-transparent blob with unreadable white text
root_cause: .tb-biz combined backdrop-filter:blur(4px) with a pale translucent gradient, frosting whatever was behind it and killing text contrast
fix: Removed the backdrop-filter and deepened the gradient to saturated colours with solid white text

title: Cross-account data leak: shared localStorage cache not cleared on sign-out
symptom: On a shared device, the next person to sign in loaded the previous user's leads and invoices from cache
root_cause: State is cached under a single global key 'hallalu_v2' (not owner-scoped), and signOut() called save() — re-writing the departing user's data back into that key and never clearing it
fix: Added wipeLocal() and call it on sign-out and on the ephemeral 'don't keep me signed in' boot path; verified the cached account data is cleared

title: Stored XSS in the public proposal-accept page title
symptom: A proposal titled with </title><script>… executed when a client opened the public /accept link
root_cause: The public unauthenticated accept page interpolated d.title / d.from raw into the <title> even though the body escaped them
fix: Escaped the title/from values consistently with the body; also added nosniff / X-Frame-Options / Referrer-Policy to the public HTML responses

title: javascript:/data: URL scheme click-XSS via stored and AI-sourced links
symptom: A live_url/repo_url/pitch_url — or an AI-sourced competitor URL — set to javascript:… became a clickable href that ran script on click
root_cause: URL fields were rendered into href using esc() only, which escapes quotes but does not validate the URL scheme
fix: Added a safeUrl() guard (http/https only, else '#') applied across all 9 href sites, including AI competitor links

title: OCR web worker used relative paths that don't resolve in worker scope
symptom: Tesseract 'Magic Fill' pipeline failed to load its worker/core; status stalled and OCR never ran
root_cause: Worker and LSTM core assets were referenced by relative URL, which do not resolve inside a Web Worker execution context
fix: Switched the worker/core references to absolute URLs (and copied the missing LSTM core variants so all vendor files serve)

title: Book-cover auto-fetch hung on a CORS blob fetch
symptom: Fetching a cover from Open Library hung/failed, so covers never appeared after adding a book
root_cause: Code did a cross-origin blob fetch of the cover image, which CORS blocked
fix: Store the cover URL directly and render it via (cross-origin loads fine and is lighter to sync) instead of fetching a blob

title: Bookshelf niche rendered dark in light themes because data-dark=0 still matched [data-dark]
symptom: In pastel/light themes the bookshelf back-panel niche rendered with the dark-mode material
root_cause: The attribute selector body[data-dark] matches whenever the attribute is present, and data-dark=0 is always present, so light mode matched the dark rule
fix: Target the explicit value with body[data-dark=1] instead of the bare presence selector

title: Global search returned zero results after new sections were added
symptom: Search returned 0 hits while the app claimed you could 'find anything you've ever written'
root_cause: Notes, Books, and Content views were added without extending the search index to include their records
fix: Extended the search index to cover notes, books, content, and journal entries

title: Wedding voice dictation dumped every spoken item into Guests
symptom: Speaking a mixed rundown (budget, vendor, song, gift, to-do) routed everything into the Guests list
root_cause: The wedding dictation parser greedily consumed the whole transcript instead of splitting on command/section boundaries like the planner's parser
fix: Rewrote it to split on command boundaries so items route to guests/budget/vendors/tasks/songs/gifts correctly

title: Voice-search mic threw because voiceSearch() was never defined
symptom: Tapping the voice-search mic did nothing and threw a ReferenceError
root_cause: The voiceSearch() handler was wired to the button but never actually implemented
fix: Implemented voiceSearch() properly (found during the static + in-browser smoke sweep)

title: Billable proxy endpoints unthrottled (denial-of-wallet)
symptom: Anyone could call /api/translate and /api/vision in a loop and run up billable third-party compute.
root_cause: The two endpoints proxied to Google Translate and Workers AI but, unlike /api/backup, had no per-IP rate limit — an unbounded-consumption / denial-of-wallet vector.
fix: Added a shared per-IP rate-limit helper and gated both billable endpoints (verified 429 after 60 calls/IP).

title: Debt payoff projection ignored APR
symptom: Debt-free date and total-interest figures were wrong — too optimistic.
root_cause: The old payoff projection computed months by dividing balance by payment with no interest accrual, so it understated both the payoff time and the total interest.
fix: Replaced with an interest-aware payoff engine (snowball + avalanche), giving an accurate debt-free date, total interest, and extra-payment savings.

title: Magic-ring foundation stitches collapsed to one cell
symptom: Round 1 of nearly every amigurumi ('6 sc in magic ring') counted as a single stitch, undercounting the row.
root_cause: The parser grouped 'N stitch in <target>' as one clustered cell. That is correct for a shell worked INTO one existing stitch, but wrong for a foundation ring where each stitch is individual.
fix: Distinguished ring/foundation targets (expand to N individual cells) from a cluster worked into a single stitch (stays grouped).

title: typeof does not guard a let/const in its temporal dead zone
symptom: A defensive `typeof x` guard still threw ReferenceError at runtime.
root_cause: `typeof` is only safe for truly-undeclared identifiers; for a lexically-declared `let`/`const` referenced before initialization it still throws (TDZ). Common false-safety assumption.
fix: Guard with a try/catch, or move the reference after the declaration / hoist a `var` sentinel.

title: Later same-specificity CSS rule silently overrides mobile media query
symptom: A mobile-only sizing rule had no effect; the element overflowed off-screen on phones.
root_cause: A global sizing rule appeared LATER in the stylesheet at equal specificity, so source order won over the earlier @media (max-width) override.
fix: Place responsive/mobile overrides after the global rules they must beat (or raise their specificity); verify computed width, not just that the rule exists.

title: System prompt leakage (OWASP LLM07:2025)
symptom: Internal system-prompt rules, filters, permissions or hidden logic can be extracted by users and used to bypass controls.
root_cause: Secrets, authorization logic, or trust decisions are placed in the system prompt, which is not a security boundary and can leak.
fix: Never put secrets/keys or the only copy of an access rule in the prompt; enforce authorization server-side; treat any prompt content as potentially public.

title: Vector & embedding weaknesses in RAG (OWASP LLM08:2025)
symptom: Retrieved documents poison answers, or one tenant's embeddings leak into another's results.
root_cause: RAG stores and embedding pipelines are a distinct attack surface from prompt injection — untrusted content is indexed and later trusted, and vector stores often lack per-tenant access control.
fix: Scope/partition the vector store per tenant, sanitize and provenance-tag ingested docs, and treat retrieved text as untrusted input to the model.

title: SSRF: allowlist outbound fetch targets (CWE-918, #1 AI-code flaw)
symptom: A server-side fetch/proxy can be pointed at internal metadata endpoints or arbitrary hosts.
root_cause: AI-generated fetch/proxy handlers commonly forward a user-supplied URL with no destination validation; SSRF is the single most common vuln class in 2026 AI-code studies.
fix: Allowlist schemes+hosts, resolve and block private/link-local IP ranges, disable redirects to new hosts, and never echo raw upstream errors.

title: KV read-after-write returns stale value (eventual consistency)
symptom: Code writes a value to Workers KV then reads it back in the same or next request and gets the OLD value (or a cached 'key does not exist' for a just-created key); UI shows stale data for up to ~60s and 'saves that didn't save' reports follow.
root_cause: KV is eventually consistent: reads are served from edge caches that can lag writes by up to 60s globally. AI codegen treats KV like a synchronous DB and assumes read-your-writes. Negative lookups are cached too, so newly-created keys can read as missing.
fix: Never rely on immediate read-after-write from KV. Return the just-written value from memory instead of re-reading; put anything needing read-your-writes (sessions, counters, dedupe) in D1 or a Durable Object; only use KV for read-mostly config/assets.

title: D1 'too many SQL variables' — 100 bound-parameter limit, not 999
symptom: Bulk insert/update or a WHERE ... IN (?, ?, ...) over a dynamic array throws 'D1_ERROR: too many SQL variables at offset N'; works with a few rows in dev, blows up on real data.
root_cause: D1 caps bound parameters at 100 per statement (lower than stock SQLite's 999). AI-generated bulk writes build one big multi-row INSERT or a giant IN() list whose placeholder count exceeds 100.
fix: Chunk writes so (rows x columns) stays under 100 placeholders per statement and run the chunks with db.batch([...]) in a single transaction; for large IN() lists, chunk the array or join against a temp/values table.

title: Worker subrequest limit hit by per-row D1/KV/fetch in a loop
symptom: A request that iterates over a list and does a DB/KV/fetch call per item suddenly throws 'Too many subrequests' (or the CRON/batch job dies partway) once the list grows; fine with small demo data.
root_cause: Every D1, KV, R2, DO, and fetch() call counts as a subrequest against the per-invocation cap. N+1 loops the AI generated blow through it under real load.
fix: Collapse N calls into one: batch D1 with db.batch()/a single JOIN, use KV bulk/list, cache repeated fetches; move genuinely large fan-out to a Queue or Workflow. Catch the limit exception so the job resumes rather than silently truncating.

title: Request state stored in Worker module globals leaks across users
symptom: Under load, one user intermittently sees another user's data (auth context, cart, tenant id), or the Worker throws 'Cannot perform I/O on behalf of a different request'.
root_cause: Workers reuse a V8 isolate across many requests. AI codegen hoists request-scoped data into module-level let/const (current user, db handle, cache object). Because the isolate persists, request B reads request A's leftover value.
fix: Keep zero mutable request state at module scope. Create per-request objects inside fetch() and thread them through function arguments; put shared handles on env bindings. Treat module globals as read-only constants only.

title: Background work dropped because it wasn't passed to ctx.waitUntil()
symptom: Analytics writes, audit logs, cache warms, or D1 upserts kicked off right before returning a Response land only sometimes; they silently vanish under real traffic with no error.
root_cause: The isolate stops executing pending promises once the response is returned. A fire-and-forget async call that is neither awaited nor registered is cancelled mid-flight, so the write never completes.
fix: Pass any post-response work to ctx.waitUntil(promise) so the runtime keeps it alive after the response is sent; await it instead if the client must see the result. Never leave a floating promise expecting it to finish on its own.
file: worker.js (fetch handler, unawaited async before return)

title: Cache-overwrite race in AI/caching layer corrupts entries
symptom: Under concurrent requests, a cached AI response or computed value gets served for the WRONG input key; passes every test because tests run sequentially, fails only under parallel load.
root_cause: AI-generated memoization uses a shared mutable cache object plus check-then-set with an await in between. Two concurrent calls with different params interleave, and the later write clobbers the entry keyed to a different input.
fix: Key the cache strictly by a hash of the full input and write atomically (no shared 'current' slot); dedupe in-flight identical requests with a promise map; load-test concurrently before merging anything touching caching.

title: Duplicate event listeners stack up on every re-render/re-mount
symptom: A click/submit/keypress handler fires 2x, 3x, Nx (double submits, doubled network calls, runaway toasts); memory grows the longer the SPA session stays open and the tab gets sluggish.
root_cause: addEventListener (often on window/document) is called inside a render/mount path that runs repeatedly, with no matching removeEventListener/cleanup. Each pass adds another live listener that closes over stale state and never gets GC'd.
fix: Register global listeners once outside the render path, or in a mount hook with a symmetric removeEventListener cleanup; for dynamic lists use one delegated listener on a stable parent. Use a named function reference (not an inline arrow) so removal actually matches.

title: White-screen ChunkLoadError after deploy from SPA index.html fallback
symptom: Users with the tab already open (or a stale service worker) get a blank page or 'ChunkLoadError: Loading chunk failed' after a deploy; a hard refresh fixes it, so it looks intermittent.
root_cause: The old cached index.html references content-hashed asset filenames that no longer exist post-deploy. The SPA/static fallback answers the missing /assets/*.js with index.html (HTTP 200, text/html) instead of 404, so the browser parses HTML as a module and the app never mounts.
fix: Make asset paths (extensions like .js/.css) return a real 404 instead of the SPA fallback; serve index.html with no-cache and hashed assets with immutable long cache. Add an inline recovery script that catches failed dynamic imports, unregisters service workers, and does a one-time hard reload.

title: Uncaught QuotaExceededError when writing large blobs to localStorage
symptom: Saving images/base64/large JSON to localStorage throws QuotaExceededError past ~5MB; the write is swallowed so the user's data silently isn't persisted, or the whole save handler crashes.
root_cause: AI codegen stores growing data (drafts, cached API payloads, base64 media) in localStorage with no size budget or error handling. localStorage is a synchronous ~5MB, string-only store; large/binary data overruns it.
fix: Wrap writes in try/catch and handle QuotaExceededError explicitly (evict, or surface a clear message). Move anything large or binary to IndexedDB; keep localStorage for small primitives only. Cap/prune cached payloads and never dump media into it.

title: AI-hallucinated dependency (slopsquatting) pulled into the build
symptom: An install/import references a package that sounds right but isn't the real project; it either 404s the build or, worse, resolves to a squatter's malicious package.
root_cause: LLMs confidently emit non-existent package names at a meaningful rate; attackers pre-register the popular hallucinations on npm/PyPI. Auto-installing whatever the agent wrote runs attacker code.
fix: Verify every AI-suggested dependency exists as the genuine project (publisher, repo, download history) before install; pin exact versions and commit a lockfile; review install scripts. Prefer platform-native bindings over adding packages at all.

title: Failed save/sync silently drops the user's edit (no offline write queue)
symptom: User adds/edits an entry while offline or on a flaky connection; the network call fails and the change just vanishes with no error and no retry. Widely reported (offline sync halting mid-way; habit/journal users losing entries in tunnels/planes).
root_cause: Writes go straight to the network as fire-and-forget; on failure there is no local durable queue, so the edit is lost and the UI may even show it briefly before it evaporates on reload.
fix: Local-first: persist every write to IndexedDB/local storage first, render from local, then flush a durable outbox to the server with retry + backoff. Never discard a local write because the remote call failed; surface a 'pending sync' state instead of dropping data.

title: Unsynced in-memory state wiped on refresh, tab-close, or crash
symptom: Everything the user typed since opening the app is gone after a refresh, an accidental close, or a background-tab eviction.
root_cause: Working state lives only in JS memory and is persisted only on an explicit save or a periodic remote sync; the browser reclaiming the tab or the user reloading throws it away.
fix: Autosave to local storage on every meaningful change (debounced), rehydrate on boot, and treat the server as a sync target, not the only store. Add a beforeunload flush for anything still pending.

title: Export is partial or lossy — misses media, one item at a time, or PDF-only
symptom: Users trying to leave or back up find the export omits photos/attachments/voice notes, only exports a single entry at a time, or dumps to a flat PDF that can't be re-imported.
root_cause: Export was bolted on for text records only and never covered blobs (images, audio, files) or bulk selection; format chosen for looks (PDF) rather than portability.
fix: Ship a one-click 'export everything' that bundles all record types plus their media into an open, re-importable archive (JSON/NDJSON + attachments in a zip). Verify a round-trip re-import. Include derived content (comments, milestones, generated docs), not just raw notes.

title: Concurrent bookings claim the same slot (double-booking race)
symptom: Two visitors open the same booking page, both see a slot as free, and both submit within seconds — the app accepts both and the owner is double-booked.
root_cause: Availability is read once into the client and the final insert does not re-check for a conflicting booking inside the same transaction. No unique constraint on (resource, start_time) and no server-side conflict guard, so simultaneous writes both succeed.
fix: Make the slot the source of truth: add a DB unique constraint / conditional insert on (owner_or_resource, start, end) so the second write fails, re-validate availability server-side at submit time, and on conflict return a friendly 'just taken — pick another time'. Optionally hold a short soft-lock while the visitor fills the form.
file: worker booking POST handler / bookings table schema

title: Availability rendered in owner's timezone, not the visitor's
symptom: Slots show the business's local hours to every visitor regardless of where they are, so an out-of-area client books '2pm' meaning their own 2pm and shows up at the wrong hour.
root_cause: Times are formatted from stored local/naive datetimes without converting to the visitor's detected timezone, and the page never states which timezone the times are in.
fix: Store all slots in UTC, detect the visitor's timezone (Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone), render every time converted to it, always print an explicit timezone label plus a picker to override, and spell out both parties' timezones in the confirmation.

title: Data export silently omits notes, activity history and timeline
symptom: Users export 'all my data' to leave or back up and get only the contact/lead rows — call notes, emails, meeting history and timeline events are missing, discovered only after the old tool is gone.
root_cause: The export function serialises only the primary entity table and does not join or include child records (notes, comms, activity, attachments), so related history is dropped without warning.
fix: Export the full object graph, not just top-level rows: include notes, communications, activity/timeline, attachments and payment history in one archive. Show a per-table row count so users can verify completeness.

title: Bulk import silently drops rows it can't parse
symptom: A user uploads 200 leads; 170 land, 30 vanish with no message. The loss is invisible until a customer can't be found weeks later.
root_cause: The importer try/catches per row and continues on parse failure without recording or surfacing which rows were skipped, and never reconciles input count against inserted count.
fix: Count input rows, count inserts, and after import show 'N imported, M skipped, K duplicates' with a downloadable list of the exact skipped rows and why. Never discard an unparseable row silently.

title: Low-contrast text below the 4.5:1 minimum
symptom: Light grey body text on white is unreadable for low-vision users and in sunlight; appears on ~84% of homepages, the single most common accessibility failure.
root_cause: Palettes are chosen for aesthetics against a bright designer monitor; muted greys used for 'secondary' text fall under the WCAG minimum without anyone measuring.
fix: Enforce 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text (and for UI/graphical boundaries). Check every token pair in BOTH light and dark themes with a contrast checker, not by eye.

title: Images with no alt attribute
symptom: Screen readers announce the raw filename (or nothing) instead of the image's meaning; present on ~53% of pages.
root_cause: alt is optional in HTML so it is silently omitted, especially for generated/icon/decorative images.
fix: Every gets an alt: descriptive text for meaningful images, alt="" for purely decorative ones so it is skipped. Detector: A11Y-IMG-ALT.

title: Form field with no associated label
symptom: A screen reader reaches the input and announces only 'edit text' — the user cannot tell what to type. Affects ~51% of pages and has been a top failure for over five years.
root_cause: A placeholder is mistaken for a label. Placeholders vanish on focus and are not exposed as the accessible name.
fix: Give each field an id plus <label for=…>, or an aria-label when a visible label is genuinely impossible. Never rely on placeholder alone. Detector: A11Y-INPUT-NOLABEL.

title: Icon-only button or link with no accessible name
symptom: Screen readers announce 'button' or read out the URL; empty links appear on ~46% of pages and empty buttons on ~31%.
root_cause: Icon-only controls (an SVG or icon font with no text node) ship without aria-label because they look self-explanatory to a sighted developer.
fix: Add aria-label (or visually-hidden text) to every icon-only control; give inline SVGs a <title>. Detector: A11Y-EMPTY-CONTROL.

title: Document missing a lang attribute
symptom: Screen readers pronounce the page with the wrong language voice, making content hard or impossible to follow.
root_cause: <html> is written without lang; nothing visually breaks so it is never noticed.
fix: Set <html lang="en"> (or the actual language), and mark inline foreign-language passages with their own lang. Detector: A11Y-NO-LANG.

title: Focus indicator removed by outline:none
symptom: Keyboard users tabbing through the interface cannot see where they are — focus becomes invisible.
root_cause: outline:none is applied to kill the default focus ring for aesthetics, with no replacement style.
fix: Never reset the outline without providing a high-contrast :focus-visible style. WCAG 2.2 requires a visible focus indicator meeting minimum size and contrast. Detector: A11Y-FOCUS-KILLED.

title: Positive tabindex breaks the natural tab order
symptom: Tabbing jumps around the page unpredictably, skipping or reordering controls.
root_cause: tabindex is set to a positive number to 'fix' an ordering problem, which promotes those elements ahead of the entire document order.
fix: Use only tabindex="0" (focusable in document order) or "-1" (programmatic focus). Fix ordering by fixing the DOM order. Detector: A11Y-POSITIVE-TABINDEX.

title: Click handler on a div/span — not keyboard reachable
symptom: A control works with a mouse but cannot be reached or activated by keyboard or screen reader at all.
root_cause: onclick is attached to a non-interactive element, which gets no implicit role, no focusability and no Enter/Space activation.
fix: Use a real <button>. If impossible, add role="button", tabindex="0" and an explicit Enter/Space keydown handler. Detector: A11Y-CLICK-NONINTERACTIVE.

title: Unverifiable superlative claim shipped in product copy
symptom: The product asserts it is the 'first', 'only' or 'best' of its kind, and the claim turns out to be untrue when checked against primary sources.
root_cause: Marketing copy is written from assumption (often generated by an LLM) and never verified against the actual market before shipping.
fix: Verify every superlative against a primary source or soften it to something provable ('built for…', 'designed around…'). Unprovable comparative claims are both a trust problem and an advertising-law risk. Detector: CLAIM-SUPERLATIVE.

title: Manufactured scarcity or urgency in the UI
symptom: The page shows a countdown, 'only 3 left', or 'X people are viewing this' that is not derived from real state.
root_cause: Pressure tactics are copied from ecommerce patterns and hardcoded or randomised rather than driven by actual inventory/traffic.
fix: Only display scarcity that is literally true and derived from real data. Fabricated urgency is unlawful under UK/EU consumer protection rules and an active enforcement target. Detector: CLAIM-FAKE-SCARCITY.

title: Statistic published with no citable source
symptom: A percentage or research-style figure appears in marketing or in-app copy, and no one can say where it came from when challenged.
root_cause: Numbers are absorbed from blog posts, competitor sites or model output and repeated as fact without tracing them to a primary source.
fix: Every published number needs a real, checkable primary source recorded next to it; if you cannot cite it, delete it. Detector: CLAIM-UNSOURCED-STAT.

title: Placeholder or sample content shipped to real users
symptom: Lorem ipsum, TODO markers, 'John Doe' testimonials or 'your text here' appear in the live product.
root_cause: Scaffolding copy is left in place because the surrounding layout looks finished.
fix: Sweep for placeholder patterns before every deploy. Note that fabricated testimonials are not just embarrassing — they are unlawful. Detector: CLAIM-PLACEHOLDER.

title: AI-generated fact asserted to users without verification
symptom: A feature summary, competitor comparison or 'insight' presented to users contains details the model invented.
root_cause: Model output is rendered straight into the UI as authoritative, with no grounding constraint and no human or source check.
fix: Ground generated text strictly in supplied data, instruct the model never to invent, show the source alongside the claim, and fall back to a deterministic local summary when grounding is unavailable.

title: Collects personal data with no privacy policy
symptom: The product takes an email, name or phone number and there is no policy anywhere saying what happens to it.
root_cause: The signup form ships before any legal surface exists; nothing in the build fails without one.
fix: Publish a privacy policy stating what you collect, why, the legal basis, how long you keep it and how to delete it. Required under UK/EU GDPR and by both app stores. Detector: PRIV-NO-POLICY.

title: Accounts exist with no delete-my-data path
symptom: A user asks to be deleted and there is no mechanism — deleting the app leaves everything on the server.
root_cause: Deletion is treated as an edge case and deferred; signup is built, teardown never is.
fix: Ship a one-tap 'delete my account and data' that genuinely purges server records and backups, and state honestly what it cannot reach (e.g. immutable audit logs). A GDPR right and an app-store requirement. Detector: PRIV-NO-DELETE.

title: Sensitive data routed through third-party ad/analytics SDKs
symptom: Health, reproductive, financial or precise-location data is transmitted to advertising or analytics platforms as a side effect of a routine SDK.
root_cause: An analytics or ads SDK is dropped in globally and captures form fields, page context or events on screens that handle sensitive categories.
fix: Classify sensitive data explicitly; keep it on-device or end-to-end encrypted; never let it reach third-party ad/analytics/attribution SDKs; gate any tracker behind explicit consent and offer a local-only mode. A jury held a major platform liable in 2025 for exactly this pattern. Detector: PRIV-3P-TRACKER.

title: Personal data placed in a URL query string
symptom: Emails, tokens or identifiers appear in links, and therefore in server logs, browser history, bookmarks and outbound Referer headers.
root_cause: GET is used for convenience when passing state between pages or to an API.
fix: Never put personal data or secrets in a URL. Use a POST body or an opaque short-lived id, and set an appropriate Referrer-Policy. Detector: PRIV-PII-IN-URL.

title: Personal data or credentials written to logs
symptom: Emails, passwords, tokens or entire user records land in the console and in retained server logs.
root_cause: Whole objects are logged during debugging and the statements are never removed.
fix: Log identifiers, never payloads. Redact known-sensitive keys centrally in the logging helper so it cannot be forgotten at a call site. Detector: PRIV-PII-LOG.

title: Consent banner that is non-compliant or purely decorative
symptom: Non-essential cookies/trackers load before any consent is given, or the banner offers 'Accept all' with no equally easy 'Reject all'.
root_cause: The banner is added as a visual disclaimer rather than as an actual gate on script execution.
fix: Load no non-essential tracker until consent is recorded; make reject as prominent and as few clicks as accept; store and honour the choice; nothing pre-ticked.

title: Data kept indefinitely with no retention policy
symptom: Every record ever created is still stored, including data for deleted or long-dormant accounts.
root_cause: No retention period is defined, and storage is cheap enough that nothing forces the question.
fix: Define and document a retention period per data class, delete or anonymise past it on a schedule, and state the periods in the privacy policy. GDPR storage limitation requires it.

title: No tests anywhere in the project
symptom: Every regression is found by a user; there is no signal before deploy that the core loop still works.
root_cause: AI-assisted builds move fast and produce working features without a test harness; nothing in the workflow demands one.
fix: Add at least a smoke test of the core loop (sign in → create → save → reload and it persists → export) and run it against the built artifact before shipping. Detector: TEST-NONE.

title: .only() left in a test suite silently skips everything else
symptom: CI stays green while running a single test; broken code ships because the rest of the suite never executed.
root_cause: describe.only/it.only is used to focus one case during debugging and committed by accident.
fix: Remove .only before committing and add a lint or CI rule that fails the build when it appears. Detector: TEST-ONLY.

title: Permanently skipped tests present as dead coverage
symptom: The suite reports passing while meaningful cases are disabled, overstating real coverage.
root_cause: A failing test is skipped to unblock a release and never revisited.
fix: Fix it or delete it — a skipped test is not coverage. If it must stay, give it an owner and an expiry. Detector: TEST-SKIPPED.

title: Tests exist but no CI runs them
symptom: A regression reaches production even though a test covering it exists, because nobody ran the suite.
root_cause: Tests are run manually and locally; no automation gates the push or deploy.
fix: Add a CI workflow that runs the suite on every push and blocks deploy on failure. Detector: TEST-NO-CI.

title: No Open Graph or Twitter card — shared links render as a bare URL
symptom: Pasting the product link into a message, Slack or social post shows a naked URL with no title, description or image, so nobody clicks.
root_cause: og: and twitter: meta tags are never added because nothing in the page looks broken without them.
fix: Add og:title, og:description, og:image (1200×630) and twitter:card to every shareable page, and verify with a card validator. Detector: SEO-NO-OG.

title: Page has no <title> or meta description
symptom: Browser tabs read 'index.html' or the domain, and search results show a machine-generated snippet.
root_cause: The page is built as an app shell rather than a document; the head is never filled in.
fix: Give every page a unique descriptive <title> and a meta description written for a human reading a search result. Detectors: SEO-NO-TITLE, SEO-NO-DESC.

title: No viewport meta — the page renders desktop-width on phones
symptom: On a phone the whole layout is zoomed out and tiny, or controls run off the edge of the screen.
root_cause: The viewport meta tag is missing, so mobile browsers assume a ~980px desktop viewport.
fix: Add <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">. This is also the root cause behind many 'control is off-screen on mobile' reports. Detector: SEO-NO-VIEWPORT.

title: Empty catch block swallows the error
symptom: A feature silently does nothing; there is no error in the console and no clue in any log about what failed.
root_cause: catch {} is used to stop an exception propagating, discarding the error object entirely.
fix: Never leave a catch empty: log the error with context and surface a user-visible failure state. If the failure genuinely is expected and safe, say so in a comment. Detector: OBS-EMPTY-CATCH.

title: Promise chain with no .catch — rejections vanish
symptom: An async action fails with no visible effect; the UI shows a spinner forever or silently stays unchanged.
root_cause: A .then() chain has no .catch(), so a rejection becomes an unhandled rejection that nothing reports.
fix: Attach .catch() to every chain (or use try/await), and register a global unhandledrejection handler as a backstop. Detector: OBS-UNHANDLED-PROMISE.

title: No global error handler — front-end crashes are invisible
symptom: Users report a white screen or a dead button and there is no record anywhere that anything went wrong.
root_cause: Nothing listens for window 'error' or 'unhandledrejection', so client-side failures never leave the browser.
fix: Register window error and unhandledrejection listeners that log/report with context (route, build version, user id — never personal data). Without them a white screen produces no signal at all. Detector: OBS-NO-ERROR-HANDLER.

title: No build/version stamp to correlate an error with a deploy
symptom: A bug report cannot be tied to a release, so it is impossible to tell whether a fix shipped or which deploy caused a regression.
root_cause: The app exposes no version or build identifier, and errors carry no deploy context.
fix: Stamp a build id/version into the app, show it in settings or the console, and attach it to every logged error so failures map to a specific deploy.

title: Recovery keys generated with Math.random (brute-forceable)
symptom: Cloud-data recovery keys came from Math.random (~15.5M combos); the key IS the password to a users synced blob, so the space is scannable.
root_cause: Math.random is not cryptographically secure.
fix: Regenerated recovery keys with crypto.getRandomValues (~39 quadrillion combos). Same fix applied to Hello Baby.

title: Opaque gate never left, so Take-me-in did nothing
symptom: The sign-in gate stayed opaque over the booted app and the Take-me-in button appeared dead.
root_cause: Author .gate{display:grid} beat the UA [hidden]{display:none} rule (author styles win), so setting hidden had no effect.
fix: Global [hidden]{display:none!important} near the CSS reset; pad rebuilt to exactly 5 digits with phone letters.

title: Deck chip truncated the name to M...
symptom: A slide chip clipped the label (e.g. M...) instead of showing the full name.
root_cause: The chip had flex-shrink:0, starving the name of width.
fix: Chip yields width first and titles wrap to two lines; also added reading-progress and tick-off.

title: Unsupportable 47% more productive landing claim
symptom: The landing asserted 47% more productive and other stats with no citable source.
root_cause: Marketing copy used an unverified stat (traces to a non-peer-reviewed internal note).
fix: Cut to verified-only claims; validated the manual-first default against real, still-true competitor gaps.

title: Live board cards blinked every poll
symptom: Activity timelines/boards re-appended cards each poll, replaying the CSS entrance animation so cards flickered every ~1.5s.
root_cause: Re-render/re-append replayed the one-time entrance animation.
fix: One-shot .enter class stripped after it plays; re-render only when content or order changes. Shipped as a reusable module.

title: Currency picker logic duplicated per app
symptom: The 153-currency parse-search picker was re-implemented in each app, duplicating a whole class of currency bugs.
root_cause: No shared module for the picker.
fix: Extracted to a standalone dependency-free module (CurrencyPicker.search/open/button) that ships its own sheet and CSS.

title: Business plan and /deck must not leak on any direct path
symptom: A passcode-gated business plan plus /deck could leak via direct asset paths (plan.html.txt, src, deck).
root_cause: Static assets can be served before the auth gate runs.
fix: Plan and deck live on a separate PLAN_PASS-gated Worker; verified every direct path returns the lock screen.

title: Admin surface kept off the user-facing app
symptom: Putting admin oversight (which reads the app D1) inside the main app would widen its attack surface.
root_cause: Admin routes co-located with the user app.
fix: Admin runs as a separate passcode-gated Worker that reads the app D1; nothing admin ships in the user bundle.

title: Touch target smaller than 24×24 CSS px (WCAG 2.2 · 2.5.8 Target Size)
symptom: Small icon buttons — a row options dot, a drag handle, an inline ✕, a bell toggle — are hard to hit accurately on touch and fail WCAG 2.2 Target Size (Minimum).
root_cause: Icons sized to the glyph (16–20px) with no padded hit area.
fix: Give every pointer target at least a 24×24px hit area (padding or min-width/height), or space inline controls so each has 24px of exclusive space. Exceptions: inline-in-text links and equivalent nearby controls.

title: Drag-only interaction with no single-pointer alternative (WCAG 2.2 · 2.5.7 Dragging Movements)
symptom: Reorder / move / slider interactions that only work by dragging exclude users who cannot perform a drag (motor impairment, switch access).
root_cause: Drag implemented as the sole path.
fix: Always pair a drag with a non-drag alternative — Move up/down buttons, a right-click/kebab menu, or number entry — unless dragging is essential.

title: PIN/OTP field blocks paste or uses a cognitive-test CAPTCHA (WCAG 2.2 · 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication)
symptom: A login/recovery step relies on a cognitive function test (transcribe/solve/recognise) or disables paste into the code field, which WCAG 2.2 Accessible Authentication (Minimum) forbids without an alternative.
root_cause: Anti-bot or per-digit inputs that intercept paste; puzzle CAPTCHAs with no alternative.
fix: Allow paste and password managers to fill PIN/OTP fields; offer a non-cognitive authentication path; avoid puzzle/transcription CAPTCHAs as the only option.

title: Calendar and day views grouped trades by the UTC date of an ISO timestamp, putting evening futures trades on the wrong day
symptom: Futures trades taken late in the local day appeared under the following calendar day, so per-day totals and per-trade minis in the month calendar were wrong.
root_cause: tradeDay() sliced the first 10 characters of the UTC ISO string instead of deriving the trader's local calendar date.
fix: Day grouping now uses the trader's local date; verified both test futures trades group on the 24th with a +$1,600 total and per-trade minis.

title: Live-session voice parser took filler words as tickers and let exit/stop chunks overwrite the entry price
symptom: 'took profit exit at 18475' created symbol TOOK and overwrote NQ; the exit chunk's 'at 18475' replaced the entry price, so the saved trade lost its entry.
root_cause: The symbol regex accepted any capitalised token not in the keyword list, and mergeTrade() merged every field of each later transcript chunk over the existing trade.
fix: Added the missing words to the keyword list, a guard that stops later chunks overwriting an established symbol, and made lifecycle chunks merge only close-side fields (exit_price, stop_price, target_price, pnl, fees); NQ entry 18450 to exit 18475 preserved.

title: Naturally dictated trade phrasing ('log a trade, pinterest ticker PINS ... price right now is 23.47') logged nothing
symptom: A real user dictation with a company name, the word 'ticker' and a spoken price produced no trade at all.
root_cause: parseTrade only recognised terse tickers/prices and trade intent was detected from a narrow phrase list; there was no 'ticker X' form, company-name lookup or 'price right now is N' form.
fix: Added a ticker-phrase regex, a company-name to ticker map, a price-phrase regex and broader trade-intent detection; the exact failing utterance now yields {symbol: PINS, entry_price: 23.47}.

title: Live-session P&L ignored the futures contract point value
symptom: NQ session P&L was computed with the wrong per-point value ($50 per point) instead of the contract point value, so futures trades in the live session summary were mis-valued.
root_cause: session.js buildTradeBody did its own price*qty maths instead of calling the point-value function the journal already used.
fix: Exposed window.pointValue from views.js and used it in the session buildTradeBody; verified NQ and equity point values (equity x1) before committing.

title: Muted/faint text was nearly invisible on light-tinted themes such as babypink
symptom: On pastel themes the secondary grey text and placeholders washed out against the tinted background; the user asked for the grey to follow each theme's colour and stay readable.
root_cause: One global muted tone was reused across all 14+ imported themes, and on pale themes it landed too close to the background.
fix: Per-theme muted/dim tokens (e.g. mauve on babypink) and theme-tinted inputs with readable placeholders; verified on the babypink theme.

title: Live chart watch board always fetched 1d candles even while the user was sharing a 1m chart
symptom: Watching a fast timeframe on TradingView, the board still read daily bars, so signal readouts did not match what the user saw.
root_cause: refreshBoard() called fetchCandles(symbol, '1d') with the timeframe hard-coded and there was no timeframe state on the watch object.
fix: Added a timeframe selector (1m to 1d) to the board, stored it on the LW state, fetched at the chosen timeframe, and made Ava suggest switching the board and the TradingView chart when the top rule needs a different interval; verified the switch does not stop the screen-share stream.

title: Native app targeted iOS 17.0 so it could not install on the owner's iOS 16.7.16 iPhone
symptom: The iPhone build would have been refused on the owner's phone even after Developer Mode was enabled.
root_cause: The Xcode project deployment target was left at iOS 17.0 although every API used (SwiftUI Charts, NavigationStack, vertical TextField) is available from iOS 16.
fix: Lowered the deployment target to iOS 16.0, rebuilt with zero availability warnings and re-ran the app on the simulator.

title: Native app aborted right after granting speech/microphone permission (AudioUnit RPC timeout)
symptom: Tapping Allow on the mic/speech prompt in the iOS simulator killed the app.
root_cause: The .ips crash report shows abort() from AudioToolbox _ReportRPCTimeout via AURemoteIO::Initialize / AudioUnitInitialize: the audio engine was started with no usable input path right after the permission grant.
fix: Speech.swift gained an inputUnavailable state and a guard around starting the recogniser/audio engine so unavailable input is reported in the UI instead of aborting the process; rebuilt for iOS and Mac.

title: Swift URL.appendingPathComponent percent-encoded '?', so native candle requests failed and the backtest silently did nothing
symptom: On iPhone/Mac, Backtest returned to the same screen with no result and no error.
root_cause: botCandles built '/bot/candles?symbol=...&interval=...' with appendingPathComponent, which encodes '?' as %3F so the server saw a bad path.
fix: Build the URL from a string/URLComponents so the query survives; backtest then ran on real Kraken candles (commit b026e6a).

title: SQLite datetime('now') strings failed both ISO-8601 parsers on native, so events showed as 56 years old
symptom: The native notifications sheet showed '56 yrs' ago and mis-sorted signals and fills.
root_cause: SQLite datetime('now') returns 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' (space, no T, no zone); both ISO8601DateFormatter variants rejected it and the fallback was epoch 0.
fix: Added an explicit UTC parser for the space-separated format; signals and fills now sort correctly and show '3 days, 20 hr'.

title: Native dark/glass pass: large currency number wrapped ('$20146 8'), pushed views lost the theme background and white tiles glared
symptom: On iPhone the big account-size figure wrapped mid-number, pushed screens showed black behind light-theme tiles, tiles were blinding white in dark mode and pager dots overlapped card content.
root_cause: Themed background and glass card styling were not applied to pushed views, and numeric text had no single-line/scale limit, so layout broke on long figures.
fix: Single-line scaled numbers, theme background on pushed views, a glass CardStyle for dark mode and dot spacing; verified in light and dark on the exact screen from the user's screenshot.

title: Worker router skipped JSON body parsing for /api/media/*, so new JSON multipart-upload routes received an empty body
symptom: The new create/part/complete multipart endpoints returned errors because body was empty even though the client sent JSON.
root_cause: The router deliberately skipped JSON parsing for everything under /api/media to protect binary uploads, which also swallowed the three JSON control routes added under that prefix.
fix: Parse the JSON body inside those three handlers; proven with served multipart test calls and then the Claude Fathom pipeline on the uploaded memo.

title: A research 'block for v1' recommendation was hard-coded as a legal block, excluding cosmetics/personal care
symptom: The catalogue refused the biggest TikTok Shop category and the user's explicit 'personal hygiene' scope although selling them only needs a gate.
root_cause: compliance.js treated a lane's risk-appetite suggestion as a regulatory prohibition and, separately, the same session had acted on a critique (Lane G's CAC figure) without verifying the critic; verified data showed a UK CPSR starts around 55 pounds, most lines finish under 500 and a seller can be their own Responsible Person.
fix: Moved cosmetics and installed batteries from blocked to gated (named Responsible Person, CPSR reference, SCPN/CPNP, ingredient list; UN38.3 for batteries) while keeping genuinely licensed categories blocked; gate re-tested at 47 rules (19 clean, 13 gated, 15 blocked).

title: Voice intent parser matched substrings: 'home' in 'trending home decor' went to the homepage and 'sell' fired inside 'best selling'
symptom: Spoken commands navigated to the wrong place; 'add this to my basket' only opened the basket.
root_cause: Intent keywords were checked as plain substrings in a fixed order, and navigation words were tested before search/filter phrases.
fix: Word-boundary matching, search/filter phrases checked before navigation words, and an add-to-basket intent that acts; testing before wiring found five defects and the parser reached 17/17 intents ('show me trending home decor under $50' now yields category, price cap and sort).

title: Denied microphone permission closed the voice panel, hiding both the error and the command list
symptom: Pressing V with the mic blocked flashed a toast and closed the panel, leaving the user with no explanation or help.
root_cause: The recogniser onError handler always removed the panel's 'on' class.
fix: For not-allowed/service-not-allowed/audio-capture errors the panel stays open with a 'Voice needs microphone access' message above the command list.

title: Keyword-matched filler photos (loremflickr) ignored the lock param, so unrelated products shared one fallback image
symptom: A vase, a throw and a washi-tape set all showed the same cat-statue photo even though every image URL was unique.
root_cause: loremflickr returns one generic fallback for obscure keyword combinations and did not honour ?lock=, so distinct URLs still resolved to the same picture.
fix: Switched to per-product deterministic picsum seeds derived from the product id; verified 63 products have 63 distinct first images (duplicates: 0), accepting 'distinct but not subject-matched' over duplicated.

title: Pricing copy told users they can 'prove the ROI' of every creator while the feature's own research says attribution is directional
symptom: The $50 Business bullet 'hire, contract, pay & prove the ROI of every creator' is an absolute, substantiation-style claim that the product itself disclaims (influence is under-counted, read it as direction).
root_cause: Marketing bullets were written from the feature list without checking the verb against the caveats shipped in the same feature (FTC s5 / UK CAP substantiation exposure).
fix: Pro now says 'see the payback'; the Business line still needs the same one-word change (prove to track/see the payback) on landing.html and views4.js, and the in-app IP and valuation caveats must stay.

title: WhatsApp was in the master social-platform map but missing from about ten hard-coded platform lists
symptom: A WhatsApp channel could be logged in Socials but not detected from a pasted link, not added in Rolodex/Creators/Study/Org profile, and rendered as a plain 'W' monogram with no media-kit or auto-site emoji.
root_cause: The platform list was duplicated across socials.js PLATS, socialsx.js platGuess/prettyPlat/emoji, rolodex, creators, study, org form and save payload, kit.html, site.html, views2/views3 and Ava's vision list instead of read from one source.
fix: Swept every hard-coded list and added WhatsApp (glyph, wa.me link builder, org field oWa, paste-link detection, icons, Ava inference), bumped ?v= 210 to 211 and verified the live files.

title: to-do-list streak card rendered dark in light mode: the dark override sat outside the @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) block
symptom: The routine streak card was a dark panel on a light page.
root_cause: The rule '.tdl:not([data-theme="light"]) .tdl-streak' was written as a normal selector, not inside the media query, so it applied in every colour scheme.
fix: Kept only the explicit [data-theme="dark"] selector at top level and moved the :not([data-theme="light"]) variant inside the media query; verified light and dark in the browser.
