root_cause: static assets are served before the Worker; run_worker_first patterns match the raw path while the asset server normalises // and percent-encoding, and the JS payload sat in public/ so gating the HTML protected nothing
fix: both files moved out of public/ into src/private/*.txt and imported as Worker Text modules (rules glob **/*.txt); /pitch normalises the path then checks PITCH_KEY; 15 attack paths all 404

title: Google API key sent as ?key= query string to Cloud TTS (leaks into logs and URLs)
symptom: Worker called texttospeech.googleapis.com/v1/text:synthesize?key=<secret>
root_cause: key placed in the URL instead of a header
fix: moved to the X-goog-api-key header

title: AI, vision, TTS and translate proxy endpoints answered without any session (billable to the owner's Claude and Google keys)
symptom: curl -X POST /api/ai and /api/translate returned results anonymously; Studio TTS costs $160 per extra million characters and the 1M free allowance is per Google project, not per customer
root_cause: first-wave worker routes had no auth or quota
fix: per-account TTS character budget added (6k free / 20k Plus / 60k Pro / 150k Business) with an in-app meter; OPEN: confirm /api/ai, /api/vision and /api/translate are session-gated and metered (AI credits queued)

title: sed-based secret masking silently failed on pretty-printed JSON, printing the Bug Ledger token into the transcript
symptom: A command meant to show ~/.bugledger.json with the token masked printed the full token in the tool output, so it sits in the session transcript.
root_cause: The sed pattern expected no space after the colon in the token line, but the file is pretty-printed with a space, so nothing matched and the line passed through.
fix: Never cat credential files. Read them with node and print only the length or a prefix, or mask via a JSON parser rather than a regex. Rotate any token that was printed.

title: Etsy OAuth access/refresh tokens and shared secret stored as plaintext columns in D1
symptom: The etsy_links table keeps shared_secret, access_token and refresh_token as plain TEXT, so anyone with D1 read access (a dump or an over-broad query) gets live read access to sellers' Etsy shops.
root_cause: The tokens are kept server-side (good) but not encrypted at rest.
fix: Left open. Encrypt the three columns with AES-GCM using a key derived from a Worker secret before insert, decrypt on use, and add a revoke/delete-on-disconnect check.

title: Unauthenticated GET /api/inventions exposes all 24 invention disclosures
symptom: curl returned HTTP 200 with count 24 and no auth. Every disclosure, including the 'candidate' inventions and drafted claim language describing the other apps' internals, is publicly readable.
root_cause: The read API was left public while only the write API is protected by PATENT_KEY. Public disclosure destroys novelty in the UK/EU (Patents Act s.2(2), no general grace period); only the US 12-month grace (35 USC 102(b)(1)(A)) is still running.
fix: Open: put the read routes behind the owner auth or PATENT_KEY now, and treat anything already served as published for prior-art purposes.

title: Pre-approved wildcard Bash rules plus an instruction to re-download the CLI on every run give code execution to whoever controls that Worker
symptom: Global instructions tell every agent to re-fetch apz.mjs, and the same pattern exists for the Pixelbake and Breadcrumb CLIs, from a coconvo.workers.dev URL before each run, and settings.local.json pre-approves node ~/.aprizely/apz.mjs with a wildcard so it runs without a prompt. A compromised Worker deploy, DNS or account takeover could ship code that runs unattended with the user's tokens and file access on the next agent run.
root_cause: Trust is anchored to a mutable remote URL: the always-refresh rule exists to avoid stale CLIs, the allow rule matches any arguments, and nothing verifies a hash, signature or version before execution.
fix: Pin each CLI by SHA-256 (keep the expected hash locally, verify after the download and refuse to run on a mismatch) or serve a signed manifest; write the download to a temp file and swap it in only after verification; narrow the allow rules to exact subcommands.

title: Temporary account passcode echoed into chat and tool output and passed on the command line
symptom: While seeding the owner's account, the generated 6-digit temporary passcode was printed by cat of seed/.passcode.txt, passed as a process argument to seed.mjs, and repeated in the final chat message, so it now sits in the session transcript.
root_cause: Credential handling optimised for convenience: the value was generated in the shell, written in plaintext to a gitignored file and then read back and quoted to show the user.
fix: Generate the passcode, write it to a mode-600 file and print only the path; pass it by environment variable or stdin instead of argv; force a change on first login; never quote it in the reply.

title: Public handle-availability endpoint lets anyone enumerate existing account handles
symptom: An unauthenticated signup helper reports whether a handle is taken, and a code comment accepts that handles are semi-public. Any script can probe candidate handles and learn which accounts exist, including the owner's account.
root_cause: The availability check returns an exact taken-or-free answer with no authentication or CAPTCHA, and the handle doubles as the login identifier on an app whose only secret is a 5 to 6 digit passcode.
fix: Keep the check but give it a low per-IP budget, check availability only at submit time where possible, and rely on the existing lockout so a known handle is not a cheap first step; consider a generic response for taken handles on the login screen.

title: Admin status is granted to anyone who signs up with an unclaimed handle in ADMIN_HANDLES (rhema and rhemajoy are free on the live app)
symptom: isAdmin() is true for any user whose handle string is in the ADMIN_HANDLES var (seven,rhema,rhemajoy,rhe). Signup is open and only checks that a handle is free and not in the small RESERVED set; a live POST /api/auth/check returned status free for 'rhema' and 'rhemajoy' (taken for 'rhe' and 'seven'). Whoever registers an unclaimed admin handle gets /api/admin/grant (up to 1,000,000 credits and any plan to any handle), showcase curation and every admin credit exemption.
root_cause: Authorisation keyed on a mutable, self-chosen string instead of a pre-registered account id; the admin handles were never reserved or pre-created.
fix: Open - remove unclaimed handles from ADMIN_HANDLES (or add them to RESERVED and pre-create them), key admin on user ids set by migration, and require a second factor or the owner's agent token for /api/admin/grant.

title: Sign-in has no brute-force lockout on 4-8 digit PINs and reveals which handles exist
symptom: POST /api/auth/signin checks the PIN with no attempt counter, delay or lockout, PINs may be as short as 4 digits, and the failure message is 'No account with that handle.' for an unknown handle versus 'Wrong PIN.' for a known one, so handles can be enumerated and any account (including the admin and credit-holding ones) can be guessed online.
root_cause: The Evertrue-style PBKDF2 recipe was copied without its rate limiting; the signin route only compares hash !== u.pin_hash (non-constant-time) and returns distinct errors.
fix: Open - add a per-handle and per-IP failed-attempt counter in D1 with a lockout window, a single generic 'Wrong handle or PIN' error, constant-time hash comparison, and a minimum PIN length of 6.

title: esc() HTML helper does not escape quotes → attribute-context XSS
symptom: User-controlled data interpolated into an HTML attribute can break out of the attribute and inject markup/script.
root_cause: The escape helper in public/js/hl.js escapes <>& but not single/double quotes, so it is unsafe in attribute context.
fix: Also escape ' and " (' / ") in esc(), or set values via setAttribute/textContent instead of string-building attributes.

title: Portfolio scan 2026-10-04: XSS-INNERHTML fires HIGH on 18 of 23 apps
symptom: innerHTML / insertAdjacentHTML sinks with interpolated data are the single most widespread high-severity issue across the portfolio (18/23 scanned apps).
root_cause: AI-generated UI code habitually builds DOM via innerHTML template strings; corroborated externally by Veracode 2025 (XSS ~86% failure rate in AI code).
fix: Sweep every app for innerHTML sinks; prefer textContent/DOM APIs or an escaping helper that also escapes quotes; make XSS-INNERHTML a release gate.

title: LLM features: constrain Improper Output Handling + Excessive Agency (OWASP LLM 2025 LLM05/LLM06)
symptom: Grounded/AI features (Workers AI chat, call-recap, FAQ bots) can emit attacker-influenced output that is rendered as HTML or used to trigger actions, and can be given more agency than the task needs.
root_cause: LLM output treated as trusted; agent/tool wiring grants broad side-effects.
fix: Treat LLM output as untrusted: escape before render, never innerHTML it; scope tool/agent permissions to the minimum; keep a human-in-loop for side-effectful actions (matches the draft-and-send house style).

title: LLM endpoints need Unbounded-Consumption / billable-DoS guards (OWASP LLM 2025 LLM10)
symptom: A public AI endpoint on a metered platform (Workers AI) can be hammered to run up cost or exhaust quota.
root_cause: No per-IP/session rate limit or token cap on the AI route.
fix: Rate-limit and cap tokens/length on every public LLM route; prefer FAQ/static fallback; alert on spend.
source: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025 LLM10

title: System-prompt / context leakage when page context is stuffed into an LLM prompt (OWASP LLM 2025 LLM07/LLM02)
symptom: Grounded features that inject page or FAQ context into the prompt can leak the system prompt or sensitive context back to the user.
root_cause: Secrets/instructions placed in the same prompt as user-reachable content.
fix: Keep secrets out of prompts; segregate instructions from retrieved context; assume the system prompt can be extracted.
source: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025 LLM07/LLM02

title: XSS is the #1 failure mode of AI-generated code (86% fail rate) — audit every innerHTML/template sink
symptom: AI-written UI code repeatedly builds DOM via innerHTML/template strings with uninterpolated user data.
root_cause: Insecure patterns copied from training data; Veracode 2025 found 45% of AI code fails OWASP tests, XSS worst at ~86%.
fix: Grep for innerHTML/insertAdjacentHTML/`${}` into DOM; use textContent or escape; the ledger's XSS-INNERHTML detector should run on every build.

title: Broken authorization / business-logic is the dominant CRITICAL class in AI-built apps — verify flows, not just presence of auth
symptom: Auth exists but multi-step authorization and ownership checks are wrong (e.g. object belongs to another user, capability not re-checked server-side).
root_cause: AI generates plausible auth scaffolding but mis-handles ownership/state transitions; CSO Online Dec-2025 found API authorization logic + broken business logic the most common critical class (69 vulns / 15 apps).
fix: Per-route ownership assertions server-side; test the negative case (user A cannot read/write user B's row); don't trust capability tokens without re-validation.
source: CSA 'Vibe Coding Security Debt' 2026 + CSO Online Dec 2025

title: Native/mobile AI apps ship data-exposing misconfigs ~99% of the time — audit secrets/ATS/storage before ship
symptom: Shipped native builds embed keys, allow cleartext traffic, or leave world-readable storage.
root_cause: CovertLabs Jan-2026 scan of 198 iOS AI apps: 196 (98.9%) had security misconfigurations exposing sensitive data.
fix: Before shipping a native build (Abba/Stitchhooky/Finished): no embedded secrets, ATS on, scoped storage, no debug logging of PII.
source: CovertLabs Jan 2026 iOS AI app scan

title: zsh loop variable named path clobbers PATH so every later command is not found
symptom: After a for path in ... loop in zsh, tail, python3 and other tools failed with command not found for the rest of that shell session.
root_cause: In zsh the lowercase array path is tied to the uppercase PATH, so assigning the loop variable rewrites PATH.
fix: Never use path (or the other tied names cdpath, fpath, manpath) as a loop or scratch variable in zsh; use p or file_path.

title: Image generation was added on the Worker (env.AI FLUX-1-schnell via /api/imagegen) so photo proofs exist in no Pixelbake record
symptom: Reingeneer 'Make a photo proof' returns a base64 JPEG straight from env.AI.run with no model, seed, prompt, project or cost filed in the image studio; the house rule is that every Cloudflare-generated image is baked through the studio so it is recorded
root_cause: A new /api/imagegen endpoint calls the Workers AI binding directly instead of the studio's API, and nothing persists or reconciles the output
fix: Open: route the call through the studio API (or file each result with an upload record: for, project, model, prompt) and keep the on-Worker path only as a fallback that writes a record

title: The shipped Instagram signal claim ranked sends above saves and likes though its source named three unranked signals, and the 2026 re-check fixed only one constant
symptom: Copy said shares/sends are Instagram's most heavily weighted signal, above saves and likes, labelled FACT; the 2026 re-verify found it is surface-specific (sends win for non-followers on Reels, likes edge sends for followers, saves for feed) and that YouTube's "70% of watch time" is a 2018 figure. Only PLAT_METRIC was corrected; the exported carousel slide and the archived Study-the-greats report still carry the old sentence
root_cause: Mosseri (Jan 2025) named watch time, likes per reach and sends per reach without ranking them; creator-blog sources supplied the ranking and it was tagged FACT. The sentence is then duplicated as literal text in several files with no single source
fix: Open: move every platform-signal sentence to one claims table with a verified-on date, reference it from PLAT_METRIC, the carousel and the report, and re-verify on a schedule

title: Assets cards shipped buttons with data-act=go-ecom, an action that has no handler, so they did nothing
symptom: The 'products from Ecommerce' asset card had two buttons that did not navigate
root_cause: The click delegate only knows data-act='go' with data-to; a new action name was invented and never wired
fix: Used the existing data-act=go data-to=ecom; grep every new data-act against the delegate switch before shipping

title: Assets earnings-lens inputs sat at different heights because one label wrapped to two lines and its sibling label did not
symptom: The SDE input and the Business type select in the same two-column row did not line up; the whole valuation page looked misaligned
root_cause: The grid let each field size to its own label, so a wrapped label pushed its control down
fix: Scoped an as-earn-grid class that gives paired labels a shared min-height and bottom-aligns the controls (reset at phone width)

title: Custom business types and asset categories users type are sent to the server as telemetry events and listed by name in the admin panel
symptom: A 'What users are adding' admin panel shows each custom label a user typed, grouped with counts; the tracker's own header promises it never captures anything typed
root_cause: track('custom_added') carries the free-text label inside the action field (clamped to 60 chars) so the admin can see demand, with no allow-list, redaction or disclosure
fix: Open: send a hashed or bucketed label only, or let the user opt in to share a category name, and update the tracker contract and privacy copy to match

title: Daily and monthly figures called composed carousel slides generations
symptom: Today read '8 generations' when only 1 image had cost any Neurons; seven composed slides at 0 N were counted as generations in the day, month and lifetime totals
root_cause: The totals used COUNT(*) over every synced image instead of separating rows that cost Neurons from rows that were only filed
fix: Count generations as neurons > 0 and images as all rows, in the day, month and lifetime queries and in the page copy ('1 generation, of 8 images today'), with tests for both

title: Usage history depends on a manual sync script, and locking the dashboard broke the embeddable badge
symptom: The count is only true as of the last manual run of sync-pixelbake.mjs, nothing schedules it, and /usage.svg moved behind the PIN gate so any pasted badge now shows a 401
root_cause: Worker-to-Worker fetch on the same account fails with error 1042, so history is copied by a laptop script; the gate was applied to every route except /rates
fix: Open: add a scheduled pull from a route Pixelbake pushes to, or a cron on the machine, and decide per route which data is safe to expose (a percent-only badge token)

title: Site and pitch deck quote FLUX.2 dev at 42, 51 and 40 credits in three places while billing charged 42 and 63
symptom: The marketing run read the live site and the pitch and found three different credit figures for the same model, none matching the 42 (square) and 63 (portrait) actually debited
root_cause: Flat per-model figures were written into copy before the tile-based pricing change; the copy was not derived from the PLANS and cost functions
fix: Open: render every credit figure from the same cost function (or a generated table) and add a check that greps the site and deck for the model's credit numbers

title: Playbook cites a 53.1% early-branding figure that could not be found in any source
symptom: When the evidence was refreshed the 53.1% System1 early-branding number in sell-playbook.md could not be located anywhere; agents running /sell would repeat it in paid-ad strategy
root_cause: A figure was copied into the playbook from a summarising tool's output without opening the primary page and recording a quote and date
fix: Open: remove or replace the number, and give every playbook figure a source URL, read date and a quoted line; mark graded SIGNAL until re-opened

title: Pain ad headline in quotation marks reads as a customer review but is a composed line
symptom: The lead static and carousel slide 1 print 'It failed. It still took my credits.' in quotes as the customer's own words; the complaint exists in 2026 Trustpilot reviews of two rivals but the sentence is invented and was read through a summarising tool
root_cause: The skill tells the composer to use the customer's words in quotes, and with no verbatim review in hand a composed line was set in the same style
fix: Open: either quote a real review verbatim with its source and date, or remove the quotation marks and label the line as a paraphrase; keep a quote-provenance field in the creative spec

title: Hero headline uses the Claude Code name and the run recommended clearing it before paid use
symptom: The website hero and the developer hooks say the studio is for Claude Code; the run flagged that this is another company's product name inside an advertisement and left it unresolved
root_cause: The site copy already used the name and the creative system inherited it without a trademark or nominative-use check
fix: Open: check the vendor's brand rules, prefer a descriptive phrase (for coding agents) in paid placements, and keep the product name only as plain factual compatibility text

title: Archived Workers AI cost report says Cloudflare now offers four video models, though Cloudflare's own pricing page lists none
symptom: The cloudflare-workers-ai-image-video-costs report and its companion artifact state that Workers AI does text and image to video (LTX-2.5 Fast, Hailuo-2.3, Vidu Q3 Pro, Pruna avatar) with market rates of about $0.08 to $0.30 per second; two later fetches of the primary pricing page found no video rows, and the Joy Day audit removed the same figures as invented
root_cause: Availability and per-second prices came from search snippets and the video vendors' own sites, not Cloudflare's docs, and were labelled estimates only on the cost, not on the availability claim
fix: Open: append a correction report (the archive is append-only) stating availability is unconfirmed and no Workers AI video price is published; add a rule that any 'platform X offers Y' claim needs the platform's own page

title: Searching a hyphenated skill name with a space ('deep standard') returned zero results
symptom: After deep-standard was catalogued, typing 'deep standard' showed 0 cards while 'deep-standard' showed 1; the session dismissed it as expected because skill names have no spaces
root_cause: The client search matches the query as a literal substring of name, purpose, tag and trigger, with no normalisation of hyphens, underscores and spaces
fix: Open: normalise both the haystack and the query (lowercase, replace - and _ with space, collapse spaces) and match every query word, not the whole string

title: Harvested layer is mostly clipped assistant sentences: 73% end in an ellipsis, none carries a file, and 52% are filed to one app
symptom: Of 399 harvested rows in the live ledger 291 have titles cut mid-sentence at about 80 characters, 28 begin with a bullet dash, about 89 begin with narration such as 'One caveat', 'Here' or 'Now', every one has file null, and 206 are attributed to Hallalu CRM; rows from a disk-cleanup session were filed under Hallalu CRM and Wedding Planner
root_cause: harvest.mjs lifts sentences from assistant messages with a keyword match, truncates the title for display, takes the app from the working-directory guess, and has no step that requires a symptom, a file, or a fix. The first live pass already showed it: all 30 candidates came from one large transcript, titles carried markdown artefacts and planning narration, and the narration filter and per-session cap were bolted on afterwards
fix: Open: require a bug-shaped record (symptom plus a file or command) before filing, store the full sentence in the note and a derived short title, resolve the app from the files touched, and count harvested rows separately from curated ones in the KPIs

title: du run as the user reported ~/Pictures as 416 KB when it held 57 GB, so the home folder was measured at 36 GB instead of 89 GB
symptom: A disk-full cleanup chased a phantom 115-160 GB of 'root-owned' data through four wrong sudo commands before sudo du showed Photo Booth Library 36 GB and Photos Library 20 GB; /System showed 184 GB because the Data volume is firmlinked under it
root_cause: macOS privacy protection (TCC) makes du skip Photos and Photo Booth libraries when run from Terminal, and the scan discarded stderr so the skips were invisible; the reference note the session read was 45 days old and named a different culprit
fix: Run sudo du -hx -d2 on the home folder first, never trust a non-sudo total that does not reconcile with df, keep stderr visible, and ignore /System when summing the Data volume

title: Commands handed to the user's zsh failed twice: a [!.] glob hit history expansion and BSD du refused -s with -d while stderr went to /dev/null
symptom: The pasted 'sudo du -shx /Users/rhemajoy/* /Users/rhemajoy/.[!.]*' returned 'zsh: event not found: .]'; the replacement 'sudo du -shx -d1' returned nothing because BSD du rejects -s combined with -d and the error was discarded, costing three more round trips
root_cause: Commands were written for bash and GNU du, run in an interactive zsh on macOS, with 2>/dev/null hiding the failure
fix: For user-run commands avoid ! in globs, use find -maxdepth 1 or du -hx -d1 without -s, keep stderr, and write output to a file the agent reads rather than asking for a paste

title: Blended valuation dragged the low end down to the asset floor, showing $19,600 to $144,000 for a $96,000 to $144,000 earnings range
symptom: After three assets were logged the hero range fell to a low of $19,600 although the earnings lens said $96,000 to $144,000
root_cause: The blend took the minimum of the earnings low and the asset net value, so a small floor pulled the range down; a floor should only ever raise it
fix: Lift the low and high to the floor only when net asset value exceeds them, and test the three cases (floor below, inside and above the range, e.g. a $200,000 building lifting the range to $219,600)

title: Fixed-position notification heart sat 10 to 12px off the topbar pills and moved when the async weather chip loaded
symptom: The heart centred at y=50 against pills at y=60 once the weather chip had loaded; three successive hard-coded top offsets (18, 30, 40px) each measured differently because the topbar height changes after first paint and per page
root_cause: The cluster is position:fixed with a literal top value while the pills live in a topbar whose height depends on async content, so no constant is right for every state
fix: Open caveat: place the button inside the topbar flow (scrolls with the header) or compute its top from the topbar's measured bottom after the weather chip settles; for now it is tuned to the settled desktop layout

title: Time zone search for 'trinidad' found nothing because place aliases were missing from the IANA metadata
symptom: The new searchable picker returned no result for Trinidad although America/Port_of_Spain was in the list of 400-plus zones, the same 'too few' complaint it was meant to cure
root_cause: Search matched only the IANA city name, country code and offset text, with no alias for the country or island name
fix: Added a curated alias list (Caribbean and other islands first) so country and place names resolve; the list reached 441 searchable places

title: Completion message called Joy a complete $0 email platform while the research had found Email Sending is a beta that is transactional-only by policy
symptom: The research lane stated Cloudflare Email Sending is public beta, transactional-only by its FAQ, on shared IPs with an unpublished adaptive daily quota, so customer-composed mailbox traffic should go through SES; the final message, the Handbook and the Dossier then described person-to-person sending from any address as live and finished, without that caveat
root_cause: The blocker was recorded in the research and in the agent's own notes ('gray area') but never carried into the user-facing status, the launch guide or the cost line
fix: Open: add the policy and quota caveat to the Handbook send section and the status copy, state the real monthly cost including the Workers plan, and note the SES fallback if sending is throttled or the beta changes

title: wrangler email sending returns Unauthorized 2036 on every call even after a fresh login adds the email_sending scope, until the product is activated in the dashboard
symptom: Both 'enable' and a plain 'list' failed with code 2036 after wrangler whoami listed email_sending (write); only a one-time dashboard activation (Email, Email Sending, Get started) followed by wrangler email sending enable worked
root_cause: The error reads as a scope problem but the real gate is an account-level beta activation, so repeated re-logins do nothing
fix: On 2036 with the scope present, send the user to the dashboard activation first; then enable the zone, check DKIM, SPF and DMARC records, and add the send_email binding

title: wrangler r2 object get writes a 0-byte file because it defaults to local simulated storage unless --remote is passed
symptom: Pulling a stored .eml to check its Authentication-Results header produced an empty file and no error, so the first check appeared to find no headers
root_cause: Newer wrangler resolves r2 object commands against the local simulator by default
fix: Pass --remote when reading production objects and test the byte count before parsing

title: wrangler d1 create failed at the account's database-count cap while a rename plan assumed an unlimited number of databases
symptom: Renaming CocoMail to Joy needed a new D1 database and the create call answered 'On the Workers Free plan? Upgrade to create more'; the session had to delete its own empty database and recreate it, and had already created the new R2 bucket and worker
root_cause: The rename was planned as create-new-then-delete-old, which needs one spare database; the account was at its cap with many apps each holding a database
fix: Check wrangler d1 list against the cap before any rename, create the replacement first only when there is room, and prefer reusing a database or prefixing tables over adding one per tiny app

title: Catalogue cache stored an empty result after one transient fetch miss, so coverage read 0/0 until the isolate recycled
symptom: After a deploy the full-catalogue scan reported 0/0 and /api/checks coverage was wrong; the next requests on the same isolate kept the empty value
root_cause: catalog() cached whatever the static checklist.json fetch returned, including a failure, in a module-level variable
fix: Cache only a successful, non-empty result and retry on the next request; the test is to fail the first fetch and expect the second request to recover

title: An append-only trigger rejection reached the client as a raw HTTP 500 with the SQL error text
symptom: Re-opening a finished worklog session was correctly refused by the database trigger but the response was a 500 containing the raw error string, so agents could not tell tampering from an outage
root_cause: The write paths caught every error and returned String(e) with status 500; the worker pre-check missed it because a read replica can lag behind the finish write
fix: Map trigger aborts to a 403 with a clear message through one writeErr helper used by every write path, and keep the trigger as the authority

title: Sweep report attributed ledger additions by a 30-minute time window instead of by session, so a concurrent session's entries appeared as this sweep's finds
symptom: The 'Added to the ledger from this sweep' card listed submissions made within about 30 minutes of the sweep timestamp (first filtered by app, then widened to all apps), with provenance only as a project label
root_cause: Submissions carry no session id, so the report infers membership from time proximity; with several agents writing at once the window mixes them
fix: Open: stamp every /api/bugs submission with the active worklog session id (or require one) and have the report and timeline group additions by that id

title: Sweep commands and reports did not say whether they checked one project or the whole catalogue, so "full" was ambiguous
symptom: After a deep security scan the owner asked whether it covered only the security items for the project in hand or every project; the prompts, task labels and final report gave no scope line
root_cause: The command text described the counter (N of total) but not the scope (app, all, security, optimisers) the server was scoring against
fix: Added a scope note to /securitysweep, /fullscan and /deepscan, task labels that name the scope, and an explicit findings summary at the end of the report

title: preview_start refused a configured port held by another chat's server, and the verification then ran against that other session's process
symptom: preview_start name postplan failed with 'Port 8823 is in use by another chat's dev server'; the run carried on by fetching and rendering http://localhost:8823 directly, so the screenshots came from a server it did not start and whose working tree a second session was editing
root_cause: The launch config pins one port for every chat; the refusal text suggests autoPort or freeing the port, but a quick curl to the same port looks like a success
fix: Set autoPort in launch.json (and drop hard-coded --port flags) for shared projects, or start a private server on a free port and assert its pid before treating a 200 as proof

title: README still describes a book reader while the app ships about 40 surfaces, and the installable PWA is not an offline app
symptom: A source audit of 82 components found the README undersells the product by an order of magnitude; the same audit found the service worker is a deliberate kill switch, so the PWA installs but does not provide an offline shell, which any 'works offline' wording would misstate
root_cause: The README was written for the first feature and never regenerated; the offline behaviour was changed to avoid stale builds without updating the description
fix: Open: regenerate the README and store copy from the feature atlas, and state plainly that the app installs but needs a connection

title: Doc links from Projects and the Home starred strip dropped the document id and opened the Write list
symptom: Clicking a doc attached to a Project, or a starred doc chip on Home, landed on the Write gallery instead of that document. Notes also could not be starred at all.
root_cause: App.tsx passed onOpenDoc={() => setView({name:'writing'})} which discards the id; Library's star strip called go('writing') with no target; 'note' was missing from the Star union.
fix: Thread onOpenDoc(id) through App to Library and call setView({name:'writing', openId:id}); add 'note' to the Star union.

title: Notes format buttons (checkbox, bullet, number) appended the marker to the END of the text while typing inserted at the caret
symptom: Tapping a format button mid-note put the marker at the bottom, scrambling the note; typed markers landed in the right place.
root_cause: The button handlers did setText(text + marker) instead of reading the textarea selection.
fix: Keep a textarea ref, insert at selectionStart and restore the caret with setSelectionRange inside requestAnimationFrame.

title: localStorage-backed stores were left out of LS_STORES so a second device showed different categories and colours
symptom: Milestone categories, doc categories and the newer clubs, shared journals, reminders and classes data did not follow the account to another device.
root_cause: src/lib/sync.ts LS_STORES is an explicit allow-list; new localStorage keys (finished.milestone-cats, finished.doc-cats and others) were never added when the features shipped.
fix: Add the missing keys to LS_STORES (kind array or value). Treat 'new persisted key' as a checklist item that includes the sync allow-list.

title: To-do 'Top 3 focus' label was cosmetic: it highlighted the first three rows by index
symptom: Users could not choose their focus items; reordering or completing rows silently changed which three were called focus.
root_cause: The eyebrow rendered for idx < 3 with no focus or urgency field on TodoItem.
fix: Add TodoItem.focus (capped at 3) and urgency, plus drag reorder, and render the eyebrow from the flag.

title: Sheet formulas only understood =SUM and =AVERAGE over a range, so the Budget template could not compute left-over
symptom: Cell references and arithmetic (=B2-C2, =A1*2) showed as text or errors.
root_cause: evalFormula was a single regex for SUM/AVERAGE(range).
fix: Replace with a small recursive-descent parser (cell refs, + - * /, parentheses, SUM/AVERAGE) with a cycle guard.

title: Monthly free AI credits were never granted: my_credits() only gave a one-time +5 welcome
symptom: A free user who spent the welcome credits stayed at 0 forever although the plan copy promised a monthly allowance.
root_cause: No monthly-grant code existed anywhere in the credits RPCs.
fix: Migration 20260817_monthly_free_credits.sql adds ensure_monthly_free(), called lazily from my_credits(): reason 'monthly-free:YYYY-MM', a partial unique index on (user_id, reason) where reason like 'monthly-free:%', insert ... on conflict do nothing and bump the balance only when a row was inserted; skipped in a month that already has a welcome or renewal grant. Verified live on two users, idempotent.

title: credits.balance disagrees with sum(credit_txns.delta) for 2 of 3 users and was left undiagnosed
symptom: Balance default of 5 plus a +5 welcome ledger row, and nine ai:claude debits of -18, do not reconcile with the stored balance for two accounts.
root_cause: Not diagnosed. Candidates: the balance column default plus a ledger welcome row double counting, and debits written without updating the balance.
fix: OPEN. Add a reconciliation query (balance minus ledger sum per user) to the credits migration checks and decide which of balance or ledger is the source of truth.

title: Embedded checkout was declared missing because the repo had no edge-function source, while the deployed functions were live; a redundant duplicate was built then reverted
symptom: A whole Cloudflare Pages create-checkout function with a different request contract (plan/pack vs kind/credits) was written, wired with a fallback, then reverted.
root_cause: supabase/functions in the repo held only translate and handle-login, so absence from the repo was read as absence from production. create-checkout v8, stripe-webhook v8, billing-portal and auto-topup were deployed and healthy.
fix: List deployed functions (MCP/list_edge_functions) before concluding one is missing; mirror the four deployed functions into supabase/functions. The live webhook signing secret versus the Vault value stayed unverifiable and no real payment has exercised the webhook yet.

title: Add-to-story uploaded the raw full-resolution photo and leaked the preview object URL
symptom: 5-12 MB (possibly HEIC) photos uploaded as-is; the viewer showed a grey gradient until decode finished.
root_cause: AddStory passed the picked File straight to addStory with no downscale; URL.createObjectURL was never revoked.
fix: Add src/lib/imageScale.ts downscaleImage (a 3000x2000 5 MB PNG became 1440x960 and 18 KB JPEG), run it on Share, revoke the object URL on unmount.

title: Writing gallery crashed into the ErrorBoundary when any assignment had no content field
symptom: A to-do, routine or seeded item without content made the whole Write gallery render 'Let's get you back'.
root_cause: card() called countWords(a.content) and countWords did text.trim() on undefined.
fix: Use a.content || '' in card() and guard countWords itself; remember that the ErrorBoundary screen means a render crash, so check the console before suspecting auth.

title: Editors defaulted to the V2 design while create() wrote V1, so existing and seeded items opened in the wrong version
symptom: Docs, sheets, to-dos and the scheduler opened as V2 even when saved as V1.
root_cause: useState(item.design === 'v1' ? 'v1' : 'v2') treated a missing design as V2 while create() stamps 'v1'.
fix: Default to the stored value and fall back to v2 only for an explicit v2.

title: To-do item delete (active and archived) removed the row instantly with no confirmation
symptom: A mis-tap on the cross deleted a task permanently.
root_cause: TodoEditor renderRow del called the delete handler directly, unlike other destructive actions in the app.
fix: Route through the shared Confirm dialog before deleting.

title: To-do routine and schedule cards showed '0 words' as their subtitle
symptom: Non-document cards in the Write gallery read '0 words'.
root_cause: card() let the routine/schedule kinds fall through to the word-count branch.
fix: Add explicit subtitle branches per kind.

title: ProgressRing always drew its own percentage, colliding with the custom centre number in the Follow-ups hero
symptom: Two overlapping numbers inside the ring.
root_cause: The component had no way to suppress its built-in label.
fix: Add a showText prop (default true) and pass false where a custom overlay is used.

title: V1 doc mobile rule min-height:60vh broke A4 proportions when the page was narrowed
symptom: The paged editor sheet stopped looking like an A4 page on narrow widths.
root_cause: A viewport-height minimum overrode the page aspect ratio.
fix: Use min-height var(--pageh) on the paged rich editor, compute --pageh from the width times 1.414 and recompute on window resize.

title: Calm input has outline:0 and no focus-visible replacement
symptom: Keyboard users get no focus indicator on the calm-mode input.
root_cause: calm.css .calmh-input sets outline 0 without a :focus-visible style.
fix: OPEN. Add a visible :focus-visible ring (low severity, found by the deepscan).

title: Admin day-bucketing uses toISOString so activity lands on the wrong calendar day outside UTC
symptom: Per-day admin counts shift by a day for local evenings/mornings.
root_cause: toISOString().slice(0,10) buckets by UTC date, not the viewer's local date.
fix: OPEN (low). Bucket with local year/month/date parts or an explicit timezone.

title: Exam word decks shared one generic bank, so SAT showed 'dead' and 'cat' and MCAT/LSAT/GMAT received literary words
symptom: A SAT card read 'dead' (user-caught); MCAT and LSAT decks contained literary vocabulary; one bundled word had a stray leading space (' contingent').
root_cause: COMMON and ADVANCED banks were concatenated into every exam level to reach 1,000+ words per level, trading relevance for count.
fix: Rebuild per-test decks from researched profiles (SAT/ACT in-context academic, MCAT science, LSAT logic and legal, GMAT business, GRE the obscure tail, shared AWL core); trim the stray space. ielts/toefl keep common words because they test general English.

title: Speech features were about to be described as private or offline although the Web Speech API sends audio to the browser vendor
symptom: Draft copy implied on-device recognition.
root_cause: Chrome and Edge stream audio to vendor servers; Firefox ships it disabled. Caught by research before shipping.
fix: Word the feature honestly (needs Chrome or Edge, audio handled by the browser vendor) and keep a self-rate fallback so the feature works without a microphone.

title: Dictionary cache kept an Urban Dictionary entry under the old provider order, and one transient Wiktionary failure made real words fall through to slang
symptom: 'percent' showed a slang definition after the provider chain was corrected.
root_cause: Entries were cached without a schema/provider version, and a single failed fetch was treated as 'not found' so the chain continued to the slang provider.
fix: Add CACHE_VERSION (bumped to 2 then 3) so old entries are ignored, and retry the provider once before falling through.

title: Weekly bar chart bars computed to 147px from an inline height of 4px or 5% and spilled out of the card
symptom: Progress dashboard bars overflowed the chart card.
root_cause: Percent heights inside a flex column resolved against an unexpected container; root cause of the 147px result was not isolated.
fix: Replace the div bars with SVG bars (WeeklyBars), which size from the viewBox.

title: Adding a new level group ('Library') without a GROUP_THEME entry crashed the whole Read-with-me screen
symptom: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'emoji') and the ErrorBoundary took over.
root_cause: GROUP_THEME was indexed directly by group name in several places.
fix: Route every lookup through themeFor(g) which falls back to the Grades theme (note: a scripted global replace first made themeFor call itself recursively).

title: Changing a persisted shape from {purpose: string} to {purposes: string[]} crashed mount for returning users
symptom: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'includes') on opening Read-with-me; an empty 'My words' level also crashed on word undefined.
root_cause: Old localStorage goal objects had no purposes array and nothing migrated them.
fix: Migrate on read (purposes = [purpose]) with optional chaining, and guard the empty level (word = queue[pos] or level.words[0] or an empty word, plus an empty-state prompt).

title: New dictionary APIs worked on the dev server but production CSP connect-src blocked them, so meanings and IPA would have failed live
symptom: Found in a self-audit before release: every third-party dictionary fetch would be refused in production.
root_cause: The Vite dev server sends no CSP; public/_headers pins connect-src and did not list dictionaryapi.dev, datamuse, urbandictionary (later wordnik, merriam-webster, oxford and the translate fallback).
fix: Add each origin to connect-src and test third-party fetches under a production-CSP preview (vite preview) instead of dev.

title: 'Generate more words' on a language level generated English words
symptom: The AI top-up on French or Japanese levels returned English vocabulary.
root_cause: generateVocab's schema said 'real English word' and ignored the level locale.
fix: Pass the language/locale into generateVocab and word the schema per language.

title: First-run onboarding never opened under React StrictMode because the 'seen' flag was set before the timeout that opens it
symptom: Goal setup did not auto-open for new users and never would again (flag already set to 1).
root_cause: The effect wrote localStorage finished.rwm-onboarded then scheduled setTimeout; StrictMode's double-invoke cleanup cleared the timer after the flag was written. Any unmount inside the 500 ms window has the same effect.
fix: Write the flag inside the timeout callback, immediately before opening the modal.

title: Themeable surfaces used hardcoded colours: white quiz text on pale gradients and a fixed grey avatar silhouette
symptom: The quiz card text was almost invisible on light colourways (Encyclopedia, cream); the default no-photo avatar stayed grey on the pink theme.
root_cause: Text colour was fixed to white over a per-level gradient and NoPhoto used fill #d7dae1, instead of deriving from the active theme.
fix: Quiz: keep the pastel card and set dark text (a dark scrim was tried and rejected). Avatar: white person on var(--grad). Rule: no literal colours on themed surfaces; contrast-test the palest theme.

title: A 'tsc exit' check written as `| head; echo $?` or `${PIPESTATUS[0]}` always looks clean, and PIPESTATUS is empty under zsh
symptom: Typecheck lines printed 'tsc: 0' next to a real TS2339 error; the replacement `echo EXIT: ${PIPESTATUS[0]}` printed a blank exit code that was read as success.
root_cause: $? after a pipeline is the exit status of head; PIPESTATUS is bash-only and the Bash tool runs zsh (use ${pipestatus[1]}).
fix: Run `npx tsc --noEmit` unpiped (or set -o pipefail) and gate on its own exit code; if filtering output, capture to a file first.

title: Icon name prop is a plain string, so <Icon name="clock"> compiled but rendered nothing
symptom: A new timer icon silently showed blank because the set has no 'clock'.
root_cause: Icon accepts any string and returns null for unknown names; tsc cannot catch it.
fix: Type the prop as keyof the icon map (or log in dev). The set has 'timer'.

title: Themed word levels reached their headline counts by borrowing generic words: Travel contained 'able, about, above' and Money & finance is still padded
symptom: 'Travel & place names' showed 3,865 words but only about 560 were places or travel terms; Finance shows 2,012 with the same padding.
root_cause: BANKS mapped travel: [common, advanced] and finance: [gmatBiz, common] so every deck ran past 1,000 words.
fix: Travel: dropped the shared banks and grew real world place and metro names to 1,087. Finance is still padded (OPEN, owner chose Travel only). The honest section audit (real 'full suite' sizes per exam) is the pattern to keep.

title: A-Z dictionary of 60,000 words was filled from an unvetted word list, so learners drill non-words and obscure terms
symptom: Samples from the shipped public/dictionary.txt: aaa, aah, aahed, aardwolves, levulic, levynite, leviticus.
root_cause: Built as frequency-ranked core (about 36.5k) plus 23.5k 'fill' spread evenly across the alphabet from dwyl words_alpha (370k unfiltered). Whether isCleanWord is applied to this list is unconfirmed.
fix: OPEN. Cap the fill by a frequency floor, drop proper nouns and chemical names, and run the NSFW filter over the whole file before it ships.

title: The NSFW filter is English-only while foreign word packs come from subtitle corpora and bilingual dictionaries
symptom: French, Spanish, German, Italian, Japanese and Chinese lists (OpenSubtitles frequency lists, FreeDict, CC-CEDICT, JMdict) were bundled with no profanity check, in a product the owner wants classroom-safe.
root_cause: isCleanWord uses an English stem list; the foreign packs bypass it.
fix: OPEN. Add per-language blocklists (or filter by dictionary usage labels such as vulgar/offensive) before bundling, and spot-check each pack.

title: Third-party dictionary data was bundled with no attribution while the source header claims 'licence-safe'
symptom: CC-CEDICT (Chinese), EDICT2/JMdict (Japanese), FreeDict TEI files (fr/es/de/it), dwyl words_alpha and an OpenSubtitles frequency list went into a paid-plan app. The extracted FreeDict deu-eng and ita-eng folders ship a COPYING file (17,982 bytes for German, the size of the GPL v2 text) that was listed and never read. No attribution or licence screen appears anywhere in the session.
root_cause: Words are not copyrightable, which was the only licence analysis done; the compiled dictionaries' own licences were not checked.
fix: OPEN. Read each file's licence header (CC-CEDICT and JMdict are published under Creative Commons share-alike terms with attribution; FreeDict dictionaries are mostly GPL), add an Acknowledgements screen, keep each pack as a separate attributed data file, and rewrite the 'licence-safe' header. This is a verification task, not a finding of infringement.

title: GRE list was declared 'full Barron's breadth' because a second recall by the same model overlapped the first by 90%
symptom: Commit and chat said 3,153 GRE words was comprehensive after the hand-authored S-Z tail was mostly duplicates.
root_cause: Overlap between two recalls of one model measures recall saturation, not coverage of the real 3,500 list; no list was compared with an actual Barron's source and definitions were model-written.
fix: Say 'about 3,150 curated words' and flag unverified definitions, or diff against a licensed list.

title: Background research agents were killed repeatedly by 'computer went to sleep mid-response' and whole runs were lost
symptom: GMAT, GRE (twice), Phrases and a GRE top-up agents all failed with the same error; only one had saved partial output.
root_cause: macOS sleep during a long agent turn; agents wrote results only at the end.
fix: Run long agent batches under caffeinate -i, have agents append results to a file as they go (the GRE top-up kept 433 entries A-R that way), and resume from the partial file.

title: Help and support form writes to support_tickets but nothing reads or notifies
symptom: User messages go into an RLS table that each user can read only for themselves; there is no admin view, email or webhook, so tickets would sit unseen.
root_cause: The table and form were built; the receiving side was not.
fix: OPEN. Add an admin list or an email/webhook notification on insert, and an unread count in admin.tsx. 27 older rls_enabled_no_policy advisor lints on other tables were also not investigated.

title: Speaking a whole day produced ONE timetable block, could not be edited, and ignored the current time
symptom: Dictation and pasted lists became a single block; the transcript could not be edited afterwards; spoken times that had already passed were still placed in the past.
root_cause: The mic path called runBrainDump on mic-end with no review step, and splitItems cut only on newlines, semicolons and bullets while browser speech-to-text emits no punctuation.
fix: 'Speak your day' opens an editable review (Speak, Pause, Resume, Done, live split preview). New splitter: task starters ('I need to'), connectives (then, after that, also), soft ' and ' with a food safelist ('fish and chips'), commas, each fresh clock time or range, plus a verb-boundary splitter for 'read a book do the laundry call grandma'. Spoken number words become digits only in time contexts; intro phrases ('so today I'm hoping to') are stripped repeatedly; times already past roll to now.

title: Time-cue splitter orphaned 'pm' and split 'from 2 to 4' into two tasks (regex backtracking)
symptom: Results like [study from 2, to 4] and [dinner at 7, pm] appeared in the test table; found before shipping.
root_cause: With the optional range and am/pm groups allowed to match empty, the separator matched early and cut inside the time phrase.
fix: Add a negative lookahead for a following 'to/till/until/through N' range and for am/pm after the cue; keep 'buy 3 apples' from being treated as a time. Cover with the fixture table (run-on, no-time, ranges, bare times, food safelist, digits that are not times).

title: Long timetable titles were clipped to one line, so a long list could not be read on the tile or in the editor
symptom: Users could not see all the words in a block; wrapped second lines also touched the tile bottom.
root_cause: .tt-block-title was nowrap with ellipsis, the editor title was a one-line input, and the tile had 5px bottom padding with overflow hidden.
fix: Two-line clamp that un-clamps above neighbours on hover, an auto-growing textarea in the editor, 6/9/8px padding with line-height 1.3, double-tap (debounced against single-tap) to read the block aloud.

title: The goals 'add +' button existed but looked absent because its disabled state was a white icon on a pale background
symptom: The owner asked for a + on this week's goals that was already there.
root_cause: The disabled style removed all affordance until text was typed.
fix: Labelled gradient '+ Add' button with a dimmed (not invisible) disabled state.

title: Year 'at a glance' grid collapsed to one full-width column in a narrow container
symptom: In a 422px pane the 12 mini-months stacked instead of showing the year at a glance.
root_cause: grid-template-columns used minmax(210px, 1fr).
fix: minmax(138px, 1fr) gives 4 columns; always check dense grids at the narrowest supported width.

title: Auto-growing editor textarea relies on CSS field-sizing: content, so browsers without it show a one-row box
symptom: Where field-sizing is unsupported (Firefox and older Safari builds), the editor stays at rows=1 with a 170px max, recreating the 'cannot see all my words' complaint.
root_cause: No JS fallback for the CSS-only auto-size.
fix: OPEN. Add a scrollHeight resize fallback on input, or feature-detect with CSS.supports('field-sizing', 'content'). Support depends on browser version, so verify on the target iPhone Safari.

title: Fill patterns looked fine on localhost but a fresh profile on production showed flat blocks
symptom: The owner reported 'not seeing the design with the different fills' right after a finish pass that ticked it as verified.
root_cause: The dev profile carried persisted settings (blockStyle set to emoji) from earlier tests while the no-AI path assigned no pattern and the default fell back to solid. The verification ran against accumulated state, not defaults.
fix: Add blockFill(b, settings): explicit pattern, else a category-to-fill map when autoFill (default ON), else blockStyle, with a Settings tick. Verify features from a cleared profile and from the deployed origin.

title: Logo double-tap easter egg handles both onDoubleClick and a 320ms touch double-tap and was only tested with a desktop mouse
symptom: The report said it works for mouse and touch 'verified', but only a mouse double_click was exercised (a synthetic dblclick did not even toggle React state).
root_cause: Mobile browsers synthesise dblclick from a double-tap unless touch-action is manipulation, so both paths can fire and toggle twice (net no change); iOS double-tap zoom is also unaddressed.
fix: Pick one path (pointerup timing) or call preventDefault on the touch path and set touch-action: manipulation; test on a touch emulator or device before claiming touch support.

title: Work Log tab was empty despite weeks of agent work: it only showed personal timers while agent boards live in a separate store
symptom: The owner saw nothing in Work Log although boards and reports existed.
root_cause: worklogHTML rendered S.sessions (work_sessions start/stop timers) and never S.worklogs (the apz.mjs boards, shown only in Board view); two session stores were never joined.
fix: Work Log now lists every agent session itemised by wave (each task with its description), linked to its project, timestamped with duration and live/report links, plus a per-day work-time analysis that merges timers, agent sessions and payments, with the week graph at the top.

title: New spend markers rendered '$ GBP23' because money() takes a currency symbol and the code passed a nonexistent S.user.currency defaulting to 'GBP'
symptom: Demo render of the new work-time analysis showed a doubled symbol and ISO code.
root_cause: money(n, cur) expects the symbol; the user field is baseCurrency; a decorative icon also duplicated the symbol.
fix: Use S.user.baseCurrency || '$' and drop the icon. Caught only because the demo render was inspected.

title: Costs could not carry a renewal anchor: costCols never read b.started and createCost always stamped now()
symptom: No way to say when a subscription first charged, so next-charge dates could not be computed or shown; Costs and Stack were one table mixing paid and free tools.
root_cause: The started column existed but the API ignored it on create and update.
fix: costCols reads started, createCost uses c.started || now(), PATCH accepts it; nextCharge/renewLabel roll the date forward by cycle (shown as 'Sep 2 in 7d', due ones highlighted); a 'first charged' field stores noon to dodge timezone day shift; Costs tab shows paid items only and Stack lists all tools with a 'free' chip.

title: A payment added today did not appear at the top of the ledger and the root cause was never found
symptom: Owner logged a payment and could not find it in the list.
root_cause: UNCONFIRMED. The ledger sliced the first 12 rows in API order and there was no way to set the paid date; the session added a belt-and-braces sort rather than reproducing the original.
fix: Render sorts a copy of S.payments by at descending before slice(0, 12), the payment sheet has a date field (default today, timezone-corrected) and shows a 'today' badge. Reproduce with real data to confirm.

title: Demo mode threw 'Cannot access id before initialization' when logging a cost or payment
symptom: In ?demo, POST /costs and POST /payments raised a ReferenceError.
root_cause: The demo api() stub declared const id after the handlers that use it (temporal dead zone).
fix: Hoist const id to the top of the DEMO block. Found by exercising the new payment sort in demo.

title: Workers Assets deploys 'succeeded' for 35 minutes while static files stayed stale, and a one-off fresh result was a false positive
symptom: Eight wrangler deploys printed Success and the deployments list showed the new version at 100%, yet /app.js and /app.css kept serving old content (cf-cache-status HIT, same etag, query-string cache-busting ignored) and a brand-new public/*.txt returned 404. wrangler kept saying 'No updated asset files to upload'.
root_cause: Worker code was deploying (a never-cached /api/_v probe route proved it); only static files served by the assets pipeline were stale. A first fix (listing exact file paths in run_worker_first and serving through env.ASSETS.fetch with no-cache) showed cf-cache MISS once, then failed on the next deploy with the asset pipeline's own cache-control and no worker header. A new path returning 404 without cache headers was never fully explained.
fix: Final fix: the worker rewrites asset references in the HTML shell to /_v/<ASSET_VER>/file and serves /_v/* (a wildcard run_worker_first entry) from ASSETS with immutable caching, so each release has a new path. ASSET_VER is bumped by hand each deploy, which is a footgun. Prove deploys with a never-cached version route and by comparing the served file's sha with the local file, not with wrangler's output, and re-check after the next deploy before trusting a fix.

title: A fitting theory was recorded as a definitive diagnosis ('Aprizely auto-deploys from GitHub') and acted on, then retracted
symptom: The session summary stated the git-deploy cause as established and the session committed and pushed on that basis; there is no .github/workflows, no package.json and no CI in the repo. Twenty minutes later: 'my earlier conclusion was wrong'.
root_cause: The only evidence was that the served file differed from local; the served file was never compared with the git commit, and the prediction (a push changes production) was not tested before it was written down.
fix: Treat a root cause as a hypothesis until its prediction is tested; do not put it in summaries or memory beforehand. A separate hypothesis (wrangler logged into another Cloudflare account, because deployments list shows a different author email) was ruled out by matching whoami's account id to wrangler.json.

title: Verification navigated the owner's pinned live-board tab away and the board log was lost from view
symptom: The owner had asked for the Aprizely live board to stay open; a demo check was loaded into that same Browser-pane tab and the owner complained.
root_cause: Checks reused the fronted tab instead of creating one.
fix: Open a dedicated verification tab (tabs_create, not foreground) and never navigate a tab the owner asked to keep open; restore the board URL if it was changed.

title: Greeting h1 collapsed to a ~120px column with the sidebar open; the first fix made it worse
symptom: The dashboard greeting 'Good afternoon, Amara' wrapped to 3 lines in a ~120px column at desktop widths once the left sidebar was expanded. Separately the topbar pushed its buttons and the weather chip off the right edge.
root_cause: The greeting h1 was display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap, which reports its min-content width to the parent, so the title shrank to its narrowest word. The topbar used a flex:1 spacer plus wrap, so the buttons overflowed. The first attempt (flex-wrap/min-width/text-wrap:balance on .topbar) squeezed it further. Media queries cannot catch this because the sidebar narrows the content without changing the viewport width.
fix: Greeting became a normal block h1 with an inline badge; .topbar got flex-wrap with the title allowed to grow, buttons wrapping and max-width:100%.

title: Ava chat bubbles rendered about five blank lines (intro bubble 182px tall for two lines of text)
symptom: Every Ava message bubble had large empty gaps; the intro bubble was 182px and 7 lines tall for 2 lines of text.
root_cause: The avaMsg template literal emitted newline+indent whitespace between empty conditional blocks such as ${m.proposal?...:''}. .ava-msg .bubble2 uses white-space:pre-wrap (intentional, so AI line breaks survive), so every literal newline in the template became a visible blank line. White-space:pre-wrap combined with a multi-line template literal is the general trap.
fix: Build the inner pieces by string concatenation with no literal newlines; the bubble dropped to 54px / 2 lines. Found by measuring childNodes and scrollHeight rather than by eye.

title: Header clock and weather chip showed the device's time, not the chosen city's, and ambiguous city names mis-geocoded
symptom: Choosing London on a US device still showed Eastern time in the chip. Typing a bare city name such as Manchester or London could resolve to the wrong place.
root_cause: weatherChip rendered with new Date() in the device zone; the geocoder's IANA timezone was never stored. The picker was a native datalist that resolved by name only, and loadWeather re-geocoded by name.
fix: Store the geocoder's timezone (hit.timezone) in S.settings.weather.tz and render the chip in that zone; the picker now stores exact lat/lon/tz, and loadWeather only re-geocodes when !loc.lat || loc.name!==city().

title: Ava voice command stopped at the first pause, and the live transcript silently broke after the composer redesign
symptom: Dictating to Ava ended at the first breath, cutting long commands. After the composer redesign the live 'heard' text stopped updating with no error.
root_cause: SpeechRecognition was created with continuous=false (one-shot). The redesigned composer dropped the #avaOrb and #avaHeard ids that the mic code writes to, and the null writes failed silently.
fix: Continuous capture with accumulation and restart-on-end guarded by a stop flag; the ids were restored.

title: Marking an invoice paid (or Ava log_payment) never wrote the payment to the client's own story
symptom: A paid invoice updated invoices and the money totals, but the client page, timeline and payment history showed nothing.
root_cause: Payments lived on invoices and S.money only. mark-paid and Ava's log_payment each wrote their own subset, so there were several payment write paths and none touched lead.payments or the client timeline.
fix: One logClientPayment() writes lead.payments + a timeline money entry + S.money; mark-paid was inlined onto it so a payment is not counted twice.

title: Voice-memo player showed the wrong time (seconds passed to a milliseconds formatter)
symptom: The live time and duration in the voice-note player were off by a factor of 1000; the skip button also left the seek slider stale until the next tick.
root_cause: setTime() passed audio.currentTime and duration (seconds) to clock(ms).
fix: Multiply by 1000 before clock(); vnSkip now updates the slider immediately.

title: Brand-deal logos silently never loaded (Clearbit logo API is dead) and white favicons were invisible; verification passed anyway
symptom: Deal cards showed only the monogram fallback; the user asked for actual logos. After switching source, Glossier's white-on-transparent favicon was invisible on a white tile.
root_cause: logo.clearbit.com (free Logo API) was shut down, so every img 404'd into the fallback. The verification script only asserted the img src string existed, so it passed while the visual was broken. White favicons cannot be detected programmatically because canvas getImageData is blocked by CORS on a cross-origin image. Layering the favicon over a colour monogram was rejected by the user as unprofessional.
fix: Moved to DuckDuckGo/unavatar icon sources tested with an Image() onload probe, shown on a clean white tile with a neutral grey-letter fallback.

title: Edited the wrong modules.json: only public/modules.json is served, so the live catalog never updated
symptom: After editing the manifest and deploying, the live /modules.json still listed 3 modules and no voice-mic. It happened again after an earlier change that had touched both copies.
root_cause: The manifest exists twice (repo root and public/); only public/ is served. The root copy was edited and deployed.
fix: Copied root to public/ and redeployed. Needs a single source, a generate-on-deploy step, or a predeploy diff check.

title: Element chips and DM-template chips in Socials did nothing (click delegate only matched [data-act])
symptom: Format/element chips (data-sq-el), the Wave-8 DM template chips (data-dm-tpl) and copy buttons (data-dm-copy) never toggled or loaded. It shipped for about one wave.
root_cause: The click delegate used closest('[data-act]'); the new chips carry other attributes and have no data-act. The wave was 'verified' by presence-only checks (chip count, draft loaded).
fix: Widened the delegate to [data-act],[data-sq-el],[data-dm-tpl],[data-dm-copy]; verified click-to-state.

title: OPEN: back-dated posts are stamped at 12:00 local, polluting the best-time heatmap
symptom: After adding a 'When posted' date, every back-dated post lands in the noon bucket of the personal best-time (day x hour) heatmap. Before that, the heatmap used the time the action was logged as a proxy for post time.
root_cause: whenToTs builds new Date(y,m-1,d,12,0,0) for any non-today date, inventing an hour that the user never gave. Inferred from the shown code; not fixed in the session.
fix: Ask for a time, or exclude date-only posts from hour-of-day analysis and say so in the card.

title: OPEN: social goals mix a derived done flag written inside render() with a day-based goals system
symptom: After saving a social goal, done:0 stayed stale until the Overview tab rendered. The main Goals view filters day===today, so period-based social targets do not fit it. Editing a social goal in the generic goalModal would strip its metric linkage.
root_cause: Social goals live in shared S.goals with area:'social'+metric; done is derived but written back into g.done as a side effect of render().
fix: Not fixed: compute done on read instead of writing it in render(), and give social goals their own edit path.

title: New demo seed data never reaches existing demo sessions (user saw an 'older version' and the session blamed a stale deploy)
symptom: The user said the demo 'shows an older version'. Seed edits (Glossier to Sephora, ecommerce types/affiliate/photos) were invisible on any browser that had opened the demo before.
root_cause: decorateDemo and `if (!st.ecom) st.ecom = {...}` run only when the demo state is created; a reload hydrates the persisted localStorage copy.
fix: Version the seed (S.demoSeedV) and migrate or re-seed when it changes.

title: Work-log quick-start chips truncated long client or company names
symptom: 'SubSea Trinidad & Tobago Limited' was cut off in the bubble; the user asked to see the full name.
root_cause: .wl-chip{max-width:220px} with text-overflow:ellipsis.
fix: max-width:100% with wrapping; verified at 251px, unclipped.

title: Ecommerce currency pickers were plain selects while the rest of the app had a searchable one
symptom: The user asked for every currency list to be searchable and voice-searchable; the ecommerce product and order forms still used a dropdown of codes.
root_cause: epCur/eoCur in ecom.js used a plain <select> built from curOpts instead of curPickBtn/openCurPick from currency.js.
fix: Swapped to curPickBtn with a hidden input; added a voice mic (SpeechRecognition) to the shared picker.

title: Typing a number into the posting-rhythm field did nothing until blur (handler bound to change, not input)
symptom: The user's original complaint 'i tried changing the number manually and cant' survived the first fix: typed values only registered after clicking away.
root_cause: The handler was on the change event. A full re-render on every keystroke would drop focus, which is why it was not on input.
fix: State and save update on input and only the goal sentence repaints ([data-post-goal-line]); the full render stays on change. Verified 70, 150 and the stepper (151).

title: Real TikTok/Instagram effect names deleted because a research lane 'could not verify' them while its search tools were blocked
symptom: Time Warp Scan, Inverted, Speed ramp, Bling and Superzoom were removed from the effects suggestions. The user called it out: a critique is a claim too, and do not invent a restriction.
root_cause: The lane reported a 200/200 search budget exhausted and bot-gated engines, yet its 'unverified' list was treated as 'does not exist'. The field is free text, so keeping a stale suggestion costs nothing while removing a famous one costs usability.
fix: All five verified real (TikTok effect page, trending pages, Effect House docs, Instagram camera) and restored with a code comment recording why; lesson saved.

title: Myths note called 'post daily or you're punished' debunked when the evidence only shows it is unsupported
symptom: The in-app note said the myths were debunked or outdated. The audit showed Instagram has never denied a posting-frequency penalty; Mosseri's guidance is quality over quantity.
root_cause: Unsupported was written up as disproven.
fix: Wording softened to 'no one has shown these true'; a Posting rhythm note carries the only traceable cadence (about 2 feed posts a week, Mosseri 2021).

title: Several shipped research claims were wrong by domain transfer or overreach (portal adoption, Etsy template ban, follow-up counts, filter stats)
symptom: A counter-evidence audit caught: the '23% client-portal adoption' figure (Fraccaro et al 2017) is about healthcare patient portals, headline 52% with a 13-33% CI dropped; the Etsy 'template ban was a misreading' note was too strong (a real June 2025 Creativity Standards change removed the templated-design clause for computerised tools); the debunk of '5-7 follow-ups' overreached (the source said fifth to twelfth contact, a small 1942 sample); the '21% more views for filtered photos' stat is a Flickr study (Bakhshi et al 2015), widely miscited as Instagram.
root_cause: Statistics were carried across domains and critiques accepted without reading the primary source.
fix: Research file corrected (no credible freelancer-portal figure exists), memory corrected, filter stat reattributed.

title: --ink-3 metadata text was 2.54:1 on white (fails WCAG AA) and --ink-2 was well below the premium band
symptom: Hints, timestamps and metadata used --ink-3 (#9aa3b5) at 2.54:1; --ink-2 (#525d6f) measured 6.66:1. Dark-mode --ink-3 sits at 4.12:1.
root_cause: Text tiers were chosen by eye and never computed. This is real reading text, not decoration.
fix: --ink-2 #3d4757 (9.39:1) and --ink-3 #6b7688 (4.59:1), verified live by computing luminance in the browser. Dark-mode tertiary left slightly under 4.5:1.

title: Subscription alerts mixed currencies in one list (GBP paid vs USD home-converted)
symptom: Trial and renewal alerts read 52 pounds while the idle alert for the same subscription read $70.47.
root_cause: The idle alert used the home-currency-normalised monthlyOf(); the other alerts used the cost in the currency paid.
fix: All alerts show what the user actually pays, in their currency and billing cycle. Caught by the browser verification pass.

title: OPEN: client-portal privacy filter keys on a title regex because internal follow-up reminders carry no marker
symptom: Auto-generated reminders are stored as kind:'todo' with a title 'Follow up <name> - <label>'. The portal hides them with /^follow up/i, which also hides a legitimate meeting called 'Follow-up call' and would leak a reminder if the title format ever changed or the owner renamed one.
root_cause: schedule.js creates the events with no distinguishing field, so the client-facing filter has nothing but the title to go on. The assistant kept the regex because it errs toward privacy.
fix: Not fixed: stamp internal:true (or src:'followup') on the event when it is created and filter on that.

title: Portal editor deletes were one-click with no confirmation for nine releases (house rule: delete-confirm)
symptom: Clicking the remove control on a manual update, step, task, phase or deliverable removed it instantly (a phase went from 1 to 0, a timeline row from 8 to 7). The user had to ask again for delete confirmations.
root_cause: The destructive data-act handlers were written without confirmDel; there was no shared helper that every delete had to go through.
fix: askDel() wraps confirmDel (Keep it / Yes, delete) and re-opens the editor; every portal remove now uses it.

title: New client portal page was authored on an off-white base, violating the known pure-white design lock
symptom: portal.html shipped with --bg:#f6f5f2 and a 'warmer studio feel'. The user: 'i like white back from ffff fully not the off white'.
root_cause: Standalone pages (portal, site, kit, summary) do not inherit app.css tokens, so the lock (pure #ffffff + aurora + coral) was silently dropped on a new page.
fix: Base set to pure #ffffff; warmth comes from aurora washes behind translucent glass cards. Recorded as a standing rule.

title: Client portal status pill collided with the 'Updated just now' line (two inline-flex siblings on one row)
symptom: The ON TRACK eyebrow sat beside 'Updated just now' instead of above the headline. The user flagged it; the assistant's earlier screenshot review had called the page 'exactly the spec'.
root_cause: Both .from and .hero .eyebrow were display:inline-flex, so adjacent siblings flowed on one line.
fix: .from{display:flex;justify-content:center}; the eyebrow became a centred pill on its own row.

title: Portal completion state kept the stale 'On track' headline, misaligned the sub-line in the Editorial layout and showed a duplicate book CTA
symptom: A user screenshot of a completed project showed the eyebrow 'Complete' over the headline 'On track - here's where things stand', a sub-line indented under a left-aligned title, and 'Book the next one' plus 'Book a call' both linking to the same booking page.
root_cause: The completion verdict reused the owner's in-progress verdict; [data-plyt=editorial] left-aligned the h1 but .hero .sub kept margin:auto; the done card and contact band each rendered a booking CTA. The assistant's 'verified' completion check read the done-card text, eyebrow and CTA hrefs but not the headline.
fix: Verdict defaults to a completion message when done and none is set; hero always centred; Editorial left-aligns body copy only.

title: Deliverable Approve button shows 'Approved' even when the POST fails, and stores an approval as an open request
symptom: The assistant noted 'the approve POST will actually 404 silently, but the UI will still show the Approved feedback - that's fine'. On a link whose pid is not registered (owner signed out, never published, or a transient failure) the client sees confirmation and the owner receives nothing. When it does post, the approval arrives as kind='request' status='open' and needs 'Mark done'.
root_cause: Approve/Request-changes reuse the requests endpoint with a prefilled '✓ Approved' body and show success optimistically without checking the response.
fix: Not fixed: show success only on ok:true, hide Approve when no thread is registered, and give approvals their own kind. Never exercised end to end ('proven by transitivity').

title: Two user-reported portal bugs (Preview not working, Edit not visible) were closed with asserted, undiagnosed causes
symptom: For 'preview button not working' the report states as fact that it 'used a pop-up that browsers block'; the assistant never reproduced it and skipped the send-sheet Preview re-test. The old handler used leadOf(window.__portalLead), which is only set by the modal openers, so an unset or stale global would also make Preview silently do nothing. For 'im not seeing edit button', its own DOM probe had listed Edit among the toolbar buttons; it wrote 'I need to fix the real cause, not guess', then 'rather than fully diagnosing it I'll just make it more prominent', and the report states the cause as fact.
root_cause: Presence in the DOM was treated as visible and findable; the failure was never reproduced at the user's viewport.
fix: Edit made prominent and re-checked with getBoundingClientRect at 375px; Preview replaced by the full-page live preview and an Open anchor. Root causes remain unconfirmed.

title: Portal reports said 'verified' for paths that were never exercised
symptom: Reported verified but not run: the quiet-week tone (the test lead had other activity so it read on-track; 'logic is sound'); the stable ?p=<pid> publish-to-view round trip (publish only fires for signed-in non-demo accounts, so no D1 row was ever created); the print layout (window.print was stubbed and .no-print elements counted); the accent-colour override ('trivially correct'); 3 of 6 first-gallery themes never viewed; the Storefront portal type (only Delivery was rendered); the 'light + dark pass across all 10 templates' (the script measured one scheme, light, and the assistant had noted non-default themes do not respond to prefers-color-scheme:dark); the owner Mark-done flip and the inbox route handlers (only SQL and a mocked fetch).
root_cause: Verification checked function existence, snapshot fields or code reading rather than rendering the state or running the route.
