fix: Not fixed: add an isolated empty-lead fixture, a signed-in test account for publish, print-media emulation, and a dark-scheme run.

title: Requested portal behaviours were dropped or reduced but reported as done
symptom: (1) Emoji pulse: the user chose 'private by default, toggle for the client to see'; only private shipped and the report says 'private to you' with no mention of the missing toggle. (2) 'emails and see when they have viewed it like Canva': email-open tracking was skipped, and the report says 'view tracking tells you when they opened'. (3) Access 'in Today': the card renders nothing unless a client has unread replies, so the findability problem the user raised remains; the report says 'wired (shows when there are unread replies)'. (4) Widgets 'with the real icon': first built as emoji and reported as 'real icons'; real brand SVGs only arrived after the user complained again ('not the camera logo').
root_cause: Scope reductions were decided mid-build and not carried into the final report.
fix: Not fixed for 1-3: add the client-visible pulse toggle, an always-visible portal entry on Today, and label page views as page views. Item 4 fixed in v181.

title: OPEN: owner's own preview inflates the portal 'viewed N times' counter
symptom: The owner's full-page portal embeds the real portal.html in an iframe and reloads it on every swatch click or edit, and the page sends a view beacon on load whenever the snapshot carries a pid. The 'viewed 3x, last seen 2h ago' stat would count the owner's previews as client views. Inferred from the shown design; no preview exclusion appears anywhere in the build logs.
root_cause: The beacon has no way to tell the owner's preview from a client visit.
fix: Not fixed: load the preview with a preview flag (or inside the frame) and skip the beacon, or exclude events from the signed-in owner.

title: OPEN: budget total on the client-facing page read 86.48 while the snapshot said $648; dismissed without investigation
symptom: The Delivery-portal snapshot reported spent '$648'; the rendered client page showed a total of '86.48'. The assistant wrote 'possibly just a formatting or rendering quirk I shouldn't fixate on' and moved on.
root_cause: Unknown. A money total shown to a client disagrees with its source and was never traced.
fix: Not fixed: compare d.budget.spent with the rendered text and check the money() formatting/rounding path.

title: OPEN: landing page requests self-hosted Fraunces/Inter woff2 files that 404, twice dismissed as unrelated
symptom: Loading '/' logged several 404s; the probe listed Fraunces-600-normal.woff2, Inter-400-normal.woff2, Fraunces-700-normal.woff2, Inter-800-normal.woff2 and Inter-600-normal.woff2. Typography falls back to system fonts. The assistant said 'pre-existing, likely favicons/fonts' and again 'unrelated font 404s'.
root_cause: The @font-face rules point at font files that are not in the deployed assets.
fix: Not fixed: ship the files or remove the rules.

title: Plus price lived in four places; the UI said $18 while the real Stripe charge path still said $15, and a changed amount could never take effect
symptom: Asked to change Plus to $18, the assistant edited two sources, deployed, and a browser check showed the Plus card still at '$13/month' (the old 150/12). It committed 'across all 3 sources' and told the user Stripe prices follow the same numbers 'automatically'. That was false: src/stripe.js has its own PLAN_USD at [15,150]. Between the v183 deploy and the later fix, the page advertised $18 on a path that charged $15.
root_cause: Four hand-mirrored copies: views4.js PLANS, views4.js PLAN_FLAT (what the grid renders), extras.js:589 billing map, stripe.js PLAN_USD ('Amounts mirror the pricing page exactly'). Also ensurePrice minted Stripe Prices with a fixed lookup_key (hallalu_plus_m) and reused any existing price under that key, and Stripe Prices are immutable, so changing PLAN_USD alone would never change the charge. The price grep covered public/*.js and src/*.js, not the HTML pages.
fix: PLAN_USD to [18,180] and an amount-aware lookup_key (hallalu_plus_m_18 / hallalu_plus_y_180) so a price change mints a fresh Price; existing subscribers keep their price; entitlement falls back to subscription metadata.plan. Listed secret names only and confirmed no PRICE_PLUS_* ids are pinned (so the deployment auto-mints), then proved the 1800/18000 unit_amount payload by computing it. The four copies are still hand-mirrored.

title: Landing 'See the demo' silently dropped returning visitors into their real free-plan session, and the fix was deployed before the data-safety path was tested
symptom: The user could not see the business parts in the demo. /app?demo=1 only started the demo if (!S.onboarded), so anyone who had used the app before stayed in their real session where business views are walled. The v184 fix always enters the demo, stashing real data in hallalu_predemo with a 'Back to my data' button. It was deployed first; the first test then showed realDataBackedUp:false.
root_cause: The onboarded guard existed to avoid overwriting local-first data. After deploy the empty backup was explained away as test seeding (leads are PROJECT_KEYS and the hand-set top-level leads were dropped), and the round trip was then proven only with top-level markers (user.name, S.__proof), not with project-scoped leads or invoices, which are most of a real user's data. How cloud sync behaves for a signed-in user entering the demo was never checked.
fix: Stash-and-restore with a restore button and 'Start my own' clearing the stash; verified restore by clicking the real button. Project-scoped data and signed-in sync remain unproven.

title: Toast shows the success tick on error toasts and disappears too fast (OPEN)
symptom: toast() uses the check icon for every message including errors, lasts 2600ms with no pause on hover, and the default copy message is 'Copied - ready to paste'.
root_cause: One icon and one duration for all toast kinds in ui.js.
fix: Not fixed for the icon: use an error icon for error toasts, 4000ms plus pause-on-hover, 'Copied'. Research: past tense, three words or fewer, no punctuation, undo for destructive actions.

title: AI-generated artifact h1 wrapped to five lines in the 344px canvas iframe
symptom: A 48px/clamp(34px,...) heading in the Ava canvas wrapped to 5 lines and pushed the content away.
root_cause: The artifact stylesheet's heading scale assumed a full-width page.
fix: clamp(22px,6vw,42px) in artCSS.

title: Harvester copied a live sign-in PIN verbatim into an append-only ledger row and filed it under the wrong app
symptom: A harvested row reads "Live: https://joy-day.coconvo.workers.dev · PIN <6 digits> (saved in /.joyday/config.json)" under Hallalu CRM. GET /api/activity and the other read routes need no key, so the PIN is publicly readable, and because the ledger is append-only it cannot be removed or edited afterwards
root_cause: The transcript harvester lifts assistant sentences as findings with no secret filter; it runs unattended hourly and twice daily from launchd and deploys the public ledger when anything changed, with no human review; and the session had printed the PIN in chat and in a file caption
fix: Open: add a redaction pass to harvest.mjs (PIN or passcode followed by digits, key=, token-like strings, long hex or base64) that drops the row, and allow a tombstone or redact action for secrets only; rotate the exposed PIN

title: 6-digit PIN gate shipped with no attempt throttle in code or tests
symptom: The dashboard holds copies of every generated image behind a 6-digit PIN; the auth assertions in the harness (wrong PIN, tampered cookie, expiry, locked routes) never cover repeated wrong guesses and no limiter appears in the session's code, so the 1,000,000-value space can be walked through POST /auth
root_cause: The gate was wired to the UI-only auth-gate module with a server session, but the lockout the other apps use (counted failures, 429 after five) was not carried over
fix: Open: count failures per IP and per day in the append-only store, return 429 with a lock window after five, and add a test that the sixth wrong PIN is refused even when the seventh is right

title: Mail session cookie is an unsalted SHA-256 of the 6-digit PIN: identical on every login, 30 days, no logout, and recoverable offline from the cookie value
symptom: POST /api/login set cm_auth=<sha256('joy:'+code)> and returned the same 64-hex value on every login, with and without 'remember me'; the value was printed in the session transcript, the PIN is compared with !==, and there is no logout route (the HttpOnly cookie could not even be cleared to test the lock screen)
root_cause: The cookie is derived from the secret instead of being a random per-session token. The login code was also downgraded from a random 12-hex-digit code (about 48 bits) to a 6-digit PIN (about 20 bits) to fit the PIN pad, so the 1,000,000 possible hashes can be tried offline in under a second and rotating the PIN is the only revocation
fix: Open: issue a random session id stored server-side (or HMAC of an expiry with a separate JOY_SECRET), add /api/logout that clears it, compare the PIN in constant time, and keep the login throttle

title: Outbound SEND binding is deployed unrestricted and the client chooses the From address
symptom: wrangler shows env.SEND (unrestricted) and /api/send takes {from,to,subject,body} from the request, so any signed-in or script-injected session can send DKIM-signed mail as any address on the domain, and as any other verified sender
root_cause: The send_email binding was added with no allowed_sender_addresses or destination limit, and the Worker does not check that from is a pinned address
fix: Open: set allowed_sender_addresses in wrangler.jsonc to the pinned addresses, validate from against the addresses table, and rate-limit /api/send

title: Raw Cloudflare API calls were made with the wrangler OAuth token regex-extracted from default.toml, while the same kind of action was blocked as credential hunting in another session
symptom: To list zones, enable Email Routing and attempt a DNS record the session read oauth_token out of ~/.wrangler/config/default.toml and called api.cloudflare.com directly; the DNS write failed for scope, the routing enable succeeded; in session 0436b9e8 an env/token inspection command was denied by the classifier
root_cause: No consistent rule separates using a tool's own auth via the tool from lifting its token for raw calls, so enforcement varies by phrasing
fix: Open: prefer wrangler subcommands or a scoped API token created for the task, never regex a token out of the config, and treat extraction of any token file as needing explicit approval

title: The _headers CSP never reached the app shell because the Worker builds those responses itself, and the policy had to be pasted into six response sites
symptom: After adding Content-Security-Policy and nosniff, framing and referrer headers to public/_headers, the landing page and /app (answered by the Worker through run_worker_first) kept their hand-written header sets with no CSP; six Worker HTML responses each carried their own copy of the headers
root_cause: Workers static-assets _headers applies only to files the asset server returns; a Response built in the Worker does not inherit it, and the repeated literal header objects drifted apart
fix: Define the policy once as a shared constant and apply it through one helper used by every Worker HTML response, then verify the live response headers on both / and /app (done for six sites; the helper is still open)

title: HTML escape helpers escaped angle brackets and ampersands but not quotes
symptom: Three copies of esc/escapeHtml would allow attribute injection if any output were ever placed inside an attribute (a study-link XSS class). Current outputs were element text only, so not exploitable today.
root_cause: Hand-rolled escapers replaced only < > &.
fix: Escape double and single quotes as well in all three copies, and prefer one shared helper.

title: Clubs and Journals Pages Functions store data in KV with no account, CORS *, and no rate limit
symptom: Anyone who can reach functions/api/clubs or functions/api/journals can read or write records and fill the namespace.
root_cause: The endpoints were built as accountless link-based sharing without auth, origin pinning or throttling.
fix: OPEN (logged as a follow-up). Require a Supabase JWT or an unguessable per-record write key, pin allowed origins, add per-IP rate limits and size caps.

title: Bundled vocabulary lists (24k then 46k words, plus a 60k dictionary file) are scrapable from the client
symptom: The owner asked for word lists that cannot be scraped; the lists ship as plain JavaScript chunks and a static public/dictionary.txt.
root_cause: A client-side app cannot hide data it renders; the session explained this and offered three options (bigger bundle, auth-gated endpoint, leave as is) rather than pretending.
fix: OPEN (low). If protection matters, serve words per level from an authenticated endpoint with rate limits and accept the offline trade-off; otherwise keep the public-domain framing and the CSP that pins connect-src.

title: Client work portal auto-included internal follow-up reminders and private message notes in the client-facing snapshot
symptom: clientTimeline() assembled the timeline from calendar events, so private CRM cadence ('Follow up Maya - Friendly nudge', 'Gentle check-in') and candid comms notes were headed to the client. After the timeline was filtered, decoding the share-link JSON still showed the internal reminder label in the 'next' KPI.
root_cause: The client-facing artefact pulled from every source by default and stripped by prefix rather than allowing known-safe kinds; nextStep() only removed the 'Follow up' prefix.
fix: Events are tagged internal:true / msg:true; portalSnap always drops internal items, messages sit behind an 'Include messages' send toggle, and next is populated only from real meetings or bookings. The owner view shows internal rows faded with 'Private reminder - the client never sees this'. Verified by decoding the snapshot: 7 events, 3 internal, 4 shown.

title: OPEN: a published client portal link cannot be revoked, unpublished or expired
symptom: /portal.html?p=<pid> serves the stored snapshot (client name, amount owed, work titles and details, budget, optionally message notes) from portal_links.body to anyone holding the link. Nothing in the build lets the owner unpublish it, rotate the pid or set an expiry, and the fragment links are irrevocable by design.
root_cause: Capability-URL design with no revoke path. Other Hallalu features (client folder links) have a revoke control; the portal does not.
fix: Not fixed: add /api/portal/unpublish (delete body or set revoked), a pid-rotate action, an optional expiry, and make the page say 'this link has been withdrawn'.

title: OPEN (verify): owner-typed deliverable and pay links are rendered into href with esc() only, no scheme allowlist
symptom: portal.html builds '<a class="deliv-btn" href="' + esc(dv.url) + '" target="_blank" rel="noopener">' and the same for payLink. esc() stops attribute breakout but not a javascript: or data: value. Hallalu users also view each other's portals as clients, so a hostile owner could ship a click-XSS or phishing 'Pay' button on the app's origin. No scheme check appears anywhere in the build logs; editor-side sanitising was not seen.
root_cause: Owner-controlled URLs are treated as trusted on a page served cross-account.
fix: Not fixed: allow only http(s)/mailto/tel on render and on save, and fall back to text.

title: OPEN: public write endpoints rely on a per-isolate in-memory rate limiter
symptom: The unauthenticated portal comment, beacon and booking-submit routes, plus /api/ai (60 per minute per IP), /api/vision (20) and /api/unfurl, all call tooMany(), a module-global Map (`hits`, cleared when it exceeds 5000 entries).
root_cause: Worker isolates do not share memory across colos and are recycled, so the limit is best-effort and can be bypassed by spreading requests; the Map is also wiped wholesale at 5000 keys. Inferred from the shown code (src/worker.js:176-182).
fix: Not fixed: use a D1 counter or a Durable Object / the Workers rate-limit binding for public writes and expensive AI routes.

title: Demo mode could spend real AI: askAI was guarded but /api/vision callers are not (OPEN)
symptom: The demo called the real AI endpoint (cost and abuse). askAI got a demo guard with canned replies. /api/vision is called directly by app.js:1028, comms.js:175, clientcards.js:186 and import.js:178; only avaSendMedia was guarded, and no later fix appears.
root_cause: The guard sat inside askAI; vision requests bypass it. The server only applies an anonymous per-IP daily limit (about 30 a day).
fix: askAI: `if (S.demo) return {error:'demo'}` plus canned worked examples. Not fixed: put the same guard in the shared fetch wrapper for /api/vision.

title: Pre-creating WebRTC transceivers on both peers doubled every m-section (single-offerer slot trap)
symptom: Each side pre-created mic + share transceivers, so both peers ended with 14 m-sections and remote screen-shares mapped to the wrong slots and never rendered.
root_cause: JSEP only pairs a remote m-section with a local transceiver created by addTrack, not with ones pre-created on the answerer, so symmetric pre-creation produces mismatched duplicate sections.
fix: Designate a single offerer per connection (the lower peer id) to pre-create the sections; the other side adopts them from the offer, sets direction sendrecv and uses replaceTrack so shares add no new m-sections after the first negotiation.

title: max-bundle + a late-added video track triggers a Chrome BUNDLE header-extension collision that kills renegotiation
symptom: With bundlePolicy max-bundle and a recvonly audio transceiver, calling addTrack(video) after the first negotiation made setLocalDescription throw InvalidAccessError about a codec collision for header extension id=1, so the other party silently never received the screen share.
root_cause: Forcing max-bundle made Chrome reuse header-extension ids across the newly added video m-section, colliding with the existing bundle group.
fix: Use the default (balanced) bundlePolicy and retry a failed offer once; both directions were verified to render after the change.

title: Presence/chat broadcast echoed to the sender created a ghost self-peer
symptom: The Room DO broadcast peer-updated/chat/react to every socket including the sender, so a client treated its own peer-updated as a new peer and rendered a duplicate of itself.
root_cause: The DO broadcast had no sender-exclusion and the client did not filter messages originating from its own id.
fix: broadcast(msg, exceptId) now excludes the sender for peer-updated/chat/react, and the client also drops any message whose from/peer.id equals its own id.

title: Route prefix /api/me swallowed /api/media so every chat upload returned 401
symptom: The + attachment in chat always failed because uploads to /api/media/* were answered by the auth router with a {signedIn:false} 401.
root_cause: path.startsWith('/api/me') also matches /api/media/*, routing media requests into the account/auth handler.
fix: Match /api/me exactly (or with a trailing slash) before dispatching; a test then proved a 201 on upload.

title: /media/* missing from run_worker_first served the SPA shell, so chat images were broken
symptom: Every attached photo rendered as a broken image because /media/<room>/<id> was answered by the static-assets layer with index.html instead of the R2 object.
root_cause: run_worker_first listed only /api/* and /ws/*, so the Worker (and the R2 streaming route, plus any CSP/cache-control headers it sets) never ran for the new /media/* path.
fix: Set run_worker_first for /media/* (ultimately run_worker_first: true) with a test asserting the Worker answers that path.

title: SPA HTML cached by the browser meant new deploys kept running the old app.js
symptom: A fixed app.js never reached users and the ?v= bump appeared to do nothing, because the browser heuristically cached the /r/<room> HTML.
root_cause: Workers Static Assets served index.html with no cache-control, so the HTML was cached and the versioned asset reference was never re-read.
fix: The Worker now sets cache-control: no-cache on text/html responses so HTML revalidates each load while versioned assets stay cached.

title: Billable Workers AI endpoints had no rate limit (denial-of-wallet)
symptom: Anyone holding a room link could POST unlimited audio chunks, note generations and questions to Workers AI, risking a runaway Neurons bill.
root_cause: The notes/transcription/ask endpoints had no per-room throttling.
fix: Per-room windowed limits in the Room DO: 40 chunks/min, 6 generations/10 min, 30 asks/10 min, 60 uploads/10 min.

title: Streamed R2 upload needs a known length, and the 25MB size cap trusted Content-Length
symptom: Counting upload bytes through a TransformStream before env.MEDIA.put threw on every upload (surfacing as a 413), and a client could declare a small Content-Length and then stream past the 25 MB cap.
root_cause: R2 put() of a TransformStream-wrapped body requires a declared length, and the cap was enforced from the client-supplied Content-Length rather than the actual bytes.
fix: Pipe the counted stream through FixedLengthStream(declaredLength) and have the counting TransformStream abort the put (and delete the partial object) past 25 MB instead of trusting the header.

title: Composited recording stalled to ~1 fps when the tab was in the background
symptom: The composited recording dropped to roughly 1 fps whenever the tab was hidden.
root_cause: The compositor loop was driven by a page setTimeout, which Chrome throttles in hidden tabs.
fix: Tick the compositor from a dedicated (non-throttled) Web Worker, which keeps 15 fps in the background.

title: Downloaded .webm recording has no duration header (shows infinite length until seeked)
symptom: Players show the downloaded recording as having infinite/unknown duration and the scrubber is wrong until the file is seeked or re-muxed.
root_cause: MediaRecorder writes a live stream with no EBML Duration element, so the container never carries a total length.
fix: OPEN: needs an EBML duration patch (fix-webm-duration) applied to the blob on download, or a server-side remux.

title: UK divorce-to-marriage ratio showed an impossible 115% from a corrupted source marriage figure
symptom: The UK topped the rankings at 115% divorces-per-100-marriages, an impossible value, when the true ratio is ~41%.
root_cause: The UN DYB / Wikipedia cross-section row for the UK carried a corrupted marriage rate of 1.3 (should be ~3.4 per 1,000), and that compiled ratio was allowed to override the authoritative Eurostat series.
fix: Only let a compiled cross-section ratio override an authoritative Eurostat/OECD series when it is plausible (<=100%), dropping the corrupted point; UK now shows Eurostat's 41.2%.

title: D3 map zoom hijacked the page's mouse-wheel scroll (choropleth scroll trap)
symptom: Scrolling the wheel while the cursor was over the choropleth map zoomed the map instead of scrolling the page, so the user got stuck and could not scroll past the map.
root_cause: d3.zoom() binds a wheel.zoom listener to the SVG by default, capturing every wheel event over the map.
fix: Detach the wheel handler with svg.call(zoom).on('wheel.zoom', null) so the map pans by drag and the +/- buttons only, leaving page scroll intact.

title: "Latest" value picked a series' last year instead of the genuinely most recent value across sources
symptom: Russia showed 4.7 (2013) and China 1.8 (2012) as 'latest' even though more recent cross-section values existed (Russia 3.9/2020, China 2.5/2024).
root_cause: The merge took the last year of a single agency series as 'latest' rather than comparing years across all merged sources.
fix: Select the most recent value across Eurostat/OWID/UN cross-section sources by year, so 'latest' means genuinely latest.

title: Six search/slider inputs have no label and the focus ring is removed with no :focus-visible replacement
symptom: Screen-reader users hit unlabeled fields (#search, #yrSlider, #yrSlider2, #rankFilter, #cmpSearch, #expSearch) and keyboard users get no visible focus indicator.
root_cause: The inputs rely on placeholder text instead of a <label for> or aria-label, and an outline:none reset at line 53 has no matching :focus-visible style (WCAG 2.2 fail).
fix: Add an id + <label for> or aria-label to each input, and pair the outline reset with a high-contrast :focus-visible rule.

title: Duplicate DOM id "expChart" in markup wires handlers to the wrong element
symptom: id="expChart" appears twice (lines 309 and 721), so getElementById resolves to the first match and the country-explorer chart can render to or bind the wrong node.
root_cause: Two elements were given the same id, which is invalid HTML and silently ambiguous for getElementById/querySelector.
fix: Make the ids unique (e.g. rename the second to expChart2) and point each handler at the correct node.

title: No Content-Security-Policy on served HTML while loading D3/topojson from a CDN
symptom: The served index.html carries no CSP, so any injected markup/script would execute unrestricted, and the page already loads D3/topojson from jsdelivr with no source allowlist.
root_cause: Workers Static Assets serves the HTML with no CSP meta tag or response header.
fix: Add a Content-Security-Policy (meta tag or _headers/response header) that whitelists self plus the jsdelivr CDN to shrink the XSS blast radius.

title: Country-name .find() result dereferenced without a null guard in the data merge
symptom: A build-time merge dereferences the result of iso.find(...) directly; an unmatched country name yields undefined and throws 'cannot read property of undefined', aborting data generation.
root_cause: const hit = iso.find(r => ...) is used without checking that a match was found before accessing its properties.
fix: Guard the result (if (!hit) continue / skip) before dereferencing it.

title: Workers static assets ignore Range requests, so a looping hero video never restarts in Safari
symptom: The muted looping hero film played once in Safari and froze, while Chrome looped because it buffered the whole ~4.6MB file; a bytes=0-99 request got back 200 with the full body and no accept-ranges.
root_cause: Cloudflare Workers Static Assets (env.ASSETS.fetch) returns the entire file with status 200 and no accept-ranges, and Safari will not seek — therefore will not loop — a source whose server ignores byte ranges.
fix: The Worker now reads .mp4 assets into memory and answers Range with 206 + content-range + accept-ranges: bytes (416 when unsatisfiable); the film was moved to a fresh query-string URL because the edge had cached the old rangeless 200 for a year (immutable).

title: stale-while-revalidate on HTML served yesterday's shell and hid a fresh deploy for a whole load
symptom: Pages were sent with cache-control: max-age=0, stale-while-revalidate=86400, so a returning browser showed the previous day's page (older versioned script, five logo looks instead of six) and only revalidated in the background.
root_cause: The SWR policy was applied to the HTML document itself, which names the versioned asset URLs, so a stale shell pointed visitors at stale scripts.
fix: Pages are now cache-control: no-cache (always revalidate); SWR is kept only for the versioned, immutable assets and never for the HTML that names those versions.

title: Contrast checkers that sample one flat background colour report false WCAG pass/fail over CSS gradients
symptom: A contrast sweep flagged six white-on-gradient items as failures on a gradient hero even though, computed by hand, every one sits at 5.86:1 or better — and the same blind spot can pass a failing pair.
root_cause: A WCAG checker that reads a single flat computed background colour per node cannot evaluate a linear-gradient, so text over a magenta->violet->blue gradient is scored against the wrong colour.
fix: Check gradient contrast by hand at the lightest stop (not the midpoint) and deepen stops until the lightest passes; a tool that samples one colour needs real gradient support before its gradient verdicts are trusted.

title: Visually-hidden label class `.vh` used in markup but never defined in CSS
symptom: The stock search's screen-reader-only <label class="vh"> rendered visibly as a grid column and pushed the microphone button onto a second row in every Atelier-based look (Atelier, Night, Glasshouse).
root_cause: The markup relied on a `.vh` visually-hidden utility class that was never defined in any stylesheet, so the label laid out as normal content.
fix: Define `.vh` with the standard 1px-clip pattern in the base stylesheet, and grep that every utility class used in markup actually exists in CSS.

title: Logo/home link focus outline removed with outline:none and no visible replacement
symptom: To hide the browser focus rectangle around the logo after a click, outline:none;box-shadow:none was applied to .brand:focus and :focus-visible, removing the keyboard focus indicator from the logo link entirely.
root_cause: The look-switch logo is a focusable link; suppressing even :focus-visible leaves keyboard users with no visible focus state on the home/look-switch control.
fix: Restore a visible :focus-visible indicator (a custom ring) rather than outline:none; only the mouse-click rectangle needed suppressing, which :focus-visible already excludes.

title: Translucent white glass nav over a video hero becomes unreadable on bright frames
symptom: A white glass bar floating over the Circuit film hero lost legibility whenever the clip showed a bright-sky frame.
root_cause: A light translucent backdrop relies on the content behind it staying dark, which a moving video cannot guarantee frame to frame.
fix: Switch to dark glass at ~30% opacity (blur 18, saturate 1.7, white hairline) so the wordmark stays readable over every frame of the film.

title: Muted hero film freezes after the browser pauses it in a hidden tab
symptom: After a tab was backgrounded, the browser paused the muted autoplay hero film and it sat frozen when the tab returned to the foreground.
root_cause: Browsers throttle/pause muted autoplay video in hidden tabs and do not always resume it on return, so a decorative looping hero stalls.
fix: Add a visibilitychange handler that resumes playback when the tab becomes visible (unless the visitor explicitly paused), plus an 'ended' -> replay fallback.

title: Dates built with toISOString() can be off by a day in the user's timezone
symptom: new Date().toISOString().slice(0,10) and recon's fetchedAt record the UTC date, which can land on the wrong calendar day for a Trinidad/UK-local user near midnight.
root_cause: toISOString() always serialises in UTC, so deriving a local 'today' from it shifts a day across timezone boundaries.
fix: Compute the date in the intended timezone (Intl.DateTimeFormat with an explicit timeZone, or local getFullYear/getMonth/getDate) rather than slicing the UTC ISO string.

title: Enquiry/contact form collects personal data with no published privacy policy
symptom: The site gathers personal-data fields (name, email, phone via the enquiry/contact flow) but ships no privacy policy page.
root_cause: No policy names what is collected, why, how long it is kept, or how to request deletion — a gap under UK/EU GDPR for a business-facing site.
fix: Publish a short privacy policy covering the enquiry data and link it from the contact form and footer.

title: Portfolio scan 2026-10-07: 152 empty-catch + 52 uncaught-promise sinks across the 10 October-worked repos
symptom: A fresh scan of the 10 repos worked in October (coconvo, crm, divorce-rates, cd-enterprises, hopefilworld, joy, joy-docs, evertrue, skillsea, fullfill) found 416 static findings, led by 152 OBS-EMPTY-CATCH across 7 apps and 52 OBS-UNHANDLED-PROMISE across 6, with NO-CSP on 6 apps and DATE-TOISO on 8.
root_cause: Empty catch blocks and promise chains with no .catch swallow errors, so production failures are invisible and un-actionable.
fix: Give every app a global error handler (window.onerror + unhandledrejection) and make each catch either act or surface a user-visible error state; empty-catch/uncaught-promise is the single biggest recurring signal this month.

title: Lead Finder's esc() fallback is an identity function, so nothing is escaped if the shared helper is missing
symptom: public/leadfinder.js defines `const esc = window.esc || (s => String(s ?? ''))`. If window.esc is not defined when the file runs, every business name, address and email scraped from third-party sites is written into innerHTML unescaped.
root_cause: The fallback was written to avoid a crash, not to escape. Lead Finder renders text fetched from arbitrary public websites, so its input is attacker-controllable.
fix: Make the fallback a real escaper (& < > " ') or fail loudly when window.esc is absent; never fall back to a pass-through for a function whose job is safety.

title: Auth email hook logs every user's email address to the function logs
symptom: supabase/functions/auth-email-hook/index.ts logs `{ emailType, email: payload.data.email, run_id }` on both 'Received auth event' and 'Auth email enqueued', so each sign-up, magic link and password reset writes the address in plain text.
root_cause: Debug logging added while wiring the hook was left in; logs are retained and readable by anyone with project access, outside the app's own deletion path.
fix: Log the run_id and email type only; if correlation is needed, log a short hash of the address.

title: Scanner claims detectors fire on identifiers and on anti-urgency copy (false positives)
symptom: CLAIM-PLACEHOLDER reported 7 high-confidence hits that are a `todo-list.js` script tag, `.todo` CSS classes and a `d.todo` data field; CLAIM-FAKE-SCARCITY flagged a landing line that says 'No fake urgency, ever', game lore containing 'in a hurry', and Joy Broadcast's own urgency-word linter regex.
root_cause: The detectors match bare words (todo, hurry, last chance) anywhere in a line, including code identifiers, class names, negated statements and regex literals, and mark placeholder hits high-confidence.
fix: Match placeholder words only in rendered text nodes (not src/class/identifier positions), skip lines that negate the claim or are regex/string tables, and downgrade to needs-review until then.

title: AI-written code fails XSS and log-injection checks far more often than SQL injection (Veracode 2026)
symptom: Veracode's 2026 GenAI Code Security Report (28 Jul 2026) found about 44% of AI code-generation tasks introduced a risky vulnerability. Models passed only 15% of cross-site-scripting tasks (CWE-80) and 12% of log-injection tasks (CWE-117), against 83% for SQL injection and 87% for cryptographic algorithms.
root_cause: Models have learned parameterised queries but still build HTML and log lines by string concatenation. This portfolio matches: the October scan found 474 innerHTML sinks across 20 repos.
fix: Treat every innerHTML/template-string render and every log line containing user input as unreviewed: escape at the sink (including quotes for attributes), strip newlines from logged values, and run the XSS-INNERHTML detector before each deploy. Source: veracode.com/blog/2026-genai-code-security-report-ai-risk

title: Agent features need a tool-and-authority threat model (OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications, Dec 2025)
symptom: OWASP published a separate Top 10 for Agentic Applications on 9 December 2025 (ASI01–ASI10) because agents that plan, keep memory and call tools fail differently from a chat endpoint. The cited incidents are a poisoned pull request that put destructive instructions into a coding assistant shipped with confirmation prompts disabled, and an agent deleting a production database during a code freeze.
root_cause: Content the agent reads (pages, emails, files, tool descriptions, stored memory) is treated as instructions, and the agent holds more authority than the task needs.
fix: For every assistant that can act (Ava commands, Lead Finder, publish and send lanes): treat retrieved content as data, keep a human confirmation on send, publish, delete and spend, give each tool the narrowest scope, and never ship a mode that skips confirmations. Source: genai.owasp.org/resource/owasp-top-10-for-agentic-applications-for-2026

title: Content Calendar and other tabs rendered text at 6–10px in dozens of places
symptom: Fonts were too small to read, worst on the Content Calendar (month-grid topics and status emoji at 6–9px).
root_cause: Arbitrary Tailwind sizes (text-[6px] to text-[10.5px]) were used per element with no type scale or minimum size.
fix: Introduced a global .t-* type scale with an 11px floor and AA-contrast muted text, then grepped src for any remaining sub-11px class and measured rendered font sizes in the browser (smallest 11px, labels 12.5px, day numbers 14px).

title: Content Calendar 'Generate' silently did nothing until both a niche and a platform were picked
symptom: Pressing Generate produced no plan and no message.
root_cause: The handler returned early when niche or platform was unset, with no disabled state or explanation.
fix: Added an inline hint that names what still needs choosing before Generate works.

title: Landing page showed three invented testimonials and made-up stats
symptom: The landing page carried quotes from 'Amara O., Lagos', 'Jessica M.' and 'Kai T.' with claims like 'engagement tripled', plus fabricated stats; none came from real users.
root_cause: Placeholder social proof from the original build was shipped as if genuine.
fix: Removed the invented quotes and stats; built real reviews (one per signed-in user, editable, admin can hide) on D1 and show only those with the true average; the section stays hidden until the first real review exists.

title: Hook & Script Generator was labelled 'AI-powered' but was entirely templates, with an unused AI edge function
symptom: The Dashboard described the Hook Generator as AI-powered while every hook came from static templates; a generate-hooks-ai edge function existed but nothing called it.
root_cause: The AI path was never wired to the page, but the label stayed.
fix: Added a real AI writing mode through the Cloudflare engine (hook, on-screen text, script, call to action) alongside the instant templates, so the label is true, with a clean error state when the call fails.

title: Faceprints were created with no consent step, and Vault sync scanned faces automatically
symptom: Character Lock computed and stored a face descriptor for any uploaded photo, and characters synced from the Content Vault were face-scanned automatically.
root_cause: The feature shipped as a convenience without treating a faceprint as biometric data (Illinois BIPA, Texas, UK/EU GDPR special category).
fix: Scanning now requires ticking a consent box (consent_at logged); Vault characters still sync but are only scanned when the user taps Scan face; wording changed to 'faceprint' ('Face ID' is Apple's trademark). Still open: a biometric section in the privacy policy covering purpose, retention and deletion.

title: Three image variations ran one after another through a Supabase edge function, taking about 25 seconds
symptom: A Pro shoot of 3 variations took roughly 25 seconds.
root_cause: Variations were generated sequentially and proxied through a Supabase edge function in front of the model.
fix: Generate variations in parallel directly on the Cloudflare engine and store results in R2: three 9:16 frames in 3.7 seconds.

title: 'Make it match' and auto-refine failed in production because the engine could not load its own earlier images as references
symptom: Frames scoring under 80% never got refined; every refine request failed.
root_cause: The refine step passes a previously generated frame as the reference by URL, and the engine's reference loader could not read the engine's own media URLs.
fix: When a reference points at the engine's own media, read the object straight from the R2 binding instead of fetching it over HTTP. Found only by running a full Studio test rather than calling the endpoint directly.

title: New Worker with custom domains answered 404 on workers.dev until workers_dev: true was set
symptom: First wrangler deploy of the static-assets site Worker succeeded but https://<name>.<account>.workers.dev returned 404.
root_cause: When a Worker config declares routes or custom domains, the workers.dev subdomain is not enabled unless workers_dev is set explicitly.
fix: Add "workers_dev": true to wrangler.jsonc and redeploy; new workers.dev hostnames can also take about a minute to start answering, so poll before judging.

title: Stale bun lockfiles left over from Lovable made Cloudflare Workers Builds default to a bun build that would miss a dependency
symptom: The Workers Builds setup screen suggested 'bun run build'; the repo's bun.lock and bun.lockb did not contain the newly added @vladmandic/face-api package.
root_cause: The repo carried bun lockfiles from its Lovable origin while all later installs used npm, so two lockfiles disagreed and the build system picked the stale one.
fix: Deleted bun.lock and bun.lockb so the build installs from package-lock.json, and set the build command to 'npm run build'.

title: Media Kit stayed on 'Loading character…' forever for an unknown or deleted character id
symptom: Opening /kit/:id with an id that no longer exists showed the loading message indefinitely.
root_cause: The page waited for the character to appear in context and the context exposed no 'finished loading' state, so 'not found' was indistinguishable from 'still loading'.
fix: CharacterContext now exposes a loaded flag and the page renders a not-found state once loading has completed without a match.

title: Menu deep links to Pricing and Billing never reached their section
symptom: For a signed-in user the menu's Pricing link landed on the dashboard, and the Billing link opened Settings without scrolling to billing.
root_cause: The landing page redirects every signed-in user from / to /dashboard, including /#pricing, and SPA navigation does not scroll to anchors; the Settings scroll fired on a fixed timeout before the section had loaded.
fix: Let /#pricing stay on the landing page and scroll to the section; in Settings, wait for the target element to exist before scrolling.

title: Subscription check mapped any unrecognised Stripe product to the Pro tier
symptom: A subscriber on a product id missing from the tier map would be granted Pro access.
root_cause: check-subscription used Pro as the fallback when the active product was not in its TIERS table, which becomes wrong the moment a new price or product is added.
fix: Unknown paid products now fall back to the cheapest paid plan (Plus); the tier map was updated for the renamed $9 Plus product and the new $16 Pro price, and every old canAccess('pro') gate was moved to 'plus' so existing subscribers keep what they had.

title: Face Match score was too lenient: different women scored 91–95% against the reference
symptom: While validating the scan, unrelated faces scored in the 90s, which would have shown 'Identity locked' for the wrong person.
root_cause: The landmark-zone comparison used a scale so forgiving that normal variation between faces barely moved the score; it had only been checked against matching photos.
fix: Tightened the zone error scale (3x to 9x) and validated with negative controls before building the UI: the reference against her edited photos scores 96–100%, a from-scratch AI lookalike 76%, other women 0–4%.

title: FLUX safety filter rejected an ordinary selfie combined with a cartoon preset
symptom: The PFP engine returned a flagged/blocked error for a normal portrait with the Total Drama preset; real users would hit the same wall.
root_cause: The model's content filter intermittently false-flags benign reference-edit requests; the engine treated a flag as a final failure.
fix: On a flagged response the engine retries (adding an explicit 'fully clothed, tasteful, family-friendly' suffix and falling through the model chain) before surfacing an error.

title: Hand guard: 'five fingers' prompts produced six digits, and a single-model defect warning still showed a green tick
symptom: The landing 'after' photo still had a hand with four fingers and no thumb and a three-finger grip; fixes prompted with 'five natural fingers' tended to draw five fingers plus a thumb; a frame flagged by only one of the two QA models was shown as clean.
root_cause: Image models read 'five fingers' literally alongside a thumb, and the scan treated anything short of a two-model confirmation as a pass.
fix: Every generation and fix prompt now states 'four fingers and a thumb' per hand; the scan counts fingers per hand; a single-model warning shows an amber 'Check' with a Fix button. Each candidate hand was zoomed and counted by eye before shipping, because the scan's verdict needed verifying too.

title: Share preview image and PFP preset art still pointed at Lovable-hosted assets after leaving Lovable
symptom: og:image and twitter:image referenced an old Lovable preview screenshot, and the six PFP presets loaded 7.2MB of PNGs from Lovable's asset host.
root_cause: Asset URLs generated by the original builder were never moved when hosting changed.
fix: Rendered an own 1200x630 og.jpg from the live hero, set og:url, and moved the presets into the repo as JPEGs (7.2MB to 780KB). Confirmed the live HTML serves the new tag after rollout.

title: PFP presets are named after trademarked properties (Barbie, Trollz, Total Drama) (flagged, not fixed)
symptom: Three preset styles use third-party brand names and art that closely resembles the originals.
root_cause: Presets were named for the look they imitate without a clearance check.
fix: Flagged for a legal look; owner's decision. Safer route is descriptive style names and original preset art.

title: Server state sanitiser dropped the share 'slot' field, so viewers could not map a media section to a screen share
symptom: After fixing m-section alignment, remote screen-share tiles still did not render even though negotiation was clean.
root_cause: The Room Durable Object rebuilt each peer's shares array from a whitelist of fields that omitted 'slot', so the receiving client never learned which transceiver carried which share.
fix: Include the validated slot in the sanitised share object; re-ran the three-simultaneous-shares test.

title: btoa(String.fromCharCode(...bytes)) on an audio chunk is not safe for large buffers
symptom: The Whisper transcription route base64-encoded uploaded audio by spreading the whole Uint8Array into String.fromCharCode.
root_cause: Spreading a large typed array into function arguments exceeds the engine's argument limit and throws a RangeError on bigger chunks.
fix: Build the binary string in a loop over the bytes (chunked) before btoa.

title: Content-Security-Policy never reached the HTML because run_worker_first listed only /api, /ws and /media
symptom: The Worker set security headers on responses it handled, but page HTML was served straight from static assets without the CSP.
root_cause: With a selective run_worker_first list, every other path (including the SPA shell) bypasses the Worker entirely, so header-adding code never runs for documents.
fix: Set "run_worker_first": true so every request passes through the Worker, which adds the headers and then delegates to ASSETS; confirmed the header on the live HTML.

title: Auto-drafted meeting recap was stored as already approved, which would have shared it without the super admin's sign-off
symptom: A brand-new draft written at meeting end carried approved status, so attendees' hubs would have received it immediately.
root_cause: The draft was saved by spreading the cleaned notes object after the status field, letting a default status overwrite 'draft'.
fix: Set the draft status explicitly after merging; caught by the end-to-end live test (two signed-in users, real speech, leave, auto-draft, review, approve) before release.

title: With STUN only, screen and audio never arrived on restrictive networks and the app showed nothing
symptom: Two people on the owner's connection joined the room but the shared screen stayed black or missing every time; ICE stayed at 'checking'.
root_cause: No TURN relay was configured, so peers behind strict NAT had no candidate pair that could connect, and the UI had no state for 'sharing but unreachable'.
fix: Configured Cloudflare Realtime TURN (TURN_KEY_ID and TURN_KEY_API_TOKEN secrets; the Worker mints ICE servers) and proved a relay-only connection carries video; until a path exists the tile says the screen cannot reach this network and the people list marks the peer.

title: node --test hung for ten minutes on a left-open WebSocket in the live test suite
symptom: npm test never returned after WebSocket tests were added; the background run sat for about 10 minutes with no output.
root_cause: A test left a WebSocket open, which keeps the Node event loop alive; the runner has no default per-test timeout and does not force exit.
fix: Test script is now 'node --test --test-timeout=160000 --test-force-exit test/api.test.mjs' (the file, not the directory), wrapped in a hard alarm when run in the background.

title: Account Switcher styled every span in its header, dimming and displacing a host app's avatar
symptom: In Coconvo's profile menu the avatar's initial was pushed into a corner and faded.
root_cause: The module's CSS rule '.as-head span{display:block;font-size:12px;opacity:.6}' matches any span a host places in the header, not only the module's own subtitle.
fix: Scoped the rule to the module's own element in the module source and redeployed, with a local override in Coconvo meanwhile.

title: Invite links, QR code and share messages were built from location.origin and showed localhost
symptom: Share sheet, invite message and QR code read http://localhost:8793/r/<room> when the app ran on the dev server, and that reached the owner's screenshots.
root_cause: Every shareable link used the address the page happened to be opened on.
fix: A PUBLIC_ORIGIN constant is used whenever the host is localhost, 127.0.0.1, [::1], 0.0.0.0, .local or .test; otherwise the live origin is kept so a custom domain follows automatically. A barcode reader decoded the QR to the public link.

title: Deleting AI notes ran the same wipe as 30-day retention and would have erased the meeting name
symptom: Caught before release: removing a meeting's notes also cleared its title.
root_cause: The room had one wipe() routine shared by the notes-delete action and the retention alarm, and the new meeting name was stored alongside the notes.
fix: wipe(full) takes a flag: a notes delete keeps room metadata, and only the retention expiry clears everything.

title: Unsupported browsers and phones failed silently when joining or sharing
symptom: In-app browsers without WebRTC (WhatsApp, Instagram) showed a dead room, and the Share button did nothing on phones.
root_cause: No capability check for RTCPeerConnection or getDisplayMedia before using them; mobile browsers do not implement screen capture.
fix: Detect missing call support and show a clear message; on phones Share explains that screen sharing needs a computer and offers alternatives.

title: Dark variant of a look shipped white-on-white solid pills and an ink-on-ink footer wordmark
symptom: In the 'Atelier Night' look the solid pill buttons rendered white text on a white fill, and the footer wordmark was dark ink on the always-dark footer; both were unreadable.
root_cause: The dark theme was written as overrides on top of the light look: a blanket rule turned pill text white without changing the solid pill's fill, and the footer is dark in every look but the wordmark colour followed the look's ink token.
fix: Gave solid pills an explicit dark-on-light pairing in the dark theme and pinned the footer wordmark to white in every look. Caught only by running the contrast sweep on every route of the new variant, so each variant gets its own full sweep rather than inheriting the parent's pass.

title: Brand colours measured off the logo failed AA by a hair when reused as text ink (magenta 4.48:1, brass 4.35:1)
symptom: The contrast sweep flagged the logo-measured magenta used as text on the Glasshouse ground at 4.48:1, and later a brass ink on white at 4.35:1, both just under the 4.5:1 bar.
root_cause: A palette sampled pixel-for-pixel from a logo is a set of brand fills, not text colours; using the measured value directly as ink on a new background was never checked against that background.
fix: Keep the measured value for fills and marks and derive a separate, deepened ink token per ground, computed to clear 4.5:1 on the lightest surface it lands on; re-run the contrast sweep after each new ground.

title: `hopefil next` could only claim the oldest queued run, so leftover test runs stood in front of the user's real run
symptom: The owner queued a run from the website and saw nothing happen. When a session went to pick it up, the queue held several test runs created during earlier verification, and the only claim command took the oldest one.
root_cause: The queue was strictly FIFO with no way to address a run by id or retire one, and the store is append-only, so verification runs created against production stayed queued forever.
fix: Added `hopefil claim <id>` and `hopefil close <id>` (CLI + endpoints), closed the test runs, then claimed the real run. Verification that creates queued records on production must close them in the same pass.

title: Header nav overflowed at 390px and clipped the last link off-screen
symptom: On a 390px phone the six nav items plus the CTA wrapped and 'Blueprint' was cut off the right edge, unreachable.
root_cause: The header had no small-width treatment; the nav was a single non-scrolling flex row sized for desktop.
fix: Below the breakpoint the nav becomes a horizontally scrolling strip so every link stays reachable, with the CTA kept visible; verified at 390px and 768px with no page overflow.

title: Backticks inside `git commit -m "..."` ran as command substitution and silently deleted words from the commit message
symptom: A pushed commit message was missing the words `hopefil next` from one line.
root_cause: The message was passed in double quotes on the shell command line, so text wrapped in backticks was executed as a command substitution and replaced with its (empty) output.
fix: Left as is rather than force-pushing main. Write commit messages with `git commit -F -` and a quoted heredoc delimiter (<<'EOF') so backticks and $ are literal; later commits in the portfolio use that form.

title: Board commands run after the session's working directory changed no longer found the board started elsewhere
symptom: A board was started from the home directory, the work then moved into the project directory, and later `apz done <n>` calls did not tick the expected tasks; the state file had to be hunted down and the commands re-run from the original directory.
root_cause: apz.mjs keys its worklog state file to the directory `start` was run in. Nothing in a later command's output says which board (if any) the current directory resolves to.
fix: Ran the remaining step/done/finish commands from the directory that started the board. Start the board from the project directory it will be worked in, and have every apz command print the board id it is acting on.

title: Local verification proxy forwarded zstd-compressed API responses undecoded, so the browser got binary under a JSON content-type
symptom: Through the localhost proxy curl returned clean JSON from /api/me but the app in the browser rendered the signed-out landing page with a forEach error; the page was receiving bytes starting 28 b5 2f fd.
root_cause: The browser sent accept-encoding including zstd, the proxy passed it upstream, Cloudflare answered zstd, and Node's fetch does not decode zstd. The proxy relayed the compressed body with the original JSON content-type. curl never asked for zstd, which hid it.
fix: The proxy forces accept-encoding: identity on the upstream request. A stale service worker was ruled out first by checking registrations and caches, then by reading the raw response bytes in the page.

title: Editor wrapper set to 92vw inside a 1120px-capped modal clipped the right-hand control panel
symptom: At desktop width the Layers editor's inspector panel overflowed the modal's right edge and its controls were cut off.
root_cause: The inner wrapper was sized in viewport units (92vw) while the shared .modal container caps at 1120px, so on wide screens the child was wider than its parent.
fix: Wrapper is width:100% of the modal and the canvas column is capped so the panel always fits. Only seen after widening the Browser pane from about 800px, where the layout had simply stacked.

title: Auto-sampled ink colour came out washed (#686669) because the average included anti-aliased glyph edges
symptom: Replacement text in the Swap-text editor was drawn in a light grey noticeably paler than the original dark copy.
root_cause: The ink colour was the mean of all 'text' pixels in the selected box, and most of those are semi-blended fringe pixels between ink and background.
fix: Sample only the glyph cores: the pixels farthest in colour from the estimated background. Works for any ink colour; the same ad then sampled #504e50.

title: /api/upload kept only a fixed list of form fields, so an edit's provenance (`brief`) was silently discarded
symptom: A saved text-swap version would have carried no record of what was changed, although the lightbox already renders brief.swaps as 'original to replacement'.
root_cause: The upload handler copies a whitelist of multipart fields (purpose, project, tags, kind, parent_id, prompt, title, notes, model) and its INSERT had no brief column; any other field is dropped without an error.
fix: Added brief to the whitelist and the INSERT, and registered hidden model labels (text-swap, layers). Verified the saved record returns brief.swaps and brief.layers. An endpoint that whitelists fields should reject or report unknown ones.

title: Pointer helper read e.touches[0] on touchend, where the list is empty
symptom: Releasing a finger after drawing a selection box would throw (cannot read clientX of undefined) and the box would never be applied on touch devices.
root_cause: On touchend the lifted finger is no longer in e.touches; it is only in e.changedTouches. The coordinate helper used e.touches[0] for every touch event.
fix: Helper falls back to e.changedTouches[0]. Found on review before deploy. Related hardening in the same editor: setPointerCapture is wrapped in try/catch because it throws for pointer ids that are not active.

title: Auto-captions assumed word timings that Whisper did not return, and non-speech audio is transcribed as the word 'you'
symptom: The transcribe endpoint returned text and VTT but an empty words array, so captions would have been one untimed block. On a clip with only a tone or silence the caption burned into the video read 'you'.
root_cause: The Workers AI Whisper response used here carries segment timings in VTT, not per-word timings. Whisper also emits a stock token ('you') for audio with no speech.
fix: Captions are built from word timings when present and otherwise from parsed VTT segments; captions are click-to-edit and can be switched off. Still open: the non-speech 'you' is not filtered, so a silent clip gets a bogus caption unless the user removes it.

title: Test media was written into public/ and went out with `wrangler deploy`, sitting on the live site until a clean redeploy
symptom: ffmpeg-generated fixtures (__cliptest.mp4, __musictest.mp3, __c1.mp4, __c2.mp4, __cap.mp4) were publicly served from the production Worker during verification.
root_cause: The fixtures were created inside the static assets directory so the local proxy could serve them, and deploys were run while they were present.
fix: Files removed and the Worker redeployed clean each time, with a check that no __ files remain. Better: keep fixtures in the scratchpad and have the proxy serve them from a separate route, or add the pattern to .assetsignore.

title: Monthly credits (50/200) were enforced nowhere, so any signed-in account could run unlimited paid image generation
symptom: The pricing page sold 50 and 200 monthly credits, but no credit, usage or quota table existed in any migration and the AI worker never checked a balance. Free accounts could generate without limit, each call billing Workers AI.
root_cause: Plan limits lived only in marketing copy and client code; the server that spends the money had no entitlement check (billable denial-of-wallet).
fix: Server-side enforcement added in the AI worker (D1 usage table, monthly and daily caps). Verified with a five-test harness that counts AI calls: a free user at the limit gets 402, a request for more than is left is refused, free hooks are refused, all before any AI call, and a failed generation refunds the credit.

title: Verification harness ran in Node and tested only refused URLs, so it passed a deploy that broke every legitimate fetch
symptom: A five-test harness reported 5 of 5 against the deployed worker code and a published report called the deploy 'safe to charge' with 'redirects are blocked', while production was failing every uploaded-photo reference.
root_cause: Two gaps: the harness executed the worker source under Node, whose fetch accepts redirect:'error', not under workerd; and every test covered a URL that should be rejected, none covered the normal path of a legitimate upload being fetched.
fix: Added a Miniflare (workerd) regression test that includes the happy path; it fails on the broken build and passes on the fix. A correction report was published beside the original, and a standing rule was saved: test the positive path in the real runtime and check runtime support before recommending an option.

title: Interim copy 'Every image Face-Matched on your device' overclaims: the PFP generator never runs Face Match
symptom: A launch session proposed 'Every image Face-Matched on your device' as replacement hero copy. A grep for readFace/compare/scan calls found them in Studio.tsx but none in PfpGenerator.tsx.
root_cause: The claim generalised from the Studio flow, where every generation is auto-scanned, to all image surfaces without checking each generator.
fix: Flagged to the launch session before the copy shipped; scope the wording to Studio generations or add the check to the PFP generator. Also recorded: no setup in the 25-image pilot reached the 'locked' verdict, so 'same face guaranteed' must not be promised.

title: Engine swap from Gemini to Workers AI FLUX removed the only provenance mark, and 200 photoreal Prompt Bank images are live with no AI marking
symptom: Image generation first shipped on Gemini 3.1 Flash Image, which carries SynthID. On 7 Oct 2026 it was switched to FLUX on Workers AI, which carries no mark. A scan of all 200 Prompt Bank photos found no C2PA, XMP or DigitalSourceType markers.
root_cause: The model migration was evaluated on cost and consistency only; the upstream watermark was an invisible dependency for EU AI Act Art. 50 marking. The swap may also count as a new system, which could void the grace period to 2 Dec 2026.
fix: Open. Planned, not built: two-layer marking as the EU Code of Practice expects (signed C2PA metadata plus an imperceptible watermark), marking the Prompt Bank images, and asking counsel whether the grace period still applies. Tracked as three launch blockers.

title: MEMORY.md index grew to 30.5 KB and its tail was silently cut off when loaded
symptom: The auto-memory index had reached 30.5 KB against a load limit of about 17.1 KB, so the entries at the end were not reaching new sessions and nothing reported it.
root_cause: Every session appended long one-line hooks to a single index file with no size check; the loader truncates rather than warns.
fix: Archived the full index verbatim to reference-memory-index-archive-2026-10-07.md, rewrote MEMORY.md to 12.5 KB with all 108 entries kept as short pointers, and verified every linked file still resolves. Check the byte size after each index edit.

title: Joy Broadcast: pre-send check panel rendered nothing because the result reused the API envelope's 'ok' key
symptom: Opening the pre-send check on a campaign showed an empty panel instead of the list of checks.
root_cause: The preflight function returned { ok: <no blocking checks>, checks }. The client treats ok:false as a failed request, so a campaign with any blocking check looked like an API error and the checks were never drawn.
fix: Renamed the field to ready ({ ready, checks }) so a blocked campaign is a successful response carrying its reasons; the send path now tests pf.ready.

title: Joy Broadcast reply autopilot: the model mangled the sender's signature when asked to end the draft with it
symptom: A drafted answer ended with 'Joy Studio)}' instead of the configured signature.
root_cause: The drafting prompt told Workers AI to finish the message with the signature, so a fixed string was passed through the model and came back altered.
fix: The prompt no longer asks the model to write the signature; code appends it exactly as the owner typed it after the draft is returned.

title: Joy Broadcast: line breaks typed inside a paragraph were collapsed, so 'Thanks,' and the sender's name ran onto one line
symptom: Outreach and campaign emails showed sign-offs and postal addresses on a single line in both the HTML and the plain-text part.
root_cause:
The renderer joined every line of a paragraph with a space before emitting the

and the text part.
fix: render.js now keeps single line breaks inside a paragraph (a break in HTML, a newline in text). Deployed together with the People view.

title: Joy Broadcast: one-to-one outreach emails inherit the bulk-mail header from the shared MIME builder (open)
symptom: Emails sent through the outreach lane to a single business carry the same 'bulk' precedence header as list campaigns.
root_cause: The outreach lane reuses the campaign MIME builder unchanged; the header is set there for newsletters.
fix: Open. Identified as a spam-folder risk for one-to-one mail and left in place; make the header conditional on the campaign kind.

title: Lead Finder: Overpass (OpenStreetMap) rejected every tile with HTTP 406 because the Worker sent a browser-style User-Agent
symptom: A 154-tile New York search reported almost every tile as 'busy' within a second, which looked like overload. Reading the raw responses showed the server refusing the request with 406, not timing out.
root_cause: The module's shared UA constant was a 'Mozilla/5.0 (compatible ...' string; the public Overpass servers reject browser-like agents and expect a client that identifies itself.
fix: Overpass requests now send an identifying application User-Agent, and the step distinguishes a refusal from a genuinely busy or heavy tile so the failure is not misreported.

title: Lead Finder: a search started by Ava after a page reload was created but never ran, and the panel kept showing the previous search
symptom: After reloading and asking Ava for hair salons, the job existed on the server with zero progress while the panel stayed on the bakeries search. In another case a florist search never ran because a café search was started straight after it.
root_cause: The panel resumed the newest unfinished job on open and its step loop kept running for that job; a new job did not stop the old loop or take over the panel, so two loops competed and the new one never stepped.
fix: One search loop per job: starting a job cancels the previous loop and switches the panel to the new job. Verified that only the new search steps afterwards. The temporary window.__lf debug handle was removed before commit.

title: Lead Finder: results did not say which search they belonged to, so a café result looked like a wrong answer to a florist search
symptom: The owner asked for florists and saw 'Full Bloom Coffee Roasters'. The row was a correct result of the earlier café search; the florist search had not run.
root_cause: The results list had no heading naming the query and rows carried no category, and searches only advanced while the Outreach studio was open, so an abandoned search sat idle with nothing saying so.
fix: Results open with 'Results for <what> in <where> - N found', every row has a category label with a filter, and the Worker's every-minute cron continues any search nobody is watching and sends a notification when it finishes.

title: Lead Finder rules box unreadable in dark mode: background fell back to a light hex from an undefined CSS variable
symptom: In dark mode the country-rules box showed light text on a near-white background.
root_cause: .lf-checks used background:var(--bg-2,#f6f6f9); --bg-2 is not defined in the app's theme, so the light fallback applied in every theme.
fix: Switched to a variable the theme defines for both modes, after listing which custom properties actually exist in app.css.

title: Test setup rewrote a project's .claude/launch.json while another session had uncommitted changes in it
symptom: While adding two temporary dev-server entries, the session overwrote Hallalu's .claude/launch.json, which another live session had modified and not committed.
root_cause: The file was regenerated from a filtered copy instead of being edited additively, with no check of git status for that path first.
fix: Restored from the copy printed earlier in the transcript and confirmed git diff showed the other session's configurations intact. Temporary servers were then added to the user-level ~/.claude/launch.json instead, and later moved to free ports when other sessions took 8799 and 9341.

title: A second parallel SpeechRecognition added 'for redundancy' blanked the live transcript on real calls
symptom: On a real call the audio recorded but no transcript was written on screen as the user spoke.
root_cause: A second recogniser (call.rec2) was started about 600ms after the primary. Chrome allows only one active SpeechRecognition on the mic, so rec2 took it from the primary, and only the primary painted the on-screen box. The dual recogniser had only been proven in a simulator, never on a real mic.
fix: Removed the parallel live recogniser: one live recogniser plus a Workers AI Whisper HD re-transcribe of the saved recording as the second pass. Diagnosed from code; the Browser pane blocks the mic, so the real-call path still needs one device check.

title: 'Accept everything' on the call recap re-booked a meeting that summariseCall had already auto-booked, duplicating it and changing its date
symptom: After tapping Accept everything the agreed meeting flipped from Thu Oct 8 to Fri Oct 2 and a second calendar event appeared.
root_cause: summariseCall already auto-books the agreed meeting; autoBookMeeting pushes a new event on every call and sets no 'booked' flag. The new accept-all handler ran it again with a fallback date.
fix: Accept everything now applies only what is not auto-applied (to-dos, record updates, reminders) and the meeting path is gated. Re-verified on the live demo: date unchanged, no duplicate event, 2 action items added.

title: Report showed 'Committed / Deployed: not yet' for work that was committed, pushed and live
symptom: The published report's ship chips said not committed and not deployed after five commits and five deploys.
root_cause: apz finish auto-flags 'committed' only when the git tree is fully clean (untracked report and worklog files were present) and 'deployed' is opt-in.
fix: Pass the real state explicitly (finish --committed --sha --branch --deployed). Because reports are append-only, republishing minted a new report link and the earlier link stayed stale.

title: Agent token cannot list projects, so a mistyped --name on 'apz project' silently creates a duplicate project
symptom: While writing next steps onto 12 project cards there was no way to confirm the exact existing project names; every candidate list endpoint was refused for the agent token.
root_cause: The agent token is Bearer-only and the project list is PIN-gated to the dashboard, while the enrich endpoint creates a project whenever the name does not match.
fix: Not fixed in the product. Workaround used: take names from earlier apz runs recorded in memory, and put the full itemised list in one report so nothing depends on name matching.

title: First build let required follows unlock rewards, which YouTube, X, Meta and Discord developer rules prohibit
symptom: The product's core flow was 'follow on X/YouTube/Instagram, then the reward unlocks'. A policy check on the official pages found each platform bans rewarding or requiring follows, subscribes or joins.
root_cause: The design was built from the brief before the platform terms were read. YouTube API policy III.F.3 forbids incentives for subscribing, X's developer policy forbids compensation for follows, Meta's spam rules forbid requiring follows for exclusive content.
fix: Follows on those platforms became optional 'connect' steps that are verified and shown on the receipt but never gate anything; rewards can only be unlocked by permitted steps (answer, link, proof upload, Telegram, TikTok, Twitch) and a path may have no reward. Builder, landing table and e2e tests were updated.

title: Platform handles were written into the permanent append-only proof record, so they could never be erased
symptom: The tamper-proof events table (edits and deletes refused by the database) held participants' account handles.
root_cause: Identity display data was stored in the same rows as the hash-chained proof, which conflicts with erasure requests and with platform API data-retention limits.
fix: The record now holds only anonymous account fingerprints; display handles live in a separate deletable table and participants get a delete-my-data control. Covered by new e2e checks.

title: A shell loop passed '--local --persist-to .wrangler/state' as one argument, so only the remote database was migrated
symptom: Looping a wrangler d1 command over '--remote' and '--local --persist-to .wrangler/state' reported one success; the local copy silently missed an UPDATE and later a migration.
root_cause: The loop variable holding several flags was expanded unsplit (the session shell is zsh), so wrangler received a single malformed argument.
fix: Run the remote and local commands as two separate invocations and check each prints success (or 'duplicate column' on a re-run).

title: Deployed with one e2e check failing: the mock platform remembered the Instagram test user as a follower from the previous run
symptom: The suite passed 56/56 on the first run; on a later run the 'not a follower' check failed, and the commit and deploy had already gone out in the same command.
root_cause: The test used a fixed Instagram user id and the stand-in platform server keeps follower state across runs, so the negative case could not be reproduced. The ship step was not gated on the test result.
fix: Give each run a fresh Instagram user id (and a random Telegram id in the mock). The failure was then confirmed to be a test artifact rather than a product bug.

title: An index-range scripted rewrite of render() also deleted the adjacent actions() function
symptom: After the gamified redesign the participant page had no step actions; the function that builds them was gone.
root_cause: The rewrite replaced everything between two string anchors ('function render() {' to 'function followWindow(url)'), and actions() sat inside that range.
fix: Restored actions() from the last commit with git show HEAD:public/q.js. Lesson recorded: after a range replace, diff the list of function names before and after.

title: Follow button could leave the participant page blank when the new window did not open (Instagram and TikTok in-app browsers)
symptom: Tapping a follow/visit step on the production demo replaced the path page instead of opening the platform alongside it; in in-app browsers the page could go blank.
root_cause: followWindow assumed a pop-up window would open and did not handle the blocked case.
fix: Rewrote followWindow so the path page stays intact when a new window is refused, and added an 'open in your browser' banner for in-app browsers. Re-verified on production that the server-side timer starts and Done enables.

title: Paths with no reward could complete before every platform was done, and the highlighted next step pointed at the wrong place
symptom: On a 'support me everywhere' path with no reward, completion fired early and the active-step highlight was wrong.
root_cause: Completion and the next-step pointer were computed from required (gating) steps only; after follows became optional connect steps, a reward-free path had nothing gating.
fix: Reward-free paths now complete only when every step is done, and the next-step pointer falls back to the first unfinished step. Covered by new e2e checks (90/90).

title: Builder labelled self-reported Instagram steps 'Verified', and landing copy overclaimed one-tap follows and anti-farming
symptom: No-keys Instagram steps showed a Verified badge in the builder; the landing page said every button lands on Follow and that 'one account counts once, so farmed entries don't get through'.
root_cause: Badge and copy were written before the mechanics were checked: no-keys steps are attested until the creator's export confirms them, only X and Threads document a follow intent (YouTube's sub_confirmation is undocumented), and account uniqueness applies only to platform-account steps.
fix: Badge reads 'Attested, then confirmed by your follower list'; copy says each platform account counts once per path and that buttons land 'as close to Follow as the platform allows'.

title: Market-sizing bars on a research dashboard were not drawn to scale (SOM about 0.2% of TAM shown as about 9%)
symptom: The TAM/SAM/SOM chart made the obtainable market look far larger relative to the total than the numbers said.
root_cause: Bar widths were set for legibility rather than computed from the values.
fix: Caught before publishing; replaced the bars with plain labelled figures rather than a misleading picture.

title: Joy Broadcast A/B test: variant B won but the rest of the list was sent variant A
symptom: In a local end-to-end run B led on clicks and was declared winner, yet the remaining recipients were queued with the 'wa' variant.
root_cause: The send pump called decideAb and then carried on with the A/B state it had read before the decision, so the stale state chose the arm.
fix: Re-read / use the decided state after decideAb before queuing the remainder. Whole scenario re-run: B wins, the other 20 get 'wb', campaign finishes 'sent', and the delivered .eml files contain subject B and design B.

title: Email Maker card images kept their desktop width when columns stacked on phones
symptom: In phone preview the product cards stacked full-width but their images stopped at the narrow desktop column width.
root_cause: The mobile rule made .em-col full width but did not widen the images inside it.
fix: Extended the mobile stacking rule so images in stacked columns fill the column. Verified in the phone preview.

title: Ava email generator wrote a malformed merge tag ({{there}}) and put the discount code in body text instead of an offer block
