symptom: A generated launch email greeted readers with a literal '{{there}}' and the coupon was plain text.
root_cause: The system prompt did not pin the exact merge-tag syntax or tell the model which block types to use for codes, headers and products.
fix: Tightened the prompt with the exact tag form and block guidance; the regenerated design used the header, coupon and product-card blocks.

title: Email-to-template importer lost buttons with placeholder '#' links and read a sans stack ending in 'sans-serif' as serif
symptom: Round-tripping the app's own rendered templates through the importer dropped some buttons and the overlay hero photo, and picked the wrong typeface.
root_cause: Links that were not http/mailto/tel were demoted to text (placeholder '#' included); the font test matched 'serif' inside 'sans-serif'; hero photos set as CSS backgrounds and accent colours on button cells were not read; an inner helper named card collided with another binding.
fix: Keep '#' links as buttons, test the font stack correctly, read CSS-background images and button-cell colours, rename the helper. Re-tested on a real sent email and two templates.

title: Email Maker pre-send check counted a bare 'https://' as a finished link
symptom: A button whose URL was only the scheme passed the unfinished-link check in a smoke test.
root_cause: okUrl only tested that the value started with http(s)://, mailto: or tel:.
fix: Require something after the scheme. The check then blocked the unfinished link in the saved-campaign test.

title: Email Maker check panel kept reporting an empty image slot after photos were baked into place in the background
symptom: After Ava designed an email and Pixelbake filled the photo, the checks still said one image slot was empty although the saved design was complete.
root_cause: The check panel was refreshed on user edits only, not after asynchronous background changes to the design.
fix: Refresh the checks on background commits too (and fixed the '1 photos' plural).

title: New shared Email Maker files were twice left out of the build copy list, so the Worker could not load them
symptom: After adding pixelbake-proxy.js, and later email-import.js, the dev server failed on the new routes until restarted with a fixed build.
root_cause: shared/build.mjs copies an explicit MAKER array of file names into each app; new files are not picked up unless added to the array.
fix: Added each file to the MAKER list (and later ava-template.js up front). A note was saved to project memory.

title: A/B pre-send check said the test would go to 'about 0 people' on a tiny list
symptom: With a very small audience the A/B card passed and described a test slice of roughly zero recipients per arm.
root_cause: The per-arm size was computed and reported with no minimum.
fix: Preflight now blocks the A/B test when the arms would be too small instead of passing it.

title: Eight bakes fired in parallel: six failed with Workers AI internal errors
symptom: A script that launched 8 pxb gen calls at once got 2 images and 6 internal errors (nothing was charged).
root_cause: Concurrent image generations against the same account hit Workers AI internal errors.
fix: Bake one at a time, with a retry ladder (same model twice, then a smaller model). The next batches of 10 and 6 all succeeded first try sequentially.

title: pxb fix (paint-a-fix) returned a smaller image and repainted the area as a different garment
symptom: Asking for a neat crew neckline on one sweater returned a downsized photo with a turtleneck painted in.
root_cause: The fix path re-renders the whole photo at a lower size rather than editing the region at source resolution.
fix: Not changed in the product. Ruled out for photos that must stay sharp; the repair was done by cropping the region, editing the crop, and blending it back with soft edges, and later by a full restage.

title: Email research pass 1 carried misattributed benchmarks: wrong Campaign Monitor rates, a Yahoo rule credited to Google, and an unsourced '+371% single CTA' stat
symptom: A second verification pass found figures in the first pass that did not match their primary pages.
root_cause: Numbers were taken from secondhand articles: Campaign Monitor's own page says 2.3% CTR and 10.5% CTOR (2021 data), not 2.69% / 14.10%; Google's sender page sets no unsubscribe processing time (the 2-day figure is Yahoo's); Klaviyo's bot-click filtering began August 2024; the '+371%' claim has no primary study.
fix: Corrections log written into the evidence file; the unreliable figures are excluded and the report benchmarks use the primary numbers.

title: Marketing site and deck said 'Same character · Era' / 'Same her, every scene' while only 2 of 25 Era images matched her reference
symptom: The owner looked at the v2 site and said the Era photos 'still look like different people'. The site sticker read 'Same character · Era' and the deck had a 'Same her, every scene' slide. Scoring the library against Era's real photo showed only 2 of 25 images under the app's match distance (<0.40); with ArcFace, only edits of her real photo scored 0.68-0.72, and two photos chosen for the Play v2 hero scored 0.19 and 0.20 (lookalike strangers score up to 0.35).
root_cause: The consistency claim was written from the product's promise and from picking photos by eye; no identity measurement was run on the images actually shown before the claim shipped.
fix: Removed the claim from the site (sticker changed to 'Era · house character') and reworded the deck slide, then built a measurement lab so a consistency claim is only made for images that pass a scored identity gate.

title: Identity Lab scores faces with ArcFace weights that are licensed for non-commercial use only (flagged, not fixed)
symptom: The new identity score (browser ONNX + Node scorer) that is meant to sit next to Face Match in a paid product runs on the ArcFace model; the session's own research brief flags it as non-commercial.
root_cause: The most accurate freely downloadable face-recognition weights were used to get a baseline quickly; their licence does not cover commercial use.
fix: Not fixed. Recorded in research/identity-measurement.md with AuraFace (Apache-2.0) named as the commercial swap before the score ships in the app.

title: New marketing site skipped heading levels on /tools and /pricing and relied on implicit labels for the /contact inputs
symptom: The a11y sweep on the freshly deployed site reported three failures: heading levels skip on /tools and /pricing, and the /contact form inputs had no label the checker could associate.
root_cause: Section headings were chosen for visual size rather than outline order, and the form wrapped inputs in label elements without for/id pairs.
fix: Added the missing intermediate headings on both pages and gave the contact inputs explicit labels; the sweep then passed all 18 routes.

title: Face-scan HUD brackets sat on the model's hair instead of her face, and would move with every viewport
symptom: In the Future direction's hero, the scan brackets framed Era's hair rather than her face.
root_cause: The brackets were positioned in the hero container's coordinates while the photo is cropped/scaled to fit, so the overlay had no fixed relation to where the face lands.
fix: Stored the face position in image coordinates on the element (data-face="0.667,0.38,0.105") and a small script maps it to the rendered photo, so the brackets stay on the face at every screen size.

title: Local Identity Lab rejected the owner's real lab key: .dev.vars held a different LAB_KEY from the saved key file
symptom: The owner typed the key from ~/.startinstory-lab.json into the local lab's sign-in page and it was refused ('i put in the key not working').
root_cause: wrangler dev reads LAB_KEY from labworker/.dev.vars, which had been given its own throwaway 'devtest-' key at setup, while the saved key file holds the production secret. Two keys for one tool, and the user was pointed at the wrong one.
fix: Compared the two without printing either, backed up .dev.vars, set it to the saved key and restarted; the right key now redirects in and a wrong key still returns 401.

title: Worker login redirect built with Response.redirect(url.origin + '/login') left the local dev host
symptom: While testing the lab under wrangler dev, the sign-in redirect took the Browser pane off localhost; after the fix the session notes 'Now on localhost'.
root_cause: Inferred, not stated in the conversation: under wrangler dev url.origin resolved to a host other than the one the browser was using, so an absolute redirect built from it sent the browser elsewhere.
fix: Replaced it with new Response(null, { status: 302, headers: { location: '/login' } }) so the redirect is relative to whatever host served the page.

title: Kit harnesses leave a Chrome profile folder in /tmp on every run; about 2 GB of them filled the disk mid-run
symptom: A sharp image-resize step failed with the disk full part-way through the v2 run. /tmp held hundreds of shoot-*, ver-*, a11y-*, con-*, ss-*, of-* and perf-* directories, about 2 GB in total; the Mac was left with about 2 GB free of 228 GB.
root_cause: shoot.mjs, verify.mjs, a11y.mjs, contrast.mjs and the other kit harnesses each launch Chrome with a fresh --user-data-dir under /tmp and never delete it; sweeping 18 routes x 5 directions several times multiplies that into hundreds of profiles.
fix: Deleted only the throwaway profiles this session created and added cleanup after each harness run. The kit scripts themselves should remove their profile directory on exit.

title: Headless Chrome captures of WebGL and lazy-rendered sites came back blank
symptom: Reference screenshots of eight 'futuristic' leader sites (Runway, Luma, Krea, Pika, Spline and others) taken with the headless shoot harness were mostly blank images.
root_cause: As stated in the session: the pages draw with WebGL and render lazily, which the headless capture does not wait for or cannot paint. Not investigated further.
fix: Read those sites in the real Browser pane instead (scrolling the full page) and recorded measurements from there; do not treat a blank headless capture as what the site looks like.

title: Appending main = "src/worker.js" to the end of wrangler.toml put it inside the [assets] table
symptom: After adding a Worker script, D1 and accounts to a static-assets-only project, the dev server did not pick up the Worker entry; the session found 'the main line landed inside the assets table'.
root_cause: The config was extended with cat >> wrangler.toml. In TOML every key after a [table] header belongs to that table, so the appended top-level key main became assets.main.
fix: Rewrote wrangler.toml with name, main and compatibility_date above the first table, and [assets] (binding, directory, run_worker_first) below. Never append top-level keys to a TOML file that already has tables.

title: Player fish faced the opposite way to where it was steered, putting the mouth on the wrong side
symptom: The owner reported 'sometimes i am putting it to the right but it is facing opposite' and that it affected eating.
root_cause: Two causes. Facing was taken from horizontal velocity past a threshold (if |vx| > 15 then dir = sign(vx)), so it lagged or disagreed with the pointer or key direction; that the lag is the mechanism is my reading of the replaced line. Separately the hero sprite had been baked facing left while the rig assumes right-facing (already ledgered).
fix: Facing now follows the steering input (cursor side or key direction) rather than velocity, and the hero sprite was flipped; every later sprite is orientation-checked before use.

title: Game shipped under another publisher's trademarked title and with its stage, region and mechanic names
symptom: The remake went live as 'Feeding Frenzy' at feeding-frenzy.coconvo.workers.dev, with the original's map name, three region names, the boss name, eleven stage titles and terms such as 'Double Frenzy', 'School Bonus', 'Food Bank' and 'Yummy!'. The owner asked for the names to change because it 'cant be exact same'.
root_cause: The working title and the vocabulary noted while studying the reference playthrough were carried straight into the shipped product; there was no naming step that cleared the game of its reference.
fix: Renamed to Hungry Tide (string-only edits), replaced every borrowed name, deployed under a new Worker name, deleted the old Worker so the old URL returns 404, and searched the rendered pages for zero old names. Naming clear of the reference became step one of the game-maker recipe.

title: New global click delegate keyed on data-open collided with an existing data-open that carries a post id
symptom: Caught in review before deploy: the CSP-safe delegate added for external links would have called window.open() with a post id on every feed card.
root_cause: The delegate claimed the generic attribute name data-open for 'open this URL', but views2.js already rendered data-open="${p.id}" and wired it to openPost. A document-level listener matches every element with the attribute, whoever owns it.
fix: Renamed the external-link attribute to data-openext. Before adding a document-level delegate, grep the codebase for the attribute name it will match.

title: Modals do not close on Escape (flagged, not fixed)
symptom: During verification the backtest modal did not close when Escape was pressed; it could only be dismissed with its button or a backdrop click.
root_cause: The modal factory wires a mousedown on the backdrop and the close buttons only; the session did not find a keydown handler. Not investigated further.
fix: Not fixed in this session. Add an Escape handler (and focus return) to the shared modal factory.

title: A nearly full disk makes the iOS Simulator hang silently, which looks like a broken login
symptom: With the Data volume about 98% full (around 4 GiB free), simctl boot, launch and get_app_container each hung past 60 seconds, the simulator lost its render surface, and the app stayed on its login screen: the seeded token was still present but /me never returned, and a manual sign-in showed no spinner and no error. The same API login worked instantly from the web.
root_cause: As concluded in the session from that evidence, not proven by a controlled test: the simulator was starved by the full disk, so its calls stalled rather than failed. The login code was untouched.
fix: Stopped retrying and reported native as build-verified only. Check free space before a simulator walkthrough, and treat 'hangs with no error' on an unchanged flow as an environment fault until space is freed.

title: df -h / reported 630 MiB free while the Data volume had 5.7 GiB
symptom: The session read 630-635 MiB free from df -h / and planned around that; a later df on /System/Volumes/Data showed 5.7 GiB free.
root_cause: On current macOS / is the sealed system snapshot volume; user data lives on /System/Volumes/Data, and the two report different free figures.
fix: Read free space with df -h /System/Volumes/Data when deciding whether there is room to build or run a simulator.

title: Slide said self-kindness made people perform better; the cited study measured time spent studying
symptom: The owner's wording for slide 6 claimed people who were kind to themselves after failing did better on the next test, attributed to a named study.
root_cause: The finding was paraphrased from memory of secondary write-ups. Breines & Chen (2012) measured how long participants studied for the next test, not their scores.
fix: Rewrote the line to 'spent longer studying for the next test' and named it as a UC Berkeley experiment, and told the owner the wording was changed and why.

title: Slide 2 carried a statistic whose cited source could not be confirmed on its primary page, and teen figures aimed at adult women
symptom: Slide 2's source line credited Deloitte for 'women still carry most of the load at home'; the figure could not be read on Deloitte's own page. The Pew numbers on the same slide (55% and 45%) are for US teens aged 13-17 although the audience is adult women. A third line (Lally 2010, 'one missed day made no real difference') rests on secondary reports because the journal page blocked access.
root_cause: The first draft took numbers from search summaries; primary pages were only opened at the citation pass.
fix: Replaced the Deloitte line with US time-use data read on the BLS page (2.8 vs 2.1 hours of housework a day), labelled the Pew figures 'US teens', and listed the Lally line as resting on secondary sources in the hand-over.

title: At 9:16 the series label sat on the photo subject, headlines shrank too far, and a long label ran into the slide count
symptom: Rendering a third post at 9:16 showed the '30 days · one thing' label on top of the person in the photo, headlines much smaller than at 4:5, and the longer '30-day consistency challenge' label colliding with the slide counter.
root_cause: The renderer used one layout for every shape: the label was anchored over the photo area, the photo took a fixed share of a taller canvas so the text block had too little height, and the label was drawn at a fixed size with no fit to the space left of the counter. The first two are read from the fixes made; the conversation states the symptoms.
fix: At 9:16 the label moves into the text area under the photo, the photo takes less of the height (0.5 to 0.4), and the label shrinks to fit. All three posts were re-rendered and sampled.

title: 'Post by hand for better reach' is not supported: Instagram's head said scheduling has no effect on reach
symptom: The positioning for a plan-and-export tool leaned on the idea that posting by hand reaches more people than scheduled posts.
root_cause: A widely repeated creator belief was taken as a benefit without a source. The market study found Instagram's head saying in March 2025 that scheduling has no effect on reach.
fix: Listed in the study as 'one claim to drop'; the product is positioned on the daily planning loop instead.

title: Reference edits of a two-person photo swapped one friend's hair colour; another edit gave the subject a green cast
symptom: Baking scenes from a reference of two best friends (one blonde, one brunette) with flux-2-klein, the beach scene returned both women blonde. In an earlier single-model set one reference edit came back with a green cast on her hair.
root_cause: Model behaviour; the cause was not investigated. The reference edit does not reliably keep per-person attributes apart when two people share the frame.
fix: Rejected and re-baked each one, restating both people's hair colour in the prompt, and checked every raw at full size before composing. Treat per-person attributes as a QA item on any multi-person reference edit.

title: Per-mille symbol (‰) on the crude rate was read as a percent, so 5.5‰ looked like a wrong 5.5%
symptom: Owner asked to 'fix charts': the crude divorce rate was labelled '5.5 ‰' in KPIs, tooltips, rankings and the explorer. The symbol reads as %, and the world's highest crude rate (Maldives 5.5 per 1,000 people) looked smaller than Russia's 74 per 100 marriages because the two measures use different denominators.
root_cause: Stated in the conversation: the ‰ glyph is visually near-identical to %, and two metrics on different denominators (per 1,000 population vs per 100 marriages) were shown side by side with equal weight and no scale note.
fix: Removed ‰ everywhere; crude rate is a plain number labelled 'per 1,000 people — a different scale, not comparable to the % figure'; the per-100-marriages ratio is shown as % and made the default metric, first toggle, lead KPI and first explorer card; 'How to read this' rewritten.

title: 'Lowest divorce rate' headline presented under-registration artefacts as definitive (Venezuela 0.2, Vietnam 4%)
symptom: The KPI row named Venezuela (0.2 per 1,000) and Vietnam (4 per 100 marriages) as the lowest in the world with the same confidence as the well-registered high end.
root_cause: Stated in the /reason pass: crude divorce rates are only comparable among countries with complete civil registration; countries with weak registration under-report, so the low tail of an all-reporters ranking is confounded. The app ranked every reporter on one scale with no completeness caveat.
fix: Added a registration-completeness caveat to 'How to read this' (a very low reported rate can reflect incomplete registration rather than few divorces); verified in the live DOM; commit 3d67080. The headline itself was kept.

title: Regional 'World / Europe / Asia over time' trend lines were an unweighted mean of whichever countries reported, shown as if a regional rate
symptom: The Trends tab drew a 'World' line rising from ~12% to ~40% divorces per 100 marriages; early years rest on ~28–33 mostly European/OECD reporters.
root_cause: Stated: the line is a simple average of the countries in a region that have data that year — not population-weighted and not a constant panel — so it is not a world or regional rate.
fix: Relabelled the chart note as an 'unweighted average of reporting countries, not a world rate' and tagged it HYPOTHESIS in the verification report.

title: Line chart drew stray dots for isolated single-year points in a regional series
symptom: Two isolated points in the crude-rate Americas trend rendered as lone dots detached from any line.
root_cause: Inference (not spelled out in the conversation): the gap-aware line generator breaks the path at missing years, so a year with data but no neighbours becomes a zero-length segment that only shows as its marker.
fix: Null out isolated single points in the regional series before drawing so only connected runs render.

title: Dealership DMS report repeated a competitor's own marketing numbers as 'independently corroborated' (Jouver '4.8 on G2', '80+ countries')
symptom: The published market study said Jouver was 'real and independently corroborated' with 5,400+ dealers in 80+ countries and a 4.8 G2 rating. A later verification stream found G2 shows 0 reviews and the country count is inflated by auto-generated SEO pages.
root_cause: Stated: the first check treated SourceForge/Slashdot listings and the vendor's own comparison pages as independent sources; those listings are vendor-supplied, so the claim had one source, not two.
fix: Report updated in place with a corrections callout (rating unsubstantiated, country count inflated); the Jouver feature gap (no BHPH, no landed-cost) was re-verified from SourceForge's explicit 'Not Supported' field rather than from absence on a feature page.

title: Dealership DMS report shipped an outdated Trinidad import age limit (3 years; liberalised to 8 by Legal Notice 477) and called a competitor's financing 'unconfirmed' when it exists
symptom: First published version quoted a 3-year used-import age limit and said Autologica's in-house financing was unconfirmed. A follow-up stream found the limit moved to 8 years (effective Jan 2026) and that Autologica has full dealer-carried financing (amortisation, penalty interest, statements).
root_cause: Stated: the first pass relied on older secondary sources for the regulation and read a competitor capability off a partial page fetch; neither was checked against a primary source before publishing.
fix: Corrected both in the report (append-only corrections section); the CRM rate pack then shipped the 8-year limit as 'confirmed' and left MVT per-cc, levy amount and hybrid exemption flagged 'unconfirmed' and editable.

title: Claude Browser pane reports inline as 0×0, which was misdiagnosed twice as a broken SVG
symptom: Three charts embedded in a report page measured 0×0 in the Browser pane although each URL returned 200 with the right content-type and rendered when opened directly. Two wrong fixes shipped first: adding intrinsic width/height to the SVGs, then converting SVG→PNG; PNGs also read 0×0.
root_cause: As concluded in the conversation (the agent's own diagnosis, not confirmed against pane internals): the page uses plain and the pane's offscreen/sandboxed view never triggers the lazy fetch, so the images never load there; a normal browser and the downloaded HTML load them.
fix: Verify images by opening each asset URL top-level (or scrolling it into view with a real scroll) instead of measuring naturalWidth on the embedding page; do not change asset format on a pane-only 0×0.

title: Sign-in screen showed the modal overlay, header and tab bar: [hidden] lost to display:flex/grid rules
symptom: On first load of the CRM MVP the modal overlay, app header and tabs were visible on top of the sign-in screen even though they carried the hidden attribute.
root_cause: Stated in the commit: author display:flex / display:grid rules on those elements override the UA [hidden]{display:none} rule (same trap already recorded for Kindly, Hallalu CRM and Bug Ledger).
fix: Added a rule so [hidden] wins over the component display rules; bumped the asset version to v2.

title: Loan schedule did not put the first instalment on the chosen start date
symptom: A 6-month loan created with start_date 2026-11-01 did not have its first instalment due on 2026-11-01; caught in API verification of the amortisation ledger.
root_cause: Not stated in the conversation. Inference from the fix and its test (first row must equal start_date, last row start + term−1 months): the schedule was generated starting one period after the start date.
fix: First instalment now falls on the chosen start date; proven on an isolated throwaway tenant (first 2026-11-01, last 2027-04-01) and deployed.

title: Long dealer and user names wrapped the phone header, and the desktop tab bar collided with the header controls
symptom: Found only when the captured screenshots were reviewed a session later: on phone width the brand and signed-in name wrapped the top bar; at desktop width the fixed tab bar overlapped the right-hand header controls.
root_cause: Stated by the fix: header text spans had no max-width/ellipsis, and the desktop layout reserved no right padding for the absolutely positioned tabs.
fix: Ellipsis with max-width (44vw brand, 26vw name) on phone; at ≥900px reserve 470px right padding for the tab bar; asset version bumped to v4 and the two shots re-captured.

title: Wisdom Marketing: new every-minute cron trigger was never seen to run on live, so scheduled posts depended on the page being open
symptom: After deploying a scheduled() handler with a '* * * * *' trigger, the tables it creates had not appeared after ~7, ~25 and ~30 minutes (past Cloudflare's documented 15-minute propagation); 2.5 minutes of wrangler tail showed no scheduled event. `wrangler triggers deploy` reported the schedule as registered.
root_cause: Not determined in the conversation. The trigger was registered but no run was ever observed; the later appearance of the tables proves nothing because the first admin page visit creates them too. There was no heartbeat or last-run record to tell 'not firing' from 'firing and failing early'.
fix: Mitigation only: GET /api/mkt/queue/list now also sweeps due posts and the marketing page polls it every minute, so posts go out while the page is open (proven locally without the cron). Still open: confirm runs in the Worker's cron history; add a last-run stamp written by the handler.

title: Wisdom Marketing overview listed platforms already posted among those still 'to finish by hand'
symptom: After Instagram was marked posted, the Overview 'finish by hand' line for the same post still named Instagram alongside Threads, LinkedIn and X.
root_cause: Stated by the fix: the label was built from every assisted-mode platform on the post, without excluding those that already had a posted record.
fix: Filter out platforms already marked posted; confirmed in the browser (label showed only Threads, LinkedIn, X).

title: Wisdom Marketing: a deleted library file is still served from the browser cache for up to a day
symptom: After 'Yes, delete' the record vanished but the file and thumbnail URLs still returned 200 in the browser; R2 confirmed the objects were gone.
root_cause: Stated: private asset responses are sent with a 1-day browser cache lifetime, so a deleted object keeps rendering from the local cache until it expires.
fix: Not fixed in this run (listed under known rough edges). Candidate fix: shorter or revalidating cache for private files, or a version/delete-busting query on asset URLs.

title: Wisdom Marketing encrypts platform credentials with a key derived from PASS_PEPPER when MKT_KEY is unset
symptom: Stored Bluesky/Mastodon/Telegram/webhook credentials are AES-GCM encrypted with an HKDF key whose input is MKT_KEY or, as shipped, the password pepper. Rotating PASS_PEPPER would silently disconnect every platform, and one secret now protects both password hashes and third-party tokens.
root_cause: Stated in the code and the closing notes: baseKey() falls back to PASS_PEPPER because no dedicated secret was provisioned; a single secret is reused for two purposes.
fix: Not fixed; documented in project memory ('PASS_PEPPER also seals tokens'). Proper fix: set a dedicated MKT_KEY and re-encrypt, or store a key id with each ciphertext so rotation is possible.

title: 'A newer Hallalu is ready' update bar covers the bottom tab bar on phone width
symptom: At phone width the update bar sits on top of the bottom navigation, hiding Outreach, Money and Ava until it is tapped.
root_cause: Inference (the conversation only records the overlap): the bar is fixed to the bottom with no offset for the mobile tab bar.
fix: Not fixed — left because app.css held another session's uncommitted edits at the time.

title: Several sessions' dev servers serving one repo share the same local D1 state, so one session's test data was replaced by another's
symptom: On resuming Wisdom Marketing tests, the original port (8797) now answered 404 for the app and two other sessions' workerd servers (8796, 8798) were serving the same ~/Hallalu folder; the morning's test library and campaign were gone, overwritten by a demo workspace loaded on another port.
root_cause: Partly stated, partly inference: every wrangler dev started from the same folder uses the same local persistence directory, so all sessions read and write one local database and bucket; the port a session started on is not reserved for it.
fix: Rebuilt the fixtures through the UI and tested against the running server. Repeatable fix: give each session its own --persist-to directory and port, or seed fixtures from a script at the start of every verification run.

title: Reference playthrough video frames were tracked in git and mirrored to a forge before being excluded
symptom: The repo's early commits and a bulk import to GitBagel included study/ (frames and strips cut from another studio's game video). At GitHub push time the history could not be published as-is, and the GitBagel copy still holds study/.
root_cause: Stated: .gitignore initially excluded only study/reference.mp4, raw/ and shots/, so every extracted frame and contact sheet under study/ was committed; a bulk importer then copied the tree.
fix: Added study/, *.mp4 and *.part to .gitignore, untracked study/, pushed a single clean snapshot to a new private GitHub repo and kept the old history as a local-only branch. Still open: the private GitBagel mirror retains study/ pending the owner's decision.

title: git push failed twice because the GitHub CLI's default account token was invalid; an explicit per-account token header worked
symptom: `git push` to the new private repo failed twice; `gh auth status` reported the default token for the account as invalid. The push succeeded only when the token from `gh auth token -h github.com -u <account>` was passed as an explicit Authorization header.
root_cause: Not established in the conversation beyond 'gh says its default token is invalid'; the stored credential the git helper used was stale while a second stored token for the same account still worked.
fix: Workaround used for both pushes; owner told to run `gh auth login -h github.com`.

title: Launch headline 'The same face. Every post. Proven.' was unsupported: 25 images of one character, none reached 'locked'
symptom: A peer session ran 25 images of the house character through the app's own Face Match: no image scored 'locked', medians 34-50. The headline had already been recommended as the lead message.
root_cause: Stated: the claim was adopted from the existence of the Face Match feature before any measurement of what the generator actually achieves. Sample is one character only.
fix: Headline held back; 'Proven' allowed only after a test of at least 5 characters x 50 prompts shows locks (added as a blocker); creatives may only show a % measured on that exact image.

title: AI engine Worker folder is not under git while two sessions edit and deploy it - no history to roll back to (OPEN)
symptom: Two concurrent sessions edited ai-worker/src/worker.js and deployed minutes apart; the only way to prove nothing was lost was to download the deployed Worker code and compare.
root_cause: Stated: ~/startinstory-app/ai-worker sits outside the app repo and has no git history.
fix: Not fixed. Worked around by coordinating every edit/deploy over session messages and diffing disk against the deployed version; recommended moving the folder into the app repo.

title: A background research subagent took over the Browser pane tab in the middle of a feature walk-through
symptom: During local verification of Joy Cloud the tab navigated away mid-test and the walk had to be re-run.
root_cause: Stated: a research agent running in parallel used the same Browser pane tab as the main thread.
fix: Opened a dedicated tab for verification and re-ran the walk. Give browser-using subagents their own tab (or no browser) while the main thread is verifying.

title: Brand mark, URL, swipe cue and slide badge vanished on bright photo areas (window, white saucer)
symptom: On several statics and carousel slides the brand mark and URL were unreadable over a bright window, and 'swipe ->' and '1 / 6' were unreadable over a white saucer. On TikTok the two pills then touched.
root_cause: Stated: these elements were drawn as plain light text with no backing, relying on the photo being dark where they sit.
fix: Added a brand-pill option and a pillBadges option (dark pills) to compose.mjs; dropped the swipe cue on TikTok, whose photo mode shows its own swipe dots.

title: Unbranded 'four-leaf clover' earrings on the house character still read as a protected luxury jewellery motif (OPEN)
symptom: The owner asked for a named luxury brand's earrings; the bake used an unbranded clover with mother-of-pearl, which is still recognisable as that brand's signature design in ad creatives.
root_cause: Stated: removing the brand name does not remove the protected design.
fix: Not resolved: flagged for a legal check before any paid use; a later scene used plain diamond studs instead.

title: A newly added report slug returned 404 for a few seconds right after wrangler deploy (page and ?download=1)
symptom: Seen twice in separate sessions: the new /a/<slug> page, and later a new report's download link, returned 404 immediately after deploy and 200 on a retry seconds later.
root_cause: Assistant's inference in both cases: deploy propagation delay, since the entry was present in worker.js and nothing was changed before the retry.
fix: Sleep a few seconds and re-check before diagnosing; do not edit the entry on the first 404.

title: Llama vision per-frame notes leaked 'Line N:' prefixes into the stored on-screen text
symptom: Per-second frame notes on the first real decode contained 'Line 2:'-style artefacts.
root_cause: Stated: the vision model echoes the numbered-line structure of the frame prompt in its answer and the parser stored it raw.
fix: Strip the 'Line N:' artefacts when splitting the vision output into screen text and notes.

title: yt-dlp aborted the whole video download when YouTube throttled the caption request
symptom: A long-form decode failed with no media file even though the video itself was downloadable.
root_cause: Stated: subtitle flags (--write-auto-sub/--write-sub) were on the same yt-dlp call as the media download, so a throttled caption fetch failed the entire command.
fix: Download media without subtitle flags, fetch subtitles in a separate tolerant call, and accept any source.* container the run produced.

title: Page scrolled sideways on phones: single-column grid track was 1fr, not minmax(0,1fr)
symptom: Horizontal scroll on the mobile layout, caught by a CDP overflow check on the live site.
root_cause: Stated by the fix: under 900px the grid switched to grid-template-columns:1fr, whose auto minimum lets wide children stretch the track.
fix: Changed the track to minmax(0,1fr) and re-ran the live overflow check.

title: Mic level meter missed short sounds while recording
symptom: The live level bar barely moved on brief sounds.
root_cause: Inferred from the fix (the conversation only states the symptom): the meter showed the instantaneous analyser value per frame, so short peaks fell between paints.
fix: Peak-hold with a gentle decay on the level value.

title: Saving a new recording or upload stopped whatever was already playing
symptom: With a sound looping, finishing a recording or adding a file cut the playback.
root_cause: Inferred from the fix location: adding a sound called select() on the new track, and selecting a track tore down the current player.
fix: select() no longer interrupts an active player when a sound is merely added.

title: Files over 5 minutes looped with an audible join because they played through <audio loop>
symptom: Short sounds looped seamlessly via Web Audio buffers, but long files streamed through an audio element had a gap/click at each repeat - the exact failure sleep-sound users complain about.
root_cause: Stated: long files bypass the decoded-buffer path and rely on the browser's own element looping.
fix: Two audio elements with a crossfade near the end of each pass (second fades in from the start while the first fades out); pause/resume/stop clean up both. Verified with a 5.5-minute file. With 'Seamless loop' off it falls back to native looping.

title: zsh: parentheses in a double-quoted --tasks string inside $(...) broke the command; the board never started
symptom: apz start with task labels containing '(~15m)' failed to run when wrapped in A=$(...).
root_cause: As stated by the assistant: zsh choked on the unquoted parens inside the command substitution. The exact parse rule was not isolated.
fix: Single-quote the --tasks argument when labels contain parentheses or tildes.

title: Export stacked the editor's new fields on top of the PDF's own built-in form fields
symptom: A PDF that already had 45 AcroForm fields exported with the newly placed fields layered over the originals, so the output carried two sets of fields.
root_cause: Export added fields to the document without removing the form it already contained (stated in the session summary: 'Export: new fields were stacked on top of the PDF's old ones').
fix: Export now strips the built-in form first (a stripBuiltInForm step, confirmed present in the deployed app.js); local test showed no duplicates.

title: A cut-off vision-model reply discarded every field on the page
symptom: When the AI field-naming reply was truncated, the whole page came back with no AI labels at all.
root_cause: Inferred, not stated: the reply was parsed as one JSON document, so a truncated tail failed the parse and lost the complete entries before it. The session only states the outcome ('a cut-off AI reply no longer loses the whole page').
fix: Keep the entries that parsed; every pixel-detected box still becomes a field even if the AI skipped it, and after 75 s the app falls back to its own boxes and tells the user to check labels.

title: Vision model invented a field where the page has no printed box
symptom: On a second benchmark form the AI returned a field that does not exist on the page (clean PDF: 10 of 13 correct plus 2 extras).
root_cause: The prompt let the model add fields freely in addition to naming the numbered boxes; one of the two extras was the model's invention, the other a pixel-detection phantom (already ledgered).
fix: The model may only add a box-less field when it is a signature, initials or date; everything else must map to a numbered detected box. Result 13 of 13, no extras on the clean PDF.

title: Test PDFs including the owner's real visa form sat in public/_t, one deploy away from being published
symptom: To test detection locally, four PDFs (one the owner's own Visa History Form pulled from R2) were copied into public/_t; the session had to warn 'delete that folder before any deploy or commit, or they would be published'.
root_cause: Fixtures were placed inside the Workers static-assets directory because the local page needed to fetch them, and everything under public/ ships on wrangler deploy.
fix: Moved the files to the session scratchpad before git add and deploy, then checked the live site for leaked test files. Repeatable rule: serve fixtures from outside the assets dir or gitignore and assets-ignore a fixtures folder.

title: Account sign-up shipped open to anyone with no email check or CAPTCHA (flagged, not fixed)
symptom: After replacing the single access code with accounts, anyone can create an account; each Free account gets 30 AI page scans and 3 signature requests a month.
root_cause: Accounts were added from the shared auth-gate module without an email verification or bot check; the session lists it under Still open.
fix: Not fixed. Needs email verification or Turnstile on register plus a per-IP sign-up limit before the AI quota is abusable at scale.

title: wrangler dev kept serving the old index.html and app.css after an edit and a ?v= bump until it was restarted
symptom: A new CSS rule did not apply locally; the page still requested app.css?v=26 after index.html had been changed to ?v=27, so an icon-size fix looked like it had failed.
root_cause: The session attributes it to the dev server holding a stale snapshot of the static assets; that is its inference, and the mechanism was not investigated. Browser caching was ruled out by the unchanged ?v= in the served HTML.
fix: Restarted the dev server; v=27 and the rule loaded. Before concluding a CSS fix failed, check the served file for the new rule.

title: Mac app launched with `open` ignored the dev env overrides, then a stale Mac binary hid the same patch
symptom: The Mac build opened at the sign-in screen instead of the local test session; after relaunching the binary directly it still did, twice costing a screenshot round.
root_cause: `open` does not pass the shell's environment variables to the app (stated), and the Mac binary had been built before the ABBA_BASE/ABBA_TOKEN override was added because only the iOS target was rebuilt (stated).
fix: Rebuild every target after a shared-source patch and launch the binary inside the .app directly with the env set.

title: DM brief framed the $100 price as given in return for a review
symptom: The requested DM copy said buyers get the price 'because our websites need reviews', which makes the review the consideration for the discount.
root_cause: Offer framing tied an incentive to leaving a review. The session's same-day web research reported Google's policy bans rewards tied to reviews, the FTC review rule (16 CFR 465) bans incentives conditioned on sentiment, and the UK DMCC Act requires incentivised reviews to be disclosed; these are the session's readings of search results and were not re-verified here.
fix: Copy reworded: the $100 is a launch price for the first 100 sites; an honest review is optional, never a condition, and is asked for in a separate later message with no mention of price.

title: 'Works with Claude Code' was positioned as unique after a rival shipped the same thing
symptom: The marketing lead and site hero leaned on the agent integration as the differentiator.
root_cause: The positioning was never re-checked against competitors; the run's evidence refresh reported Krea has shipped a Claude Code connector since June 2026 (the session's research finding, not re-verified here).
fix: Lead moved to the per-image receipt (why, when, seed, cost) and 'failed bakes cost nothing'; the agent line was kept for developers only.

title: 'Read all conversations' pass skipped the nine largest sessions and missed a whole live app
symptom: A portfolio sync reported complete; the owner pointed out missing work. Postplan (a live app) was in neither the portfolio nor memory, and CD Enterprises was recorded as v5/v6 when v7 was live.
root_cause: The agent distilled about 20 sessions and trusted memory notes for the rest, including 81 MB and 47 MB transcripts (it said so itself).
fix: Distilled the nine skipped sessions and appended the corrections. Rule: a 'read all' claim needs a census of sessions read versus sessions present, largest first.

title: File mtimes made about 60 restored transcripts look like new work
symptom: 148 session files appeared changed since the last checkpoint, suggesting a large unsynced backlog.
root_cause: A filesystem sync/restore on 1 October rewrote modification times; the session found about 60 of the files were that restore, not real work.
fix: Date each transcript by the timestamp in its first line (and compare against the checkpoint ledger) instead of mtime.

title: A validated security fix sat uncommitted and undeployed for three days after a disk-full abort
symptom: The C1 vault fix (token-bound vault id, backup rate limit, write verifier) written on 4 October existed only as working-tree changes until 7 October; production kept the brute-forceable vault id.
root_cause: The disk hit zero bytes free mid-session, so commit and deploy could not run, and nothing recorded the open item where the next session would see it.
fix: Found during a transcript sync, re-reviewed, API-tested locally (unauthenticated overwrite returns 403), committed f2cd1b7 and deployed. Rule: when a session aborts with a security fix on disk, log it as an open item immediately.

title: Claude Code session transcripts reached 2.1 GB and refill a near-full disk as work proceeds
symptom: Free space fell from 6.7 GB to 1.1 GB between turns and to 306 MB at the start of another; shells failed with ENOSPC.
root_cause: Each session writes a .jsonl containing every tool result, 40 to 80 MB per long session (1,172 files older than two days held 1.6 GB), on a disk where about 160 GB sits in TCC-protected ~/Pictures that the agent cannot read or clear.
fix: Partial: regenerable caches cleared repeatedly; the owner chose to keep transcript history. Durable fix is the owner's (Photos/Photo Booth, optional trim of old transcripts).

title: Client-page Meetings card listed only hand-added meetings; a meeting booked from a call never appeared
symptom: A meeting agreed on a call showed in the calendar but not on that client's own page; the Meetings card looked empty or incomplete.
root_cause: The card read only the lead's own meetings array (mtgs(l) = l.meetings). Call-booked meetings live in the calendar store (S.cal.events, kind 'call'), which the card never consulted.
fix: The card now also surfaces calendar events of kind 'call' for that client, read-only with a 'from a call' tag and a Send-card action, de-duplicated against manual meetings (which mirror to the calendar as kind 'event' with an evId). Verified on a clean demo.

title: Background-removal results were labelled 'Fixed' and 'Cost: free' although each one charged 1 credit
symptom: Cutout tiles carried the 'Fixed' badge and the lightbox said 'Cost: free'; transparent cutouts also sat on a plain background so the transparency was not visible.
root_cause: Cutouts were filed as a versioned edit, and the tile and lightbox derived their label and cost line from the generic edit kind rather than from the cutout tag and the credits actually debited.
fix: Tiles now say Cutout, the lightbox says Cutout or Refined cutout with '1 credit', transparent results render on a checkerboard, and the Refine button also appears on refined transparent saves. Re-verified in the browser.

title: Long-recording splitter produced empty M4A pieces: lazy piece closures read a loop variable that had already moved on
symptom: A 58-minute test file split into six pieces correctly for WebM, MP3 and Ogg, but every M4A piece came out empty, so nothing would transcribe.
root_cause: Each M4A piece was a deferred (lazy) function that sliced by the loop's start/end variables. Those variables were updated after the closure was created, so by the time a piece was read every closure saw an empty range.
fix: Capture the start and end for each piece in per-iteration constants before pushing the lazy reader. All five formats then passed piece by piece on the live site.

title: Workers AI Whisper 503s silently dropped part of a long transcript
symptom: During a multi-piece HD transcription, Workers AI returned repeated '503 Service Unavailable'; half of one piece vanished from the stitched text with no sign anything was missing.
root_cause: The per-piece sender treated a failed request as an empty result. A transient capacity error therefore became missing text instead of a retry or a visible gap.
fix: Each piece is now retried with a wait (up to four tries), then re-encoded on the device and tried again; anything still missing leaves a visible '[couldn't transcribe 1:10:00-1:20:00]' marker and is retried on the next run. Verified with 503s occurring: all 173 numbered items of a 23-minute clip arrived.

title: A browser test on the deployed HTTPS app could not load a fixture from a localhost file server; the local app's own policy and a 25 MB asset cap blocked the fallbacks
symptom: An end-to-end run of a 58-minute audio fixture showed no progress. Fetching http://127.0.0.1 from the live HTTPS page failed, the local wrangler dev copy refused the same fetch, a relay popup was blocked, and copying the M4A into public/ failed because the local server limits assets to 25 MB.
root_cause: Browsers block a public HTTPS page from reading plain-HTTP localhost; the app's content security policy blocks cross-origin fetches in the local copy; popups opened from script are blocked in the pane; Workers static assets are capped at 25 MB per file.
fix: Serve the fixture same-origin: copy a smaller version (the 21 MB WebM) into a temporary folder under the app's public/ for the local run, then delete it before committing. Decide this up front instead of discovering each block in turn.

title: Adding a script tag to index.html from one session dropped the tag a concurrent session had just added
symptom: While one session added its longtx.js script line, the session building Wisdom Marketing reported that its marketing.js line had disappeared from public/index.html and had to put it back.
root_cause: Inferred, not confirmed in the conversation: the file was rewritten whole from content read before the other session's edit landed, so the later save overwrote the earlier one. Two sessions were editing the same shared file in one working tree.
fix: The other session restored its line and both tags were confirmed present before deploy. Later the same day the session deployed from a clean checkout of its own commit so the other session's uncommitted work did not ship. For a shared index.html, re-read immediately before a narrow in-place edit and grep for every expected script tag before deploying.

title: preview_start ignored a repo-local .claude/launch.json and read the home-level file, because the session was rooted at ~
symptom: In two sessions a launch config written to <repo>/.claude/launch.json could not be started by name; the pane only knew the configurations in ~/.claude/launch.json.
root_cause: The Browser pane resolves launch.json from the session's own project root, and these sessions run from the home directory and cd into repos. A file created inside the repo is therefore never read. This qualifies the existing advice to use a project-local launch.json: it holds only when the session is opened in that project.
fix: Delete the stray repo-local file and add the entry to ~/.claude/launch.json (checking the name and port are not already taken by another chat's server).

title: Headless Chrome phone-width screenshots looked clipped on the right, a capture artefact rather than a layout bug
symptom: A 390-pixel-wide headless Chrome screenshot of a redesigned page showed content cut off at the right edge, suggesting horizontal overflow.
root_cause: As attributed in the session: headless Chrome enforces a minimum window width, so a --window-size below it captures a wider layout cropped to the requested width. The page itself did not overflow.
fix: Checked a real 375 px viewport in the Browser pane, where nothing spilled sideways. Treat narrow --window-size shots as untrusted and confirm phone layouts with device emulation or the pane's mobile preset before changing CSS.

title: Phone HUD at 375 px pushed the pause button past the right edge
symptom: On a 375 px wide screen the top HUD row overflowed and the pause control sat off-screen, so a phone player could not pause.
root_cause: The HUD row was laid out for desktop with fixed-width groups (hands, growth track, zone name) and no narrow-screen rule; a first media query at 700 px was not enough.
fix: A second pass at 520 px hides the hands group, caps the growth track at 110 px and ellipsises the zone name, plus a rotate-to-landscape hint in portrait. Verified at 375 px. Still open from the same check: the three star icons are not visible in the top row at that width.

title: sudo du over the root listed /System at 184 GB, a re-count of the whole data volume rather than system bloat
symptom: While hunting about 100 GB of unexplained disk use, a root-level du reported /System as the largest directory at 184 GB on a 228 GB disk.
root_cause: As explained in the session (an inference from the macOS volume layout, not separately tested): the data volume is mounted under /System/Volumes/Data and linked back to /Users, /Applications and others, so sizing /System counts the user data again.
fix: Ignore the /System line and size /Users/<name> two levels deep with sudo instead; that located the real 57 GB in ~/Pictures.

title: On a phone the Joy Mail menu strip filled half the screen and left the inbox as a small box at the bottom
symptom: An owner screenshot from an iPhone showed the navigation area taking roughly the top half of the screen, with the message list squeezed underneath.
root_cause: At phone width the per-address list stacked inside the menu strip, so the strip grew with the number of addresses instead of staying a compact bar.
fix: A phone layout pass was written in the UI source so the address list no longer stacks inside the strip. The conversation ends while the local send and layout tests were still running, so the fix was not yet verified or deployed in this record.

title: Marketing set uses two composite quote hooks and 'free in beta' copy that have no source behind them yet
symptom: The 14-piece creative set includes two hooks written as quotations and several pieces saying the product is free in beta. The session's own closing notes state the quotes are composites, not real testimonials, and that there is no pricing page.
root_cause: Hooks were drafted from the 30 pain quotes gathered in research and merged into representative lines; the price claim was written before any pricing exists.
fix: Flagged, not fixed: nothing was posted. Before publishing, either attribute each quote to a real, linkable source or reword it as a plain statement, and change the 'free in beta' line when pricing ships. AI photos in the set are already labelled on the image.

title: Memory notes recorded global search and the vault fix as shipped for both apps, but Social LevelUp had neither
symptom: Two 75-day-old memory notes said global search and the C1 vault fix shipped on 21 July. A grep of the monorepo showed Budget LevelUp had both, while Social LevelUp still derived its vault id from the public handle, had no rate limit on its backup endpoint and had no search at all.
root_cause: The earlier work was done in one app of a two-app monorepo and written up as if it covered the family; nothing re-checked the sibling app against the note.
fix: Verified the real state in code before building, then ported the proven Budget implementation to Social LevelUp (random retrieval token, dual-read migration, proof-of-possession, per-IP limit, and a search module). In this conversation the port was syntax-checked only; browser verification and deploy were blocked by a full disk. Rule: a 'shipped' note for a multi-app repo must name each app, and stale notes get a code check before they are relied on.
